items.title: [Feature][KV Offload] Support joint GPU/CPU prefix cache lookup
items.body:
## Purpose

### Background

We deploy DeepSeek V4 Flash Vision Exp with vLLM Ascend v0.27 in our internal network, with Simple CPU Offload enabled. During operation, we observed a cache miss rate exceeding 10%. Investigation showed that some reusable cache entries were not being retrieved due to the unimplemented TODO in `vllm/v1/simple_kv_offload/manager.py`: the existing API only matches a CPU suffix following the GPU prefix, rather than searching for a complete valid prefix across both pools.

After implementing joint lookup, we ported the change to the v0.27 branch in our fork and redeployed it in the same environment. The deployment has been running for five days, with normal operation and successful retrieval of cache entries previously affected by this limitation.

This PR targets upstream main. The deployment observations above come from the v0.27 backport in our fork.

### Changes

Support valid prefixes composed of interleaved GPU and CPU cache blocks, replacing the limitation of matching a GPU prefix followed by a CPU suffix.

For example, given a `GPU → CPU → GPU` cache layout, reuse both GPU blocks directly and allocate and load a target block only for the middle CPU block. When both pools contain a required block, prefer the GPU copy.

The implementation:

- Provides a read-only joint lookup view for existing attention-specific matching algorithms, preserving hybrid-attention convergence and memoizing queries within each request.
- Records hit sources by group and block position, distinguishing GPU hits, CPU blocks requiring loads, and attention padding.
- Pins source blocks before allocation and allocates targets only for CPU hits. Targets are registered in the cache after loading completes, without re-registering interleaved GPU hits.
- Attributes GPU/CPU cache statistics and cache events to their actual sources.
- Preserves full-block CPU loads, copy-on-write for partial GPU hits, and existing watermark and speculative-decoding reservation rules. If capacity is insufficient, allocation of the entire match is deferred.

### Relationship to related work

This PR implements joint lookup for interleaved GPU/CPU prefixes in `SimpleCPUOffloadConnector`. The related #52773 / #52774 address boundary backfill in `OffloadingConnector`, so the connector and implementation scope differ.

## Test Plan

Cover the following behaviors:

- All-GPU, all-CPU, multiple interleavings, duplicate hits across pools, missing intermediate blocks, and different sources across groups.
- GPU block identity reuse, exact CPU transfer positions, and no publication of target cache entries before loading completes.
- SWA/Mamba, different block sizes, DCP/EAGLE matching boundaries, final-token recomputation, and copy-on-write for partial blocks.
- Insufficient capacity, speculative-decoding reservations, and reference cleanup after retries, cancellation, and reset.
- Bypassing separate GPU/CPU scans on the joint path, with no repeated probes for the same hash/group.
- GPU/CPU statistics and interleaved cache events.

Regression command after the latest code cleanup:

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/v1/simple_kv_offload/test_scheduler.py \
  tests/v1/simple_kv_offload/test_kv_events.py \
  tests/v1/core/test_prefix_caching.py \
  tests/v1/core/prefix_cache/test_partial_prefix_cache_hits.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_simple_cpu_offload_connector.py \
  -q
```

Run pre-commit on modified files, along with Python 3.10/3.12 type checks.

Local real-model validation uses OPT-125m, Qwen3-0.6B, and Qwen3.5-0.8B. GPU cache capacity is constrained and cache residency layouts are controlled to trigger actual CPU loads. Validation compares cold-cache and warm-cache outputs under deterministic generation settings and checks transfer positions and reference cleanup.

## Test Result

After the September 20 rebase, 575 distinct relevant tests passed (574 in the broad run and one rerun after restoring the Ray test dependency), along with pre-commit and Python 3.10/3.12 type checks. This includes regressions for discarding short joint hits under bounded prefix replay and replaying longer hits after CPU loading. Earlier, 22 real-model combinations passed, completing 9,146 exact cold/warm output comparisons and exercising actual CPU loads, copy-on-write, and preemption; that model matrix has not been rerun after this rebase. Some OPT/MTP combinations showed cold/warm differences that also reproduced on the legacy lookup path and are excluded from the passing results.

## AI assistance

GPT-6 Astra assisted with the implementation, tests, and this description. The code has undergone human review.

items.title: [Test] Pin the fine-grained prefix-cache-hit gate to prefix-cacheable groups
items.body:
## Purpose

Test-only. Adds a regression guard for the `prefix_cacheable` scoping of the fine-grained-hit veto that #53896 (`e126687a`) introduced in `HybridKVCacheCoordinator.__init__`. No production code changes; the fix this covers is already in `main`.

**What the gate does.** When a hybrid model has an align-mode Mamba group, the coordinator enables fine-grained (hash-block-aligned) partial hits, then scans the managers and switches them off again if any manager can only answer block-aligned lookups (`vllm/v1/core/kv_cache_coordinator.py:644-660` at `22df3a3`). Since #53896 that scan is scoped to groups whose spec is `prefix_cacheable` (`:649`), because `verify_and_split_kv_cache_groups` skips the other groups (`:675-682`) and they are never looked up, so their `supports_fine_grained_hash_lookup` cannot affect any hit.

**What is uncovered.** `grep -rn prefix_cacheable tests/` finds only `tests/v1/core/test_contiguous_kv_packing.py`, which exercises grouping, hash-granularity and truncation, not this gate. We found no assertion that a non-prefix-cacheable group leaves `enable_partial_hash_hits` on; with `and group.kv_cache_spec.prefix_cacheable` removed at `:649`, such a group reduces every other group's hit granularity from `hash_block_size` to `scheduler_block_size` (`_cache_hit_alignment_tokens`, `:665-673`) with nothing to catch it.

The regression is easy to reintroduce because the veto reads the *manager* (`supports_fine_grained_hash_lookup`, `block_size`) while the scoping reads the *spec*, and `CircularBufferManager` is exactly the shape that trips it: it subclasses `FullAttentionManager` and overrides `supports_fine_grained_hash_lookup = False` (`vllm/v1/core/single_type_kv_cache_manager.py:1118-1121`), and `CircularBufferSpec` defines `block_size` as the ring capacity (`vllm/v1/kv_cache_interface.py:753-761`), which the test sets to differ from the hash block size.

**The tests** (`tests/v1/core/prefix_cache/test_partial_prefix_cache_hits.py`, one shared helper building full-attention + Mamba("align") + one extra group):

1. `test_scratch_group_does_not_veto_fine_grained_hits` — extra group is a `CircularBufferSpec` ring (block 4, hash block 2). Asserts the preconditions the gate reacts to (`not prefix_cacheable`, `not supports_fine_grained_hash_lookup`, `block_size != hash_block_size`), then that `enable_partial_hash_hits` stays on, `_cache_hit_alignment_tokens == hash_block_size`, and that the group is absent from `attention_groups`.
2. `test_prefix_cacheable_group_without_fine_lookup_still_vetoes` — negative control: a prefix-cacheable `SlidingWindowSpec` with the same two properties must still veto, and the alignment must fall back to `scheduler_block_size`. Without it, test 1 would also pass if the whole check were deleted.

**Why it is worth a test PR.** Any hybrid model that carries a non-prefix-cacheable scratch group is exposed: before #53896, such a group pinned every warm-turn hit to scheduler-block alignment. On the deployment that surfaced it (GLM-5.3-Flash on 2× DGX Spark: a kpool-tail scratch group at block 4 next to MLA/Mamba groups at 3584 and a 64-token hash block) hits were 3584-aligned instead of 64-aligned.

**Not a duplicate.** `gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search "partial hash hits"`, `--search "prefix_cacheable"`, `--search "fine-grained hash"` (2026-09-01): I found no matching open PR in those searches; nearest is #54397 (fine-grained SWA hits, draft), which works on the SWA *manager's* lookup, not on the coordinator's group scoping. If #54397 lands and `SlidingWindowManager` gains fine-grained lookup, the negative control's precondition (`not swa_manager.supports_fine_grained_hash_lookup`) will need another prefix-cacheable manager without fine-grained lookup; test 1 is unaffected.

## Test Plan

```
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/core/prefix_cache/test_partial_prefix_cache_hits.py -v -k "fine_grained_hits or still_vetoes"
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/core/prefix_cache/test_partial_prefix_cache_hits.py -q
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/core/test_contiguous_kv_packing.py -q
```

Mutation check: remove `and group.kv_cache_spec.prefix_cacheable` at `vllm/v1/core/kv_cache_coordinator.py:649` — `test_scratch_group_does_not_veto_fine_grained_hits` must fail and `test_prefix_cacheable_group_without_fine_lookup_still_vetoes` must still pass.

## Test Result

Run on an upstream-compatible CPU environment (macOS arm64, Python 3.13 venv, `torch` 2.13 CPU wheel, `requirements/common.txt`, `PYTHONPATH` at the clone @ `22df3a3` + this commit). The repo's root `tests/conftest.py` segfaults on this host while importing the full `LLM`/multimodal stack (unrelated to these tests), so the runs below use `--noconftest`; the test file is self-contained (its own autouse `init_none_hash` fixture, helpers from `tests.v1.core.test_prefix_caching`).

```
$ .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/core/prefix_cache/test_partial_prefix_cache_hits.py -v -k "fine_grained_hits or still_vetoes" --noconftest
tests/v1/core/prefix_cache/test_partial_prefix_cache_hits.py::test_scratch_group_does_not_veto_fine_grained_hits PASSED
tests/v1/core/prefix_cache/test_partial_prefix_cache_hits.py::test_prefix_cacheable_group_without_fine_lookup_still_vetoes PASSED
2 passed, 40 deselected, 15 warnings in 3.64s

$ .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/core/prefix_cache/test_partial_prefix_cache_hits.py -q --noconftest
42 passed, 15 warnings in 2.63s

$ .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/core/test_contiguous_kv_packing.py -q --noconftest
21 passed, 15 warnings in 2.53s
```

Mutation check — with `if group.kv_cache_spec.prefix_cacheable` replaced by `if True` at `vllm/v1/core/kv_cache_coordinator.py:649`:

```
>       assert coordinator.enable_partial_hash_hits
E       assert False
FAILED tests/v1/core/prefix_cache/test_partial_prefix_cache_hits.py::test_scratch_group_does_not_veto_fine_grained_hits
1 failed, 1 passed, 40 deselected, 15 warnings in 2.54s
```

(the negative control still passes, as intended). Lint: `pre-commit run --files tests/v1/core/prefix_cache/test_partial_prefix_cache_hits.py` (ruff-check, ruff-format, typos, mypy, SPDX) — all passed.

## Model evaluation

Not applicable: no runtime code changes.

## AI assistance

Submitted by nood-co1 on behalf of Blockbrain Labs (https://x.com/blockbrain_labs, GitHub org blockbrain-ai); drafted with AI assistance (Claude, with an independent adversarial review pass by OpenAI Codex folded in) and reviewed line by line by the submitter, who ran the tests listed above. Every `file:line` was checked against `22df3a3`.

items.title: [KV Connector][Mooncake] Skip lookup for locally reused prefix
items.body:
## Purpose
Skip Mooncake Store lookup when the local prefix cache already covers the maximum usable external prefix.

A full external hit is already clamped to the following block-aligned range:

```python
(request.num_tokens - 1) // block_size * block_size
```

When `num_computed_tokens` has reached this range, an external lookup cannot
produce any loadable KV blocks. Return early instead of issuing the lookup.


## Test 
```bash
python -m pytest  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_store_scheduler.py -q
```

The added tests cover:
- local cache fully covers the usable external prefix: no lookup is issued;
- local cache does not fully cover the usable external prefix: lookup and load
  planning remain unchanged.

items.title: [Perf][KV Offload] Avoid repeated hash-prefix scans
items.body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Avoid repeated scans of previously processed request hashes when `OffloadingConnector` updates offload keys. Preserve key order, chunk boundaries, and recorded token positions.

## Claims

- Each update reads only the newly selected hashes, instead of traversing the existing prefix again for each cache group.
- Updates with no complete new chunk avoid scanning old hashes.
- The regression test checks incremental updates, incomplete chunks, repeated calls, multiple chunk sizes, key order, and token positions.

## Validation

On macOS arm64 with Python 3.12.13, the five focused tests below passed on this rebased change. All applicable hooks passed.

```bash
uv run --no-project .venv/bin/python3 -m pytest \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector/test_scheduler.py \
  --noconftest -q \
  -k 'update_offload_keys_without_scanning_hash_prefix or normal_store_excludes_align_mode_mamba_sources or partial_lookup_returns_exact_boundary_and_group_load_keys or recurrent_group_unhashed_block_does_not_truncate_load_boundary or partial_lookup_requires_every_cache_group'

uv run --no-project .venv/bin/python3 -m pre_commit run --files \
  vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/offloading/scheduler.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector/test_scheduler.py
```

These are CPU tests with mocked scheduler inputs. `--noconftest` excludes unrelated GPU fixtures. Buildkite already includes this test file in the V1 KV Connectors suite.

The regression uses a hash list that rejects iteration but permits indexed access. Restoring the method from main (`8fb16ea5a66f0ef362e728f0ff025f2845927fd5`) in memory makes the test fail. The rebased method passes. This establishes the traversal change without a timing threshold.

End-to-end serving and model evaluation remain pending for this rebased commit. No model, GPU, workload, or serving speedup is claimed. Human review of every changed line and the required serving validation remain pending.

## Details

Without this change, `RequestOffloadState.update_offload_keys()` uses `islice` to skip hashes that already have offload keys. Skipping still consumes the iterator from the beginning. Every call therefore traverses the hash list again, even when the request has no new complete chunk.

This method runs during offload lookup, scheduler updates, and request completion. The repeated CPU work grows with the request hash count and affected requests. It adds work to the scheduler path. The effect on serving latency and throughput is not measured here.

`Request.block_hashes` is a list. Indexed slicing starts at the next unprocessed chunk boundary and selects each chunk's final hash. Key construction and position updates remain unchanged. The temporary list contains only newly selected hashes, at the cost of one short-lived list per group per update.

Open-PR searches for `update_offload_keys` and `offload hash` found no duplicate of this traversal fix. Related #54743 changes which cache groups support offloading. It does not remove this repeated hash-prefix traversal.

AI assistance was used to prepare, review, and test this change.

---

items.title: [Bugfix][KV Offload] Anchor the partial-tail lookup on the full-attention prefix
items.body:
## Purpose

Split out of #57216 per @orozery's review (part 1 of 2): the lookup half. The DCP store half is #58619.

`_lookup` anchors the partial-tail search on `_lookup_complete_chunks`, which requires *every* KV cache group to have a complete chunk at the anchor boundary, including the recurrent groups. A recurrent `align` group holds state only where a scheduler step ended on one of its block boundaries: in practice at the producer prompt's last full recurrent block and at its tail.

With **uniform block sizes** (dcp=1, the only shape `supports_partial_tail` admits today) the last-full-block boundary is also a full-attention chunk multiple, so that aligned row lands on the chunk grid, `complete_hit` reaches it, and the existing one-window probe finds the tail. The anchor only fails when that row is missing, e.g. evicted separately from the tail. So on `main` today this is a robustness fix.

With **mixed block sizes** -- under DCP the full-attention offload block is `dcp x` the attention block while recurrent blocks stay unsharded (12288 vs 1536 at DCP 8) -- the aligned row sits at a recurrent multiple that is essentially never a full-attention multiple. `complete_hit` is then 0 for any prompt past the first chunk, the search is capped at one window from zero, and a correctly stored tail further out is never probed although it is resident. That is the state #58619 (the DCP store side) would land in without this PR: tails get stored, but only those within one window of the complete-chunk hit are ever found -- the "#58619 only" column of the hardware table below. **This PR is the prerequisite for #58619's lookups to work.**

Instrumented `_lookup` on a replay (chunk 12288, hash 128), before the change:

```
n=12620  complete_hit=12288  complete_boundary=12288  max_boundary=12544
           boundary=12544 ALL GROUPS HIT                  <- restores
n=15136  complete_hit=0      complete_boundary=0      max_boundary=12160
           boundary=12160 group=0 MISS ... 11776 MISS     <- tail stored at 15104,
                                                            never probed
```

Fix: anchor on the full-attention complete prefix and check recurrent groups only at the candidate boundary. Following the review suggestion, the anchor is `_lookup_complete_chunks` itself restricted to the full-attention groups via a new `lookup_groups` parameter, so it honours the same `max_num_new_tokens` / `max_load_tokens` caps, deferral and being-loaded rules as the all-groups hit, and only chunks verified resident can be requested by the load path. No new lookup method.

The returned boundary is always strictly greater than the complete-chunk hit, so the change can only widen what a lookup reports, never shrink it; wherever the aligned row is on the chunk grid the anchor equals `complete_hit` and the behaviour is unchanged. The probe window stays bounded at one full-attention block.

## Test Plan

Eleven tests on the existing dcp=1 hybrid fixture (`_make_partial_tail_scheduler`: 16-token full-attention and Mamba blocks, hash 4):

```
pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector/ -q
```

Fail on `main`, pass here (they guard the fix):
- tail found with no recurrent state at the chunk boundary (30-token prompt, tail at 28)
- the same across **two** complete chunks (46-token prompt, tail at 44) -- the production shape, where the complete-chunk anchor is 0
- the load path requests only the verified chunk keys plus the tail keys
- `_lookup_complete_chunks(lookup_groups=full_attention_groups)` returns the full-attention prefix while the default still requires every group
- `max_num_new_tokens` caps which tail the anchored search may report
- deferral while the anchor chunk is being loaded, and while it is `HIT_PENDING`

Pass on both (regression guards for what the anchor must not change):
- 0 when no tail was stored; 0 when the full-attention chunk is not resident
- the tail is preferred over an aligned recurrent state at the chunk boundary
- a tail is found after a GPU prefix hit (`num_computed_tokens = 16`)

## Test Result

**Unit suite**, this branch vs. its base (`origin/main` @ a9eafde59c):

| arm | CPU-only host | GB300 (in the vLLM nightly container) |
|---|---|---|
| this branch | 103 failed, **367 passed**, 2 skipped | **478 passed**, 0 failed |
| base | 103 failed, 356 passed, 2 skipped | 467 passed, 0 failed |

On the CPU host the failure sets are byte-identical; all 103 are no-GPU artifacts (`VllmConfig` "Hybrid KV cache manager … not supported", HF-hub 429s). On GPU everything passes. The 11 added tests account for the entire +11; 7 of them fail when run against `main`. The GB300 unit run was on the previous rebase (base `ddd6fbca14`). `scheduler.py` and `test_scheduler.py` are byte-identical to this head, and the only change to `vllm/v1/core` since then is the #56723 `dcp_sharded` refactor, which keeps the block geometry the same. `mypy-3.12`, `ruff check` and `ruff format` pass.

**Hardware** (1 x GB300 node, `vllm/vllm-openai:nightly-29468dde8b` with only `offloading/scheduler.py` replaced). Model: Kimi-Linear-48B-A3B-Instruct (KDA + MLA), TP4, `--mamba-cache-mode align --prefix-match-unit 128`, OffloadingConnector with a 16 GiB CPU pool. Recurrent block 512, full-attention offload block 2048 at DCP4 (512 at DCP1), hash 128: the K3 shape (1536 / 12288 / 128) scaled down.

Protocol per prompt: clear all tiers, cold run (asserted 0 cached), reset only the GPU prefix cache, replay. The table shows tokens restored from the CPU tier, i.e. the replay delta of `vllm:prompt_tokens_by_source{source="external_kv_transfer"}`.

| prompt tokens | best boundary | DCP1: `main` | DCP1: this PR | DCP4: #58619 only | DCP4: #58619 + this PR |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 645 | 640 | 640 | 640 | 640 | 640 |
| 2309 | 2304 | 2304 | 2304 | 2304 | 2304 |
| 2565 | 2560 | 2560 | 2560 | **0** | **2560** |
| 2949 | 2944 | 2944 | 2944 | **0** | **2944** |
| 3717 | 3712 | 3712 | 3712 | **0** | **3712** |
| 4101 | 4096 | 4096 | 4096 | 4096 | 4096 |
| 4485 | 4480 | 4480 | 4480 | 4480 | 4480 |
| 17029 | 17024 | 17024 | 17024 | **0** | **17024** |
| 2949, replay diverges at 2700 | 2560 | 2560 | 2560 | **0** | **2560** |

- **DCP1:** this PR is identical to `main` on every trial, including store and load bytes. That is the expected no-regression result: the aligned row is on the chunk grid there, so the anchor equals `complete_hit`.
- **DCP4:** without this PR, only tails within one window of the complete-chunk hit are found. With it, every prompt restores to its last hash boundary.
- **All trials:** replayed greedy output is byte-identical to the cold recompute (32 tokens), with 0 allocation failures and no errors in the server logs.

An earlier run of the combined change on a 2-node GB300 K3 deployment (TP8/DCP8) is in #57216.

## Notes

- Related: the DCP store-side half is in #58619. Both are standalone; they touch adjacent lines in `__init__` and merge cleanly together (verified; the merged tree passes the suite). #58413 (MTP/EAGLE Mamba offload) touches the same file and also merges cleanly.
- Not duplicating an existing PR: #52832 fixed the analogous producer-side gap for the Mooncake connector; #52397 covers the `max_offload_tokens` cap in the store path, which this PR does not touch.
- AI assistance (Claude / Devin) was used to draft code and tests; every changed line was reviewed and the tests were run by the submitter.

items.title: [KV Offload] Expose the processed prefix at request finalization
items.body:
## Purpose

[#51787](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/51787) (f12fe10c5c) removed repeated scheduler touch() calls and introduced key positions for request-scoped recency handling. Those positions can include the full prompt before execution completes, so they cannot distinguish the processed prefix from an untouched suffix when a request terminates early.

Expose num_computed_tokens, num_in_flight_tokens, num_prompt_tokens, and num_tokens as read-only ReqContext properties that delegate to Request and stay up to date. These allow offload backends to derive the processed-prefix boundary, excluding in-flight work and the uncommitted final sampled token. Contexts without an associated Request return None. The complete key-position map remains available for outstanding transfers.

Since ReqContext now retains a reference to Request, release completed-batch context references in the async lookup worker before it waits for another batch.

This is separate from [#54979](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/54979) and [#43569](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/43569), which address GPU cache registration and rollback, and [#52103](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/52103), which carries provenance through stored events. This PR exposes metadata; it does not change existing eviction policies.

## Test Plan

- Added a scheduler context test checking that token counts reflect subsequent request updates and return None for contexts without a request.
- Added an async lookup regression test checking that completed request contexts are released while the worker remains idle.

## Test Result

All 20 isolated checks passed using the relevant production definitions and repository tests.

items.title: [Perf][Core] Restore compact prefix-cache entries after duplicate eviction
items.body:
## Purpose

When a prefix-cache hash has multiple physical copies, `BlockHashToBlockMap` promotes its value to a dictionary. Eviction currently retains that dictionary even when only one copy remains. Subsequent lookups can repeatedly scan its deleted entries, and its allocation remains live.

Restore the existing direct `KVCacheBlock` representation when eviction leaves one copy. Extend the existing mapping test to cover re-insertion, an unknown block ID and final removal, and update the pool-eviction expectations. Block identity, reference counts, cache contents and KV-event behavior are preserved.

The state is reachable through repeated `prompt_logprobs` requests followed by cache pressure. The benefit applies when the surviving prefix is subsequently reused; ordinary cache hits need not encounter this state. Checked the actual diffs of #55092 and #48933, which change removal-event semantics/counts and retain singleton dictionaries, and #40459, which adds an optional Rust pool without fixing this Python mapping. This follows the compact-representation approach introduced in #24830.

## Test Plan

Current CPU validation uses Python sources at `fff03267dae61d03615225c2f48a06082d842e2d` plus this patch:

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/v1/core/test_prefix_caching.py tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py \
  tests/v1/core/test_async_scheduler.py tests/v1/core/test_deferred_block_free.py \
  tests/v1/core/test_priority_preemption_bug.py \
  tests/v1/core/test_single_type_kv_cache_manager.py tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_utils.py \
  tests/v1/simple_kv_offload -q --durations=10
.venv/bin/python -m pre_commit run --files \
  vllm/v1/core/block_pool.py tests/v1/core/test_prefix_caching.py
```

## Test Result

- **649 passed, 2 skipped**; the two skips are the CUDA/ROCm-only simple-offload worker/integration modules on CPU. All applicable pre-commit checks passed. The compact-representation assertion was first shown to fail on the original implementation.
- CPU environment: AMD Ryzen 7 9700X, WSL Ubuntu, Python 3.12.3, torch 2.13.0+cpu. CPU extensions are from nightly `29468dde8`, not an exact current-main binary build.
- Prior GPU validation used base `a4eb3f25` with its exact CUDA wheel and the same production patch: RTX 4090, Qwen3-0.6B revision `c1899de289a04d12100db370d81485cdf75e47ca`, FP16, seed 0, V1/MRV2, eager, single GPU. Four baseline–patch–patch–baseline runs passed. All 211 completed requests per run had identical generated tokens, generated-token logprobs and cache-hit counts. Active-request reset/recomputation and cancellation checks passed; all non-null blocks were released. The model workload reached 16 copies → one and released 5,056 bytes of inner dictionaries for its eight target hashes. This GPU validation has not been rerun on the newer base.

Earlier real-`KVCacheManager` CPU lookup measurements at `a4eb3f25`, for a 4,096-token prefix after duplicate eviction (1,000 queries × 7 repeats, median):

| Original copies → one | Baseline / patch, µs | Inner dictionary storage, baseline / patch |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 → 1 control | 84.71 / 85.38 | 0 / 0 bytes |
| 2 → 1 | 102.69 / 83.61 | 57,344 / 0 bytes |
| 32 → 1 | 106.25 / 84.19 | 299,008 / 0 bytes |
| 128 → 1 | 122.26 / 85.49 | 1,200,128 / 0 bytes |

The 128-copy case is a constructed CPU workload, not the GPU workload. These are dictionary allocation sizes, not process RSS or GPU memory savings.

A further CPU comparison on the current base included duplicate creation, pressure eviction and subsequent hot-request query/allocation/free costs in one timed phase. With two copies → one, followed by 8 or 32 normal requests, wall-time medians were 1.844 → 1.489 ms and 5.352 → 4.805 ms respectively. This used a 4,096-token prefix, one CPU, enabled GC, two warmups and 30 alternating repetitions; manager/request construction and model execution were excluded.

There is a tradeoff: continuously cycling one ↔ two copies **without prefix reuse** reallocates dictionaries. The isolated insert/pop pair took 0.369 versus 0.279 µs. In a separate real-manager repeated-scoring workload, the 4,096-token query-entry/allocation/free cycle measured 303.70 versus 276.68 µs, with substantial sample variation. These costs remain relevant; the optimization is workload-dependent.

Production prevalence, long-running RSS/GC behavior and a statistically significant serving-throughput improvement have not been established. Multi-GPU, quantization and speculative decoding were not model-tested. Prefix-query savings must not be multiplied by generated-token count; admission retries/recomputation can add queries, but their real frequency was not measured.

<details>
<summary>CPU lifecycle/lookup reproducer (run on the base and patched checkout)</summary>

Save the following as a temporary script and run it using the checkout's `.venv/bin/python` with the checkout on `PYTHONPATH`. It uses normal cache-manager APIs and performs no model execution.

```python
"""CPU cache-manager lifecycle and timing; no simulated GPU/model result."""
import json
import platform
import statistics
import sys
import timeit

import torch
import vllm.v1.core.block_pool as block_pool_module

from vllm.sampling_params import SamplingParams
from vllm.utils.hashing import sha256
from vllm.v1.core.kv_cache_manager import KVCacheManager
from vllm.v1.core.kv_cache_utils import get_request_block_hasher, init_none_hash
from vllm.v1.kv_cache_interface import FullAttentionSpec, KVCacheConfig, KVCacheGroupSpec
from vllm.v1.request import Request


def request(name, tokens, scoring=False):
    return Request(request_id=name, prompt_token_ids=tokens,
                   sampling_params=SamplingParams(max_tokens=1, prompt_logprobs=1 if scoring else None),
                   pooling_params=None, block_hasher=get_request_block_hasher(16, sha256))


def run(copies, num_blocks):
    num_tokens = num_blocks * 16
    tokens = list(range(num_tokens))
    manager = KVCacheManager(
        KVCacheConfig(num_blocks=copies * num_blocks + 1, kv_cache_tensors=[],
                      kv_cache_groups=[KVCacheGroupSpec(["layer"], FullAttentionSpec(
                          block_size=16, num_kv_heads=1, head_size=64, dtype=torch.float16))]),
        max_model_len=num_tokens + 16, scheduler_block_size=16, hash_block_size=16,
        enable_caching=True,
    )
    # Prompt logprobs require recomputation, so distinct physical copies of
    # identical prefixes accumulate even for sequential scoring requests.
    for i in range(copies):
        req = request(str(i), tokens, scoring=True)
        computed, hit_tokens, _ = manager.get_computed_blocks(req)
        assert hit_tokens == 0
        allocated = manager.allocate_slots(req, num_tokens, hit_tokens, computed)
        assert allocated is not None
        manager.free(req)
    # An unrelated request consumes older copies under ordinary cache pressure.
    evicted = manager.block_pool.get_new_blocks((copies - 1) * num_blocks)
    probe = request("probe", tokens)
    computed, hit_tokens, _ = manager.get_computed_blocks(probe)
    assert hit_tokens == num_tokens - 16
    assert len(computed.blocks[0]) == num_blocks - 1
    assert all(b.ref_cnt == 0 for b in computed.blocks[0])
    values = manager.block_pool.cached_block_hash_to_block._cache.values()
    dict_bytes = sum(sys.getsizeof(v) for v in values if isinstance(v, dict))
    lookup = lambda: manager.get_computed_blocks(probe)
    for _ in range(50):
        lookup()
    samples = timeit.repeat(lookup, number=1000, repeat=7)
    # Cache hits remain usable, and releasing requests restores the pool.
    assert manager.allocate_slots(probe, 16, hit_tokens, computed) is not None
    manager.free(probe)
    manager.block_pool.free_blocks(evicted)
    assert manager.block_pool.get_num_free_blocks() == copies * num_blocks
    return dict(copies=copies, prefix_tokens=num_tokens, cached_tokens=hit_tokens,
                retained_dict_bytes=dict_bytes,
                lookup_us_median=statistics.median(samples)*1000,
                lookup_us_samples=[s*1000 for s in samples])


init_none_hash(sha256)
print(json.dumps({"python": sys.version, "platform": platform.platform(),
                  "source": block_pool_module.__file__,
                  "torch": torch.__version__, "warmup": 50, "iterations": 1000,
                  "repeats": 7, "records": [run(c, b) for b in (16, 256) for c in (1, 2, 32, 128)]}, indent=2))
```

</details>

## Purpose

Add scheduler regression coverage for the Mamba same-step cache deferral path
after #48860 moved prefix-cache statistics recording from lookup time to request
admission.

Hybrid attention/Mamba requests can be looked up more than once when a Mamba
state block cached by a sibling request in the same scheduler step temporarily
prevents admission. These retries are not preemptions. The new test verifies
that each request and its prompt tokens are counted exactly once despite those
repeated lookups.

The existing hybrid scheduler helper is generalized so the test can select
`mamba_cache_mode="align"` without attaching a KV connector.

## Overview

External prefix-cache-aware routers cannot determine a group's prefix reuse policy from its attention kind alone. This PR exposes `prefix_cacheable` and `prefix_replay_tokens` from the resolved spec through `EngineCore.get_kv_cache_group_metadata()`.

## Claims

- Report whether each group participates in prefix caching and its required tail replay length.
- Cover KpoolTail, Sliding MLA with bounded replay on/off, and uniform-type wrappers in the existing CPU metadata suite.

## Validation

```bash
VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu PYTEST_DISABLE_PLUGIN_AUTOLOAD=1 \
  .venv/bin/python -m pytest -p no:cacheprovider -q \
  tests/v1/engine/test_kv_cache_group_metadata.py
.venv/bin/ruff check vllm/v1/engine/core.py tests/v1/engine/test_kv_cache_group_metadata.py
```

## Details

KpoolTail is classified as sliding-window attention but has `prefix_cacheable=False`. Bounded-replay Sliding MLA also opts out of shared prefix lookup and declares a replay window. Related to [#48121](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/48121), which expands canonical metadata and frontend access. Its current diff does not include these two prefix-policy properties; this PR adds only those fields to the existing RPC.

items.title: [Bugfix] Register hybrid prefix-cache boundaries at hittable positions

labels.name: verified
labels.description: Run pre-commit for new contributors without triggering other tests

items.body:
## Purpose

A prefix-cache lookup ends at `num_tokens - 1` at most (`get_computed_blocks`); Eagle block drop takes one more unit. The scheduler's Mamba tail split and `_cache_partial_tail_block` in the full-attention and Mamba managers floored from `num_tokens`, so a block-aligned prompt, or any prompt under Eagle, registered state one unit above the highest position a lookup can reach, and a resubmit fell back to the previous retention checkpoint.

Floor all three from `num_tokens - 1`. The scheduler's tail stop backs off one unit under `use_eagle_block_drop`, as its block stop already does (#53388 made the drop optional, so the predicate is the drop flag, not `use_eagle()`), and the SWA mask keeps the tail ending there so fine-grained hits reconcile. Two `test_prefix_caching.py` expectations gain SWA block 14 for that reason: the full-attention partial tail of their 128-token prompt now registers at 120 instead of the unreachable 128.

Replaces the first revision, which keyed the shift on `use_eagle()`. Keying on the drop flag also means the shift follows #54163 if that narrows the drop to eagle/eagle3/MTP: DFlash and DSpark prompts then stop being shifted with no change here. #53479 densifies Mamba states and drops the Eagle back-off; this PR fixes the registration/lookup mismatch and composes with it.

## Test

`pytest tests/v1/core/test_prefix_caching.py tests/v1/core/test_mamba_align_chunk_split.py` - 138 passed. New cases pin the chunk ends for block-aligned and partial-tail prompts with and without Eagle.

2x DGX Spark, TP=2, Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4 hybrid, FLASHINFER, `--prefix-cache-retention-interval 4800`, block 800, no drafter (none boots on `main` until #54834). Divergent-tail resubmit of a 133k-token document, cold cache. Block-aligned prompt: `main` 89.8% prefix hits and 11.75 s TTFT, the lookup falling back to the previous retention checkpoint; this commit 99.4% and 1.02 s. Unaligned prompt: 99.5% and 0.87 s with and without it. On a lineage with a DFlash2 drafter and unified pages (block 1568) the fix is neutral at 97.7% to 98.6% hits either way, decode 12/12 at 175 tok/s; the first revision's ~0% -> 98% came from an earlier geometry of that lineage.

AI assistance was used; every line reviewed and the unit tests above run by me.

items.title: [Feature] Add routed-expert prefix omission with KV offload compatibility
items.body:
# [Feature] Add routed-expert prefix omission with KV offload compatibility



## Purpose

Related RFC: [Efficient Routed-Expert Replay with Prefix Omission and KV Cache Offloading](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/56402).

Add opt-in routed-expert prefix omission for multi-turn RL workloads and compatibility with same-engine KV offloading. Returning cached-prefix routes on every turn repeats data the caller already retains. Slicing the prompt range before gathering reduces scheduler-side NumPy gathering, response serialization/payload, and frontend concatenation work; worker-side expert D2H copies are unchanged.

- Add `--enable-omit-prefix-routed-experts`. Record `request.num_cached_tokens` at the first successful cache admission and return prompt routes starting at `max(routed_experts_prompt_start, request.num_cached_tokens)`.
- Require a stable session identity when omission is enabled and combine it with the existing cache salt, with idempotent normalization across serving paths, including split render/generate.
- During recovery before decode starts, cap GPU prefix reuse at `num_cached_tokens` and use a connector bypass hook instead of external lookup, preserving required connector initialization and cleanup.
- After decode starts, retain normal lookup: previously collected routes remain in the frontend state of the same request.
- Support SimpleCPUOffloadConnector, CPU-only OffloadingConnector with CPUOffloadingSpec, and MooncakeStoreConnector. Unsupported configurations fail validation; PD disaggregation, tiered offloading, and custom offloading specs are out of scope.

Callers must retain and correctly assemble routes across requests sharing the same identity; cache hits are not proof of response delivery. Prefix omission is disabled by default. This PR does not implement the RFC's optional slot invalidation or change expert-array dtypes.

## Test Plan

Add independent test cases using existing pytest fixtures to cover:
- Session-salt identity, preservation of the original salt, idempotency, and missing/conflicting identity rejection; no identity requirement when omission is disabled.
- First successful cache admission, allocation retry, and preservation of the cached boundary through preemption and reset.
- Actual Scheduler lookup selection and prompt-route output ranges, with async scheduling both enabled and disabled.
- Connector bypass cleanup, repeated bypass, and subsequent zero-external-token allocation.
- Supported/unsupported configurations, including validation after automatic connector creation from native offloading settings.

Run the full related connector and API utility files, plus the targeted scheduler/configuration tests:

```bash
python -m pytest \
  tests/utils/test_routed_expert_session.py \
  tests/entrypoints/serve/utils/test_api_utils.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector/test_scheduler.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_store_scheduler.py \
  tests/v1/simple_kv_offload/test_scheduler.py \
  tests/test_config.py::test_routed_expert_offloading_connector_capability \
  tests/test_config.py::test_routed_expert_offloading_guards \
  tests/test_config.py::test_routed_expert_auto_offloading_config \
  tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py::test_routed_expert_recovery_lookup \
  tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py::test_routed_expert_recovery_schedule_uses_bypass \
  tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py::test_routed_expert_prompt_output_start \
  tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py::test_prefix_cache_stats_counted_once_for_retried_then_scheduled_request \
  tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py::test_routed_expert_cached_boundary_survives_recovery \
  -v --tb=short
```

Run with the repository's test dependencies installed. The reported run used normal pytest fixtures and `HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1`, with the OPT configuration/tokenizer required by existing fixtures cached locally. The original upstream cache-statistics and prompt-logprobs tests are preserved unchanged; the new boundary and bypass checks use separate test names.

## Test Result

### Automated tests

The exact selection above ran on a GPU worker: **390 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped** in 78.35 seconds, with 14 Torch deprecation warnings. These tests validate scheduler/configuration/connector behavior, not full-model GPU inference, and are not a full-repository test run.

Ruff check, Ruff format check, and `git diff --check` passed for the modified test files.

### Manual end-to-end checks

Separate checks used real BF16 Step3.5 weights on 8 H200 GPUs (TP=8, PP=1, DP=1), async scheduling, prefix caching, and omission. With a 2,048-block GPU cache, a 1,024-token initial prompt, pressure from 48 distinct sessions, and three revisits, all three supported connectors produced an external hit of 1,008 tokens. Returned route shapes, MoE expert-ID ranges, and token-aligned multi-turn assembly passed. This does not establish exact expert-ID equality against an independent recomputation baseline.

Known end-to-end limitations: reset-induced preemption recovered requests with both CPU connectors, but the reset endpoint returned HTTP 500 due to held blocks. Mooncake reset during active prefill triggered an `_unfinished_requests` assertion, also reproduced on the same branch with routed-expert return and omission disabled and no bypass invocation. Successful active-request reset is not claimed; a clean upstream-baseline reproduction remains pending.

### Preliminary performance from the RFC

The following results are reported in the [RFC](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/56402), not a fresh benchmark of this PR branch. They measure prefix omission with **KV offloading disabled**, not offload performance.

Setup: Step 3.5 FP8, 8 H200 GPUs, TP=8, PP=1, async scheduling; 128 concurrent lanes over 100 turns, starting at 640 prompt tokens and adding 320 generated plus 320 random tokens per turn. Each turn includes a 1-second pause, counted in RPM. Ratios are normalized to expert return disabled.

| Configuration | Mean latency (s, lower is better) | Requests/min (higher is better) |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Routed-expert return disabled | 5.695 (1.00x) | 1144.20 (1.00x) |
| Full routed-expert output | 6.642 (1.17x) | 999.29 (0.87x) |
| Prefix omission | 5.793 (1.02x) | 1127.64 (0.99x) |

In this workload, prefix omission reduces mean-latency overhead relative to no expert return from approximately 17% to 2%.

items.title: [Perf][KV Offload] Record GPU-local prefix reuse
items.body:
# [Bugfix][KV Offload] Record GPU-local prefix reuse in offload recency

## Summary

The CPU offload cache can hold a backing copy of a prefix that is also
resident on GPU. When a request hits that prefix on GPU, it bypasses
`prepare_load()`, so CPU recency is not updated. The CPU cache may then evict
the backing copy even though the prefix was just reused.

This change records the GPU-local hit as a request-scoped access. It only
refreshes recency for keys already present and ready in CPU; it does not load,
store, or backfill GPU-only keys. Existing load/store decisions are unchanged.

## Implementation

- Add `record_access()` to `OffloadingManager` and propagate it through
  tiering.
- Record the retained GPU-local prefix once per request, including sliding
  window boundaries.
- Keep `prepare_load()` and `prepare_store()` semantics unchanged.
- Add CPU policy, scheduler, and tiering tests.

Example (simplified LRU):

```text
CPU LRU: A (oldest), B    GPU: A
Request reuses A on GPU; no CPU load is needed.
Before: CPU order unchanged; inserting D may evict A.
After:  A becomes recent; inserting D may evict B instead.
Later, if A leaves GPU, its CPU copy can still serve as a fallback.
```

## Relationship to existing work

- #51787 introduced request-scoped recency tracking; this fixes the missing
  GPU-local access source.
- #57325 changes joint lookup for `SimpleCPUOffloadConnector`; this change
  targets recency accounting in `OffloadingConnector`.
- #57646 exposes processed-prefix metadata; it does not update cache recency.

## Test plan

Commands run against the latest `origin/main`:

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/v1/kv_offload/cpu/test_manager.py \
  tests/v1/kv_offload/tiering/test_tiering_offloading.py -q
```

Result: **110 passed**, 14 warnings. The targeted scheduler regression also
passed.

Pre-commit checks passed for all changed files, including Ruff, formatting,
typos, mypy, SPDX, forbidden-import, and configuration checks.

description. The human submitter must review every changed line and verify
the final test results before opening the pull request.

items.title: [KV Connector][Mooncake] Start async lookup on the input thread via on_preschedule_request
items.body:
## Overview

Start MooncakeStore's async prefix lookup on the engine-core input thread as soon as a request arrives, so the lookup overlaps both the wait for the busy loop to pick up the request and the wait in the scheduler's waiting queue. GPU KV allocation and transfer remain in the scheduler's existing path.

This adds a generic connector hook, `KVConnectorBase_V1.on_preschedule_request(request)`, in place of using `on_new_request()` (which runs on the scheduler thread, after the request has already waited in the input queue).

## Design: start on the input thread, hand off via the request, adopt on the scheduler thread

`on_preschedule_request` runs on the input thread and may run concurrently with `schedule()`. To keep connectors free of locks:

- The hook must not read or write mutable connector or scheduler state. It may only start self-contained, thread-safe background work and return a handle.
- `EngineCore.preprocess_add_request` stores the handle on `request.kv_preschedule_handle`. The request then travels through the input queue, which gives the scheduler thread a happens-before edge on the handle.
- The connector adopts the handle on the scheduler thread (Mooncake: in `get_num_new_matched_tokens`) and owns it from then on.

For MooncakeStore:

- `LookupKeyClient.prefetch()` (input thread) only takes a slot from a `BoundedSemaphore` and submits to the single lookup executor. The ZMQ socket is still used only by that executor thread. It returns a `LookupState` without registering it.
- `LookupKeyClient.adopt()` (scheduler thread) registers the state in `_lookups`, which only the scheduler thread touches. The existing `lookup()` reuse, signature-change and TTL logic then applies unchanged.
- An unadopted handle is cancelled in `request_finished` (a request aborted while it was still waiting). Adopted lookups are discarded on finish, preemption, reset and close, as before.
- Requests with `skip_reading_prefix_cache`, sub-alignment prompts, or no block hashes are not prefetched.

## Claims

- With `lookup_async=True`, `enable_lookup=True`, and a positive `lookup_prefetch_limit`, eligible requests submit their lookup on the input thread at arrival. Off by default.
- `lookup_prefetch_limit` caps arrival-time lookups in flight. A slot is released when the RPC completes or is cancelled, so it cannot leak if a request never reaches the scheduler. Over the cap, the request is looked up when the scheduler first reaches it. Scheduler lookups are not capped.
- Arrival-time lookups create no `LoadSpec` or GPU allocation. The scheduler still computes the external tokens to load from its current local-prefix hit count.
- An arrival-time result older than `lookup_prefetch_ttl_s` (default 2 s) at the scheduler's first probe is looked up again. Cached async results expire the same amount of time after their first read. A changed token/hash range also triggers a fresh lookup.
- `MultiConnector` does not forward `on_preschedule_request` yet (base default: no-op), so the feature is off when MooncakeStore is wrapped in a `MultiConnector`.

## Validation

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest --confcutdir=tests/v1/kv_connector/unit \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_store_scheduler.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_store_connector.py -q
```

**124 passed** (Linux, Python 3.12, on current `main`). New and updated cases cover:

- an input-thread prefetch adopted by the scheduler-thread lookup with a single RPC
- the in-flight cap, including slot release on completion and scheduler lookups bypassing the cap
- a duplicate adopt keeping the existing lookup
- expiry before the first probe, and changed or expired queries
- skipping ineligible requests
- cancelling an unadopted handle on finish, and discarding on finish or preemption

`pre-commit run --files <changed files>`, `pre-commit run mypy --hook-stage manual`, and `git diff --check` all passed.

Not run: GPU serving, real Mooncake transfers, model evaluation, TTFT/throughput benchmarks. Those, plus human line-by-line review, are required before marking this ready.

## Trade-offs

An earlier lookup adds backend work for requests that later abort or hit entirely in the local cache, and the single lookup worker can queue that work ahead of later requests. The cap bounds this. The TTL can cause a second lookup after a long queue wait. Both defaults need measurement on real workloads. Cancelling a queued future works; an RPC that is already running cannot be interrupted.

Duplicate-work checks: searched open vllm-project/vllm PRs for Mooncake lookup, async/prefetch lookup, `on_new_request` lookup, and connector input-thread hooks. #48230 skips lookups for locally reused prefixes, which is a different change. #42321 (enqueue-time prefetch for `LMCacheMPConnector`, scheduler-thread `on_new_request`) was closed for inactivity, not rejected. This PR adds an input-thread hook with a handle-handoff contract, which also lets `LMCacheMPConnector` start its lookup earlier if it adopts the hook.

items.title: [Perf][Scheduler] Add risk-aware prefix-cache admission
items.body:
## Purpose

Related to #48485. This is an opt-in admission-side approach to prefix-cache
reuse loss under constrained KV capacity. It does not implement the issue's
proposed waiting-queue-informed eviction policy; block eviction remains unchanged.

Before allocating blocks for a fresh waiting request, the risk policy inspects
the free-block queue against estimated full-prompt block demand, excluding the
candidate's own cache-hit blocks. Potential cached-block exposure triggers
ranking of a bounded waiting window by cached-prefix length.

- Skip policy lookups when no admission slot is available, including slots held
  by paused streaming sessions.
- Recompute a promoted head's cache hit and allocation demand before allocation.
- Allow at most one risk-ranking attempt per admission position.
- Bound free-queue inspection; an inconclusive scan does not reject admission.

The window defaults to zero, leaving the policy disabled. The risk path currently
uses the custom scheduler entry point; selecting a nonzero window alone on the
base scheduler enables the threshold-based path instead. For the risk path, set:

```python
scheduler_cls="vllm.v1.core.sched.qwenfuse_risk.RiskPerfScheduler"
cache_aware_admission_window=16
enable_prefix_caching=True
async_scheduling=False
```

The supported risk-policy scope is synchronous FCFS with local prefix caching
and a single full-attention KV group. KV connectors, LoRA, encoder-decoder
models, speculative/lookahead decoding, and prefix replay are excluded by the
current guard. The risk subclass uses exposure, rather than the configured
legacy usage threshold, as its ranking trigger.

## Test Plan and Current Results

Validated after integrating upstream main at
`e5f3d08d722870a5301560fad0cfa65b7e333900`. The update adapts risk admission
to the upstream KV-holding waiting queue and deferred-request handling.
It retains upstream queue priority, avoids popping an admitted request twice,
and resets the bounded ranking retry when the admission position advances.
The change relative to that main snapshot remains confined to nine scheduler,
configuration, KV-manager, and test files.

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py -q --tb=short
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py   -k 'cache_aware_admission or risk_admission' -q --tb=short
```

- Targeted admission regression: **25 passed**. Three added tests cover
  KV-holding request priority, risk rechecking after a successful admission,
  and risk rechecking after a promoted request is skipped.
- Full scheduler regression: **220 passed, 2 failed**. Both failures reproduce
  on unmodified target main in the same single-GPU environment:
  `test_async_scheduling_pp_allows_rescheduling_with_output_placeholders`
  and `test_diffusion_read_deferral_keeps_a_longer_pp_wait` fail GPU-count
  validation for PP=2 and PP=3 respectively. They were not skipped or
  reported as passing.
- Local style and type checks: **passed** on all nine changed Python files, using the applicable upstream hooks, including Ruff, typos, mypy for Python 3.10-3.13, SPDX headers, and Buildkite test tethering.
- Qwen3-8B BF16 / FlashAttention 2 eager smoke passed with the risk policy,
  APC, chunked prefill, window 4, and a 4 GiB KV budget. One warmup request
  and two subsequent requests completed with 8 output tokens each;
  the repeated prompt reused **224 cached tokens**.

This validation used the updated Python source with the existing Python
3.12.14 / PyTorch 2.13.0+cu130 environment and September 20 native extensions
on an A100-PCIE-40GB. It is not a fresh native build or new performance result.
The eager smoke does not establish CUDA Graph execution, model-quality
equivalence, or multi-GPU compatibility.

## Historical Performance Results

Measurements on commit `27757dde`, A100-PCIE-40GB, Qwen3-8B BF16,
FlashAttention 2, with APC and chunked prefill enabled. Baseline and risk-policy
runs used the same operator configuration; only the admission policy differed.

For the constrained 8 GiB random mixed fixed-burst workload:

- Median throughput improvement: **5.02%**.
- Median batch completion time reduction: **4.78%**.
- Five of six paired comparisons improved; throughput changes ranged from
  **-2.37% to +6.12%**.
- Sufficient-capacity and all-cold controls showed near-zero median changes.
- Cold-request TTFT increased substantially for one seed.

These are historical fixed-burst measurements, not sustained-serving results
or performance measurements on the current submitted head.

## Known Limits and Review Questions

- Cached-prefix ranking can delay cold requests; the current implementation
  does not provide an aging mechanism or a bound on waiting time.
- A bounded waiting window cannot discover reusable prefixes beyond that window.
- Exposure is a snapshot-based estimate, not proof that a particular waiting
  request's reusable prefix will be evicted. Decode growth and future frees
  are not predicted.
- Scheduler CPU overhead, sustained-load fairness, and updated-head performance
  still need measurement. No overhead-neutrality or starvation-free guarantee
  is claimed.
- The current integration uses a custom scheduler subclass and retains the
  threshold-based base path. Feedback on the preferred upstream configuration
  and integration surface is welcome.

items.title: [Bugfix][Metrics] Do not count skip_reading_prefix_cache requests as external prefix cache misses
items.body:
Closes #57596

## Purpose

With a KV connector, a request that sets `skip_reading_prefix_cache` (`prompt_logprobs`, and `token_embed` / `token_classify` / `plugin` pooling) is counted as a full external prefix cache miss: `vllm:external_prefix_cache_queries` grows by the prompt length, `vllm:external_prefix_cache_hits` by nothing, and the "External prefix cache hit rate" log line drops accordingly. This PR stops counting such a request, the rule the local prefix cache already applies.

Since #57269 the scheduler discards the connector's hit for such a request (`ext_tokens, load_kv_async = 0, False`), which is right: those rows must be computed. But the stats derived a few lines later still use the discarded answer, so `connector_prefix_cache_queries = request.num_tokens` and `connector_prefix_cache_hits = 0` are recorded. The local side excludes the same request on purpose: `KVCacheManager.record_prefix_cache_stats` (#48860) returns early with the comment "Don't count a request that skipped the cache lookup". #30522 defined the external counters as the tokens actually queried from the connector; a request that never reads the answer did not query it.

Before #57269 the two in-tree offload connectors (`OffloadingConnector`, `SimpleCPUOffload`) already returned 0 for this flag themselves, so their flagged requests were already counted as misses; every other connector loaded the rows and counted a hit. After #57269 all of them count a miss. This PR makes all of them count nothing.

## Changes

- `vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py`: leave `connector_prefix_cache_queries` and `connector_prefix_cache_hits` at their initial 0 when `request.skip_reading_prefix_cache` is set, so the existing `connector_prefix_cache_queries != 0` guard at the record site skips the request. The connector is still consulted and `update_state_after_alloc(request, blocks, 0)` still runs; only the two counters change.
- `tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py`: `test_kv_connector_honors_skip_reading_prefix_cache` (from #57269, same setup: mock connector reporting a 32-token hit, one plain and one `prompt_logprobs` request of 64 tokens) now also asserts that `connector_prefix_cache_stats` counts one request, 64 queries, 32 hits. (Review: originally a separate test with the same setup plus a comment above the guard; both folded away.)

## Test Plan

```bash
# the stats assertions fail on main (requests == 2), pass with the change
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py -k test_kv_connector_honors_skip_reading_prefix_cache

# what the ":computer: (CPU) V1 Others" shard runs, from tests/
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -m cpu_test v1/core
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -m cpu_test v1/kv_connector/unit
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -m cpu_test v1/metrics

pre-commit run --files vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py
pre-commit run mypy-3.12 --files vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py --hook-stage manual
```

End to end, on the CPU backend with a real connector: `facebook/opt-125m`, `enforce_eager`, prefix caching off (so every prompt token is a connector query), `ExampleConnector` (the in-tree shared-storage connector) with `kv_role="kv_both"`, one 401-token prompt sent three times: plain (stores KV), plain again (served from storage), then with `prompt_logprobs=1`. Counters read through `llm.get_metrics()`.

## Test Result

Fedora 44, Python 3.12, torch 2.13.0+cpu, transformers 5.17.0, no GPU.

| | `main` (44dd18fe) | this branch |
|---|---|---|
| the stats assertions in `test_kv_connector_honors_skip_reading_prefix_cache` | `assert 2 == 1` (external_stats.requests) | passed |
| `-m cpu_test v1/core` | | 636 passed |
| `-m cpu_test v1/kv_connector/unit` | | 396 passed, 2 skipped |
| `-m cpu_test v1/metrics` | | 20 passed |
| pre-commit, mypy-3.12 | | all hooks passed |

End to end, `vllm:external_prefix_cache_queries` / `_hits` after each request:

| request | `main` | this branch |
|---|---|---|
| 1, plain, first sight | 401 / 0 | 401 / 0 |
| 2, plain, served from storage ("Inject KV cache of 384 tokens") | 802 / 384 | 802 / 384 |
| 3, same prompt, `prompt_logprobs=1` | **1203 / 384** | 802 / 384 |
| engine log line | `External prefix cache hit rate: 31.9%` | `External prefix cache hit rate: 47.9%` |

On request 3 the connector logs "External Cache Hit!" and injects nothing in both cases; only the accounting differs.

Also run: the change inverted on purpose (`if request.skip_reading_prefix_cache:`) fails the stats assertions and all four cases of the existing `test_external_prefix_cache_metrics` (5 failed), and the file reverts byte-identically (sha256); the module in two seeded shuffled orders (175 passed each); the #57269 and #48860 tests unchanged; a fresh clone with a fresh venv following `docs/getting_started/installation/cpu.md` (Python-only build) reproduces the 8 relevant tests passing and the end-to-end numbers above.

Model evaluation: not applicable. This changes what two counters record; scheduling, KV loads and model outputs are untouched (request 3 is scheduled in full and computes its prompt in both cases).

## Not in this PR

- Whether a flagged request should count as an external query at all is a metrics-semantics question; this PR follows the local side's existing answer. If maintainers prefer counting it as a query with 0 hits on both sides, the change is the local one instead.
- The CPU Python-only build docs (`cpu.md`, `VLLM_PRECOMPILED_WHEEL_VARIANT=cpu`) fail on a GPU-less Fedora host because `setup.py is_rocm_system()` sees the distro's `/usr/bin/rocminfo` before reading the variant; and `VLLM_PRECOMPILED_WHEEL_COMMIT=nightly`, documented in `gpu.cuda.inc.md`, is rejected by `setup.py` as "not valid". Both found while setting up for this PR; happy to file them as issues.

## Not a duplicate

Searched open PRs for `skip_reading_prefix_cache`, `external_prefix_cache`, `connector_prefix_cache_stats`, `prefix cache stats`, and open and closed issues for `external prefix cache hit rate` and `skip_reading_prefix_cache`. #39566 is the local-side double count on allocation failure (superseded by #48860 on main); #50795 guards the runner against the same flag and does not touch the counters; #54335 touches `update_from_output` only. No open PR or issue covers the connector counters.

## AI assistance

Claude Code assisted me with this. I chose the target, set the workflow and the evidence bar (reproduce on a real host before touching code, a test that fails first, every claim in this description backed by a run), directed each step and reviewed the code, the test and the evidence before anything was posted. The tracing, the fix and test, the runs listed above and the first draft of this description were done with it under that direction.

items.title: [Docs][Metrics] Document prefix cache hit rate monitoring and add a G…
items.body:
## Overview The prefix caching guide never mentions `vllm:prefix_cache_hits` or `vllm:prefix_cache_queries`, and none of the example dashboards chart the hit rate. Working out what the number actually counts currently means reading the scheduler. This adds a short Monitoring section to `docs/features/automatic_prefix_caching.md` and a hit rate panel to the Prometheus and Grafana example dashboard. ## Claims - The guide gives the PromQL for the hit rate and explains why it can differ from the "Prefix cache hit rate" log line, which covers the last 1000 requests rather than a time window. - It lists what limits the number and what it leaves out: full-block hits, the recomputed last token, the system prompt upper bound, preemption reschedules and requests that skip the lookup. I checked each one against `kv_cache_manager.py`, `scheduler.py` and `stats.py`. - The panel goes in the empty slot next to TPOT and copies the Cache Utilization panel's settings. No existing panels change. Docs and the example dashboard only. ## Validation I ran the Prometheus and Grafana example against vLLM 0.31.0 on one A10G and imported the dashboard from this branch. The only change to the example setup was adding Grafana's image renderer for the screenshot. The model was a randomly initialized 2-layer Llama with a small word-level tokenizer, which is enough because the hit rate only depends on token IDs. Load came from `vllm bench serve --dataset-name random --random-output-len 16 --ignore-eos --num-prompts 600 --request-rate 4`, run in two phases: | phase | prompts | hits / queries | hit rate | expected | |---|---|---|---|---| | A | `--random-prefix-len 2048 --random-input-len 256` | 1,227,232 / 1,382,400 | 0.888 | 599 × 2048 / (600 × 2304) = 0.887 | | B | `--random-prefix-len 0 --random-input-len 2304` | 4,576 / 1,382,400 | 0.003 | ~0 | Hits and queries are the counter deltas over each phase. The panel shows the same two plateaus. The log line shows the window difference nicely. It read 88.8% after phase A and 35.8% after phase B, because its 1000-request window still held 400 requests from A: (400 × 2048 + 4,576) / (1000 × 2304) = 0.358. `pre-commit run markdownlint-cli2` and `typos` pass on both files. ## Details No open PR touches either file. #56923 also documents metrics, but only in `docs/design/metrics.md` and `loggers.py`. I only changed the `prometheus_grafana` example. The dashboards in `examples/observability/dashboards/` come in Grafana and Perses pairs, so adding the panel there is better as its own PR. I used Claude to trace the counting logic and draft the text. I reviewed every line and checked each claim against the code and the run above. ---

In particular, `KVCacheManager.get_computed_blocks()` already returns 0 cached tokens when `request.skip_reading_prefix_cache` is True.
