items.title: test(prefix cache): pin two mamba "align" + EAGLE prefix-cache defects
items.body:
Tests only, no production change. Three properties of mamba `align` + EAGLE/MTP prefix caching, pinned as executable assertions so a fix can be judged against them.

CPU only: drives the KV-cache manager through the existing `make_kv_cache_manager` / `make_request` harness. No model execution, no GPU.

```
11 passed, 7 xfailed
```

**How to read the table.** A test that **passes** on `main` is pinning behaviour as it is today — it goes red if that behaviour changes, intentionally or not. A test marked **xfail** is asserting the behaviour we want and does not get it; it carries `xfail(strict=True)`, so CI stays green now, and when a fix lands the test XPASSes and `strict` turns that into a failure — the marker has to be removed together with the fix. Nothing here is expected to be red on `main`.

---

## 1. The EAGLE drop costs a whole block, not one hash unit

`tests/v1/core/prefix_cache/test_eagle_mamba_drop_cost.py` — block 16, hash unit 4, producer caches 48 tokens (three whole blocks), consumer shares all 48.

`prefix_match_unit` exists so the drop costs one hash unit rather than one cache block. It does that for full attention, but not for the reconciled hit: mamba is capped at the attention candidate (44) and its state exists only at 16/32/48, so its lookup falls back to 32.

| test | what it measures | on `main` |
|------|------------------|-----------|
| `test_full_attention_gives_up_only_one_hash_unit` | full attention's own hit is `48 - 4 = 44` — the drop is one hash unit, as designed | **passes** |
| `test_mamba_alone_reaches_the_full_prefix` | mamba's own hit is `48` — `MambaManager` ignores `drop_eagle_block` | **passes** |
| `test_without_eagle_nothing_is_given_up` | with EAGLE off the joint hit is `48`, isolating the drop as the cause | **passes** |
| `test_reconciled_hit_should_not_give_up_a_whole_block` | joint hit should be `44`; it is `32`. Also asserts every group returned enough blocks to cover the hit | **xfail** |

Neither group gives up a block on its own — it is given up in the reconciliation.

---

## 2. Sparse mamba keys walked as if they were a dense grid

`tests/v1/core/prefix_cache/test_mamba_align_sparse_keys.py` — parametrised over two shapes, `[toy]` (hash 2, attention block 2, mamba block 4) and `[large-block]` (hash 16, attention block 64, mamba block 64), so nothing depends on one set of sizes.

Under `align`, interior mamba blocks are null and carry no key on purpose — the group's only hittable positions are chunk ends. `emit_cached_block_events` walks the hit list positionally, as though every index carried a key.

| test | what it measures | on `main` |
|------|------------------|-----------|
| `test_mamba_group_grid_is_sparse[toy]` / `[large-block]` | the mamba group stores exactly one key (the prompt tail); the interior block index has none | **passes** |
| `test_emit_cached_block_events_current_shape[toy]` / `[large-block]` | what the event stream emits today — the two invented keys, and a `token_ids` span twice the length of the hit. Unmarked, so it goes red the moment the shape changes | **passes** |
| `test_emit_cached_block_events_invents_mamba_keys[toy]` / `[large-block]` | the published set should contain the one key that was stored and should not contain a key beyond the hit; today it is the reverse | **xfail** |
| `test_emit_cached_block_events_indexerror_on_unaligned_prompt[toy]` / `[large-block]` | on a prompt not aligned to the mamba block the same walk runs off the end of the block-hash view and raises `IndexError` inside `get_computed_blocks`. Pinned with `raises=IndexError` so a different exception is a failure, not a silent pass | **xfail** |
| `test_plain_mamba_align_no_partial_hash_also_invents_keys` | the same invented key with **no** `prefix_match_unit` set at all (`hash_block_size == block_size`), so this is not a partial-matching-only problem | **xfail** |

Requires `kv_cache_report_mode="full"` to observe, except the last, which needs only `align`.

---

## 3. The same drop, when the shared prefix ends before the producer's prompt

`tests/v1/core/prefix_cache/test_eagle_mamba_shared_system_prompt.py` — block 16, hash unit 4, producer prompt 40 = 24 shared + 16 private, consumer shares the first 24.

Section 1 uses a producer whose whole prompt _is_ the shared prefix. A served system prompt is the other shape: every request opens with the same preamble and then diverges, so the producer's prompt tail sits over tokens no consumer shares. The shared prefix ends mid-block (`24 % 16 = 8`), so full attention stops at the last whole shared block (16) and the drop takes it to 12; mamba has state at 0 and 16 only, and capped at 12 it can only fall back to 0.

| test | what it measures | on `main` |
|------|------------------|-----------|
| `test_full_attention_gives_up_only_one_hash_unit` | full attention's own hit is `16 - 4 = 12` | **passes** |
| `test_mamba_alone_reaches_the_shared_block_boundary` | mamba's own hit is `16` | **passes** |
| `test_without_eagle_the_hit_survives` | with EAGLE off both groups reach 16 and the joint hit is `16` | **passes** |
| `test_reconciled_hit_is_currently_nothing` | the joint hit today is `0` — the consumer recomputes the entire shared prefix. Unmarked, so it goes red when this improves | **passes** |
| `test_reconciled_hit_should_reach_the_resume_point` | joint hit should be `12`, the position EAGLE resumes from | **xfail** |

Here the drop does not cost a block — it costs the **entire** hit, while both groups independently reach at least 12.

The distinction between this and section 1 matters for where a fix puts the state: a check-point at the producer's prompt **tail** cannot serve this shape, because 40 — and 36, one hash unit below it — are both over the private suffix. The state has to exist one hash unit below the shared _block_ boundary.

items.title: [Bugfix] Exclude DSpark draft-model KV-cache group from core prefix-cache lookup veto
items.body:
Fixes #48455

### Purpose

Split out from #47891 per review feedback there: this PR is the core-only
half of that fix, the offloading connector's PR will be rebased to align
with this once it merges.

`HybridKVCacheCoordinator.find_longest_cache_hit()`
(`vllm/v1/core/kv_cache_coordinator.py`) requires every KV-cache group of a
hybrid model to independently report a nonzero hit before confirming any
prefix reuse for a request, on the GPU tier. When serving DeepSeek-V4 with
DSpark speculative decoding, the draft-model KV-cache group can never
satisfy this, so it incorrectly vetoes reuse of the target model's own
KV-cache groups (SWA, compressed C4A/C128A, indexer) even when those groups
genuinely still hold valid, resident GPU blocks for a matching prefix. A
follow-up request sharing a prefix with GPU blocks still resident from a
previous request, or a request resumed after preemption, gets treated as
having zero reusable prefix and is fully recomputed from scratch.

### What this PR changes

- `SpeculativeConfig.has_ephemeral_draft_context()` (new,
  `vllm/config/speculative.py`): a predicate on the speculative method
  itself, following the same pattern as the existing `use_dflash()` and
  `use_dspark()`. Returns `True` for `"dspark"`. Identifies methods whose
  draft-model KV-cache group is rebuilt from the target model's auxiliary
  hidden states at generation time, rather than accumulated incrementally
  through the draft's own attention (EAGLE/EAGLE3/MTP).
- `KVCacheGroupSpec.eagle_group_is_veto_exempt` (new,
  `vllm/v1/kv_cache_interface.py`): a plain boolean field, computed once
  from the predicate above wherever `is_eagle_group` is already set
  (`vllm/v1/core/kv_cache_utils.py`).
- `HybridKVCacheCoordinator.find_longest_cache_hit()`
  (`vllm/v1/core/kv_cache_coordinator.py`, the primary fix): when a
  veto-exempt eagle group reports zero hit blocks in a round, that group is
  dropped from the round instead of zeroing the whole request's confirmed
  hit length. It still participates normally in every other round,
  including any round where it reports a nonzero hit.

Neither `find_longest_cache_hit()` nor `find_longest_cache_hit_per_group()`
contains a single method-name string comparison; the exemption is derived
once from `KVCacheGroupSpec.eagle_group_is_veto_exempt` and consumed as a
plain boolean.

### `eagle_group_is_veto_exempt` does not mean "excluded from the lookup"

A veto-exempt group's hit length is still computed every round exactly like
any other group's. The exemption only changes what happens when that
computed hit length is zero: normally a zero from any group vetoes
(truncates to zero) every other group's independently confirmed hit; for a
group whose KV has no request-independent, stable meaning, a zero is not
informative about whether the target model's own groups have a real,
reusable hit, so it is left unconfirmed for that round instead of zeroing
everyone else. A nonzero hit from the same group participates in the
AND-convergence exactly like before, with no special casing.

### Why this has no downside for DSpark, unlike EAGLE/EAGLE3/MTP

EAGLE/EAGLE3/MTP's draft model runs its own causal self-attention over
tokens it has itself drafted. Once a draft token's KV is computed, it stays
valid for the rest of the request and is genuinely reusable across requests
that share a prefix.

DSpark's draft context KV works differently.
`DSparkDeepseekV4Model.precompute_and_store_context_kv`
(`vllm/models/deepseek_v4/nvidia/dspark.py`) derives each draft layer's
context KV directly from the target model's own auxiliary hidden states at
that exact decode step, and writes it into that layer's context slots. This
runs once per drafting round: the target produces real hidden states,
DSpark writes fresh context KV from them, the draft model attends over that
freshly written context to produce this round's speculative tokens, and the
next round overwrites those same slots again from the target's next hidden
states. It is a write-then-immediately-consume-within-round buffer, not an
incrementally accumulated cache. There is no window in which reusing it
would be meaningful, so this PR does not forfeit any reuse opportunity
DSpark had. It never had one to begin with.

### Scope

Two independent scope boundaries.

**Speculative method: DSpark only, DFlash is a follow-up.** DFlash's
drafter builds its context KV from the target model's auxiliary hidden
states the same way DSpark's does, so `has_ephemeral_draft_context()` could
mechanically be extended to cover `"dflash"` with a one-line change. This
PR deliberately does not do that: DFlash has not been validated end to end
in a live server (blocked on an unrelated attention-backend /
KV-cache-dtype compatibility gap for the DeepSeek-V4 target, plus a
checkpoint-architecture mismatch for the specific community DFlash
checkpoint available), so claiming the fix for DFlash here would be a claim
without evidence.

**Model architecture: the whole DeepSeek-V4 family (Flash, Pro, and any
other size variant), not size-specific.** `eagle_group_is_veto_exempt` is
only ever set inside `_annotate_eagle_groups_deepseek_v4` (pre-existing
code, `vllm/v1/core/kv_cache_utils.py`), which is itself hard-scoped to
`model_version == "deepseek_v4"`. That value is set in exactly one place,
`vllm/models/deepseek_v4/attention.py`, shared by the whole
`DeepseekV4ForCausalLM` architecture regardless of size variant. Every
other model architecture falls back to a different, pre-existing path that
flags all groups as `is_eagle_group` uniformly and never touches this new
field, so this PR has no effect there.

Live serving validation of this mechanism, via #47891 which shares the
same core fix, was on the Flash size variant.

### Testing

| Suite | Result |
|---|---|
| `tests/v1/core/test_prefix_caching.py` | included in full run below |
| `tests/v1/core/` (full directory, 2 GPUs) | 423 passed, 0 failed |

Run inside an isolated throwaway container (source `.py` tree synced over
an installed `vllm` build to avoid needing a full rebuild), on this
branch alone, with no dependency on the offloading connector changes in
#47891.

items.title: [Bugfix] Bound accepted-token state lookups in GDN/KDA spec decode
items.body:
## Summary

On a hybrid GDN model (Qwen3.5 / Qwen3.6) with MTP speculative decoding and prefix caching (`--mamba-cache-mode align`), the engine dies with `CUDA error: unspecified launch failure` within 7-10 requests of agent-shaped traffic. The GPU faults, not the runtime: the signature is an SM address exception (`Xid 13`, `ESR 0x404000`) or an MMU fault (`Xid 31`), depending on whether the wild address happens to be mapped.

> **Validation scope (added 2026-08-19).** Everything below was developed and validated with
> `--mamba-cache-mode align` and `--enforce-eager`. That matters: `align` is the only branch in
> which `gpu_model_runner` still calls `num_accepted_tokens_event.synchronize()` (the wait is
> skipped when `use_async_scheduling and mamba_cache_mode != "align"`), and eager mode removes
> CUDA-graph stream structure. So this PR addresses accepted-count-derived indices that are
> **correctly synchronized but out of range**. It does **not** address the separate cross-stream
> race reported by @noonghunna under async scheduling with the default (non-`align`) mamba cache
> mode, where the accepted-count value itself arrives unsynchronized: in-kernel bounds cannot
> repair a value that arrives wrong. See the discussion in this thread; that path needs stream
> ordering, not bounds. Note `mamba_cache_mode` resolves per-model: with prefix caching and no
> explicit flag it is `"all"` (sync skipped) when `model_config.supports_mamba_prefix_caching`,
> else `"align"` (sync kept).

This is the crash half of the problems reported around hybrid-Mamba + MTP. It is distinct from the prefix-cache corruption in #43559 (the coordinator-level EAGLE cache-peek gating for Mamba), which is already handled on current `main`. This PR does not touch that path and does not claim to fix #43559; it fixes a separate GPU fault in two kernels downstream.

## Not a duplicate

- #51508 edits the same accepted-count lookups in five of the kernel files here, but only for a zero count, which it clamps to column 0 so the row's first state is read. This PR fails closed on zero and also bounds counts past the row. The two disagree on count 0: with #51508's kernel hunks merged onto this branch, all 5 zero-count KDA cases below fail and all 5 oversized-count cases pass (Triton interpreter on CPU), and `git merge-tree` at `8a2364605c` conflicts in `causal_conv1d.py` and `test_fused_sigmoid_gating_delta_rule.py`. Whichever lands second has to pick one zero-count policy.
- #55506 changes which block-table row the V2 mamba copy kernels read (request slot instead of batch row); this PR bounds the column inside that row. Complementary: no overlapping hunks in `mamba_utils.py`, and `git merge-tree` at `8a2364605c` is clean.

## Root cause: unchecked accepted-count-derived indices

Speculative decoding produces a per-request accepted-token count. Multiple GPU state consumers turn that count into an array index without bounding it, so a count that is stale, zero, or too large indexes outside its tensor and yields a wild address the GPU then dereferences.

**Site 1** `fused_recurrent_gated_delta_rule_fwd_kernel` (`fused_recurrent.py`):

```python
i_t = tl.load(num_accepted_tokens + i_n).to(tl.int64) - 1        # unbounded
state_idx = tl.load(ssm_state_indices + i_n * stride_indices_seq + i_t)
if state_idx <= 0: return                                        # positive garbage passes
p_h0 = h0 + state_idx * stride_init_state_token                  # dereferenced
```

`i_t` (= count - 1) is unbounded against a `stride_indices_seq`-column tensor. A zero accepted count gives `i_t == -1`, a read before this request's row (before the tensor for `i_n == 0`); a stale or too-large count reads past the row. The `state_idx <= 0` guard only rejects non-positive values, so an out-of-range read that returns a garbage positive int flows into the address math and faults the SM.

**Site 2** `_copy_mamba_state_block` (`mamba_utils.py`): the block-table columns derive from the same count and index the per-request block-table row unbounded; the loaded block id becomes `state_base_addr + block_id * state_block_stride`, which is then read and written.

The two sites fire under different loads. A light decode load exercises only Site 1; a heavy cache-transition load (long prefills, A->B->A prefix reuse) also drives Site 2. Both must be bounded.

## The fix

Both loads are masked to the valid range, so an out-of-range index falls into the existing invalid-state path instead of producing an address. No stream-ordering change, no device sync, no measurable throughput cost.

## Follow-up bounds audit

A follow-up audit expanded the same fail-closed rule to the remaining consumers in this path:

- Both FLA wrappers now zero rejected output deterministically instead of returning with new_empty storage visible downstream.
- _causal_conv1d_update_kernel now bounds the accepted-count offset before state address math; invalid active rows produce zero output and leave state unchanged.
- GPU regressions cover too-small/too-large accepted counts, NULL block IDs, source/destination columns crossing the block-table row, and temporal-bias overflow.

## Kimi K3 KDA expansion

The same accepted-count-derived state selection pattern also existed in Kimi K3 KDA fused recurrent decode, in both the NVIDIA and AMD vendored kernels. This PR masks that initial state-index load to the request row, zeroes all invalid-count output tokens, preserves state on invalid counts, and releases NVIDIA PDL dependents before the new empty/invalid early returns.

Since #58045, a one-sequence AMD spec-decode launch takes a new single-sequence path, so the one-sequence invalid-count test no longer reaches the AMD kernel's multi-sequence code. `test_kda_spec_invalid_accepted_count_spares_neighbor` adds a two-sequence batch on both kernels, and on AMD through both the dynamic and the static sequence-length paths: the sequence with the invalid count must zero its own output and keep its state, and the other sequence must match an all-valid batch. #58045 also added a `SPEC_DECODE_IMPLS` dict for the `fused_recurrent_kda` wrappers, so this PR's tests call the lower-level `fused_recurrent_kda_fwd` through a separate `SPEC_DECODE_FWD_IMPLS`.

## Mamba2 selective-state expansion

The Mamba2 selective-state-update kernel also derives its initial state-slot lookup from `num_accepted_tokens - 1`. It already clamps the lower side, but had no upper row bound. This update preserves that zero-count behavior and makes an oversized count fail closed: it writes zero output and returns before reading or writing state.

## Test commands and results

```
pytest tests/v1/worker/test_mamba_utils.py \
       tests/kernels/mamba/test_causal_conv1d.py \
       tests/kernels/mamba/test_mamba_ssm.py \
       tests/kernels/test_fused_sigmoid_gating_delta_rule.py \
       tests/models/kimi_k3/test_kda.py
```

All five need a GPU. The PR adds 20 cases to them.

### Re-run on this push (main `8a2364605c`, 2026-09-26)

NVIDIA GB10 (sm_121, driver 580.173.02), torch 2.13.0+cu132, triton 3.7.1, precompiled wheel for `9bf44c4013` (3 commits before the base, no `csrc/`, `cmake/`, `setup.py` or `requirements/` change in between):

| tree | passed | skipped | failed |
|---|---|---|---|
| main `8a2364605c` | 597 | 31 | 0 |
| this branch | 617 | 31 | 0 |

The 628 tests the two trees share have identical outcomes, and the 20 extra are this PR's cases, all passing. That includes all 28 cases of `test_kda_spec_decode_correctness` as #58045 reworked it; its `amd-*` cases run the vendored AMD Triton kernel on this NVIDIA card. The 31 skips are the same on both: 16 need sm_100 stochastic rounding, 13 are FlashInfer KDA paths this card does not support, 2 are unlabelled in `test_mamba_ssm.py`.

Negative controls, this branch with one kernel file swapped for main's copy, running only that file's new cases:

| file from main | result |
|---|---|
| `v1/worker/mamba_utils.py` | 4 of 4 fail |
| `mamba/ops/causal_conv1d.py` | 2 of 2 fail |
| `mamba/ops/mamba_ssm.py` | past-the-row case fails, in-row positive case passes |
| FLA `ops/fused_recurrent.py` | `num_accepted=0`: illegal memory access, `Xid 31`. `num_accepted=5`: wrong output |
| FLA `ops/fused_sigmoid_gating.py` | same as the line above |
| KDA `nvidia/.../fused_recurrent.py` | 4 of 4 nvidia cases fail |
| KDA `amd/.../fused_recurrent.py` | 6 of 6 amd cases fail, including all 4 two-sequence cases |

The two `Xid 31` lines (`FAULT_PTE ACCESS_TYPE_VIRT_READ`, one per FLA arm) are the only ones in the host log for the run. With the tree restored, the 20 new cases pass again and no further Xid is logged. Not run on AMD hardware: the `amd` cases above compile the vendored AMD kernel for NVIDIA.

CPU, x86_64, no GPU:

- `pre-commit run --files` on the 12 changed files, default and `manual` stages: every hook that selected a file passed, including `mypy-3.10` through `mypy-3.13` and the test-tethering check. The top-level `exclude:` skips `vllm/third_party/` and both vendored KDA directories for every hook, so 4 of the 12 files are not linted by CI.
- KDA invalid-count tests under the Triton interpreter (`TRITON_INTERPRET=1`, CPU tensors, the committed test functions called directly): 10 of 10 pass on this branch and 10 of 10 fail with the base's two KDA kernels swapped in. A launch hook recorded the AMD path each case took: the one-sequence cases run `IS_SINGLE_SEQUENCE=True`, the two-sequence cases run `SEQUENCE_LENGTH=0` (dynamic) and `SEQUENCE_LENGTH=3` (static).

### Historical, not re-run on this base

- 2026-09-22, RTX 5090 (sm_120), torch 2.13.0+cu130, tree `389e250d6f` on main `f944491db9`: 591 passed, 31 skipped, 0 failed across the five files, with the same one-file-swap negative controls (the KDA arms had 2 cases per vendor then). Details in [this comment](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/50021#issuecomment-5783551734).
- 2026-09-01, vLLM 0.28.0 container, `test_mamba_utils.py` only: 24 passed with the guard, 1 failed / 23 passed with `dst_col`'s upper bound neutralized, 24 passed restored.
- Original submission, RTX 5090, Qwen3.6-27B NVFP4, TP=1, `--enforce-eager --max-model-len 16384`, MTP 3 (`qwen3_5_mtp`), prefix caching on, `align` mode:

| build | crash (Xid) | corruption (A->B->A probe) |
|---|---|---|
| stock | dies at 7-10 requests, Xid every run | 0/N reproduced (already fixed on main) |
| Site 1 fix alone | survives light load; still crashes on the first heavy probe (`Xid 31`) | 0/N reproduced |
| **both fixes** | **68 heavy probes + a 39-minute soak, 0 new Xid** | **0/68 reproduced** |

  The A->B->A probe issues an agent-shaped sequence (long prefill, prefix reuse, 20 tool schemas) and reports whether a poisoned prefix reappears; 68/68 returned a clean verdict, which also confirms the out-of-range early-return does not drop a needed state copy. Warm throughput and MTP acceptance length (3.98-4.00 of 4) are unchanged.
- 2026-08-12, RTX 5090: 186 FLA/causal-conv kernel tests plus all 21 fused Mamba postprocess tests passed; KDA invalid-count 4/4 passed and 4/4 failed at the previous head `e7f66b199`; Mamba2 red/green with `num_accepted=4` against a three-column row.

## Model evaluation (historical)

GSM8K through the in-tree `tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py`: 1319 questions, 5-shot, temperature 0, seed 42, `max_tokens=256`, client concurrency 32. NVIDIA GB10, vLLM `0.26.1rc1.dev861+g9a198c0f8`, Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4 with `qwen3_5_mtp` at 4 speculative tokens, prefix caching, fp8 KV, async scheduling, `align` mode confirmed in every server log. Two runs per arm, interleaved, server restarted per run, the patch toggled with `git apply` / `git apply -R` on one install.

| arm | correct (pooled) | accuracy | output tok/s (mean) | mean acceptance length |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| patched | 2216/2638 | 0.840030 | 233.17 | 4.232 / 4.256 |
| stock | 2229/2638 | 0.844958 | 232.59 | 4.235 / 4.238 |

Difference -0.493 pp, z = 0.4913, two-sided p = 0.6232, 95% CI -1.47 to +2.46 pp. No accuracy, throughput or acceptance change the 2638-question comparison can resolve. This model exercises the GDN, FLA and causal-conv changes; it does not run the KDA or Mamba2 kernels. Full method, the concurrency-64 empty-output cliff seen equally in both arms, and the reproduce commands are in [this comment](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/50021#issuecomment-5411813140).

## Note: a separate, still-open livelock (#49203)

Independently of this crash, the same stack can occasionally hang: engine alive, `/v1/models` answering, but the in-flight request stuck at 0% GPU util with no Xid. It is rare and timing-variable (seen once, then not across the 68 probes here) and matches open issue #49203. This PR does not address it and does not claim to; the 68/68 clean-verdict result rules out this change as a cause.

## AI assistance

items.title: [Core][KV Connector] Share in-flight external-prefix KV loads
items.body:
Concurrent requests for the same externally cached prefix can allocate separate GPU destinations and transfer the prefix repeatedly. This change lets eligible requests share pending GPU blocks and wait for one load.

The block pool indexes exact pending prefixes by the existing hash/group namespace and pins their blocks with transfer-owned references. Pending entries are separate from readable prefix-cache hits; failed loads cannot be discovered, and completion removes the pending entry and releases its pins. The scheduler retains connector eligibility, request waiters, and completion/failure-policy handling. Successful loads are published before releasing an aborted initiating request. Followers cancel independently; failed readers detach before local recomputation. Pending loads prevent connector-cache resets.

Initial support is explicitly opt-in for the built-in CPUOffloadingSpec with built-in LRU/ARC policies: prefix caching enabled, one FullAttentionSpec group, exact contiguous block-aligned partial-prompt prefixes, including prefixes extending a local hit. Full-prompt loads, speculation, context parallelism, encoder inputs, custom specs/policies, and other connectors retain existing behavior. Cache salts and token-hash isolation are preserved.

Addresses #44882. Duplicate checks covered issue comments, open PRs referencing the issue, and area searches. #48189 closed unmerged; #44295 changes connector convoy handling, rather than shared core allocation/lifetime. #53067 and #55724 address connector context and admission. NIXL is being pursued as a separate follow-up by NolenLiang.

Validation on October 13, against main `f26d9f432c`:

```bash
HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 TRANSFORMERS_OFFLINE=1 .venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector/test_scheduler.py \
  tests/v1/core/test_prefix_caching.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_remote_prefill_lifecycle.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_kv_load_failure_recovery.py \
  -q --tb=short --maxfail=3 --confcutdir=tests/v1
```

**636 passed.** Coverage includes shared allocation/loading, transfer pins after all request references are released, pending/cache separation, group isolation, duplicate registration, initiating-request/follower cancellation, late followers, local-prefix extension, both failure policies, block/request receive failures (including aborted owners), queue/statistics cleanup, and reference/job cleanup. CPU-offload scheduler integration emits one logical load job in sync/async scheduling modes; worker completion is simulated. The earlier four request-level failure regressions failed before the fix and passed afterward.

`.venv/bin/python -m pre_commit run --files <eight changed files>` passed all applicable hooks, including mypy (Python 3.11 target), ruff, test tethering, and SPDX. `git diff origin/main --check` passed.

External evidence: [LysanderPhong reported five successful real CPU↔GPU test executions](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/57418#issuecomment-6094266885) on an RTX 5070 Ti Laptop at the older commit `244daac75b`: synthetic FP16 bytes, shared destinations, private tails, and cleanup. The archive/test checksums, source, logs, and JSON were reviewed; execution was not independently repeated. That evidence does not validate this pool revision, GPU cancellation/failure, model outputs, performance, or multi-rank behavior. Its evidence-oriented candidate test is not included here.

Local hardware is macOS arm64 without CUDA/XPU. **GPU lifecycle, model-output/accuracy evaluation, and hardware performance validation remain outstanding before merge.** No hardware performance claim is made. Upstream CI remains behind the contributor eligibility gate.

AI assistance: OpenAI Codex assisted with implementation, tests, and this description. The human submitter previously confirmed reviewing/testing the earlier revision. Subsequent queue/statistics changes, merges, and this block-pool revision still require human review and relevant test execution.

items.title: [Bugfix][KV Offload] Preserve running request prefixes across LRU store batches
items.body:
## Overview

Keep positioned prefixes useful under CPU-offload LRU pressure while their request is still running, across store batches and KV groups. Related to [this observation in #58804](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/58804#issuecomment-6098736505); this does not claim to explain or resolve all throughput regression in that issue.

## Claims

- Newly observed and inserted keys share one provisional request rank, with later token positions evicted first across batches.
- Existing-prefix reuse, transfer pinning, newer shared accesses, and cache resets retain their ordering contracts.
- No repeated full-prefix refresh; ARC frequency accounting stays at finalization and external policies inherit a no-op hook.

## Validation

Python base: `187a0eb98aa42341d703f83421d693fa7585581b`, Linux x86_64, Python 3.12, PyTorch 2.13.0+cpu.

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Added tests against the base manager/LRU | 11 failed, 2 passed |
| CPU manager and policy factory | 72 passed |
| Tiering and offloading scheduler | 465 passed |
| Complete cloud rerun on 2026-10-11 | 537 passed |
| All applicable pre-commit hooks, including mypy | Passed |

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q tests/v1/kv_offload/cpu/test_manager.py tests/v1/kv_offload/cpu/policies/test_factory.py
PYTHONPATH=/workspace/vllm-onboarding/offload-prefix-repro HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 .venv/bin/python -m pytest -p offline_model -q tests/v1/kv_offload/tiering/test_tiering_offloading.py tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector/test_scheduler.py
.venv/bin/python -m pre_commit run --files vllm/v1/kv_offload/cpu/policies/base.py vllm/v1/kv_offload/cpu/policies/lru.py vllm/v1/kv_offload/cpu/manager.py tests/v1/kv_offload/cpu/test_manager.py
```

The cloud-only `offline_model` fixture plugin supplies a local OPT configuration in place of the test factory's default `facebook/opt-125m` model parameter because model-host access was blocked. All other configuration parameters, production code and assertions remained active; no OPT weights were used. The unmodified base fails the same representative online-config tests before test setup under this network restriction. In a network-enabled checkout, omit the plugin and offline environment settings to use the ordinary test fixture.

Native CPU inference: two-layer tiny Llama with dummy weights, float32, greedy decoding, two 192-token prompts, block size 32, eight offload slots. A remains generating while B fills the tier. After aborting A and clearing only the model-side prefix cache, replay A:

| Metric | Base manager/LRU | This change |
|---|---:|---:|
| Second-turn cached tokens | 0 | 64 |
| Real KV pages read back | 0 | 2 |
| Output token IDs | 21, 17, 21, 17 | 21, 17, 21, 17 |

This executes the native CPU model using a test-only out-of-tree worker that copies real CPU KV pages synchronously. Existing CPU native extensions built at `e5d33a36e` were reused for both runs; only the manager/LRU differs. The separate real scheduler replay with three groups changes retained A positions from `[4,5]` to `[0,1]` in each group and issues a two-block load per group on the second turn.

CUDA transfer behavior, GPU TTFT/throughput, FS tiering and the reporter's Qwen/DFlash workload have not been measured. The dummy model checks usable KV reuse and the observed output, not model quality.

## Details

Insertion ranks previously left an unfinished request's head older than its tail until finalization. A later request could evict the head, making every remaining suffix chunk unreachable by contiguous-prefix lookup.

The new hook distinguishes fresh allocation from first observation. LRU assigns positioned keys `(request_rank, -token_position)` during the request, including already resident keys it reuses. The provisional rank is anchored at first observation, finalization still commits recency, and older requests cannot demote a newer shared access. Reset invalidates provisional state. Keys without token positions retain insertion ordering; chunks remain evictable rather than pinned.

The existing heap update/compaction path is reused. This adds a tuple per cached rank and a small scratch state per request, and has measurable bookkeeping cost:

<details>
<summary>CPU manager microbenchmark and variability</summary>


| Chunks/group (9 groups, batches of 8) | Base default median [min,max], ms | Changed default median [min,max], ms | Base full-prefix refresh median, ms |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 64 | 1.40 [1.31,2.10] | 1.79 [1.68,2.37] | 2.68 |
| 256 | 6.19 [5.94,9.04] | 7.75 [7.55,10.01] | 24.99 |
| 1024 | 26.75 [24.82,298.47] | 34.34 [34.05,309.39] | 414.57 |

Five runs per case, timing manager stores and position recording only. Median overhead is approximately 25–28% compared with the incorrect base ordering, but avoids the full-refresh alternative's repeated traversal (594,432 additional touch-key visits in the largest case). These CPU microbenchmarks do not establish a serving speedup. A regression test bounds token-position queries linearly without a timing threshold.

</details>

Not a duplicate: #57813 adds optional in-flight pin preference and saturation fallback across policies; #50422 adds SAE; #57746 records GPU-local reuse; #60469 changes KVCR recency. None fixes this default LRU cross-batch order. Checked issue comments and open PR searches for `58804 in:body`, offload LRU/prefix/session/recency and LRU tail.

AI assistance from OpenAI Codex was used during development.

items.title: [Bugfix][Core] Emit full reuse events for converged hybrid connector hits
items.body:
## Overview

Restore full prefix-cache reuse events for converged hybrid hits selected by a KV connector. This fixes missing `BlockStored` notifications without changing cache-hit lengths, allocation, or scheduling.

## Claims

- A nonzero, converged hybrid hit now emits the same full-report events as the regular lookup when events are enabled.
- Incremental reporting and disabled events remain silent; divergent hits are not prematurely reported.
- Scheduler fallback still publishes each reused group exactly once.

## Validation

**Regression tests (CPU):**
- New manager coverage: baseline 1 failed / 7 passed; fixed 8 passed.
- New Scheduler → connector lookup → publisher coverage: baseline 1 failed / 3 passed; fixed 4 passed. Restoring pristine source reproduces the original failure.
- Selected existing prefix-cache, Mamba chunk-split and Scheduler tests: 381 passed, 69 deselected (unrelated multimodal/encoder and multi-GPU cases excluded).
- Repository pre-commit hooks, including test tethering and mypy: passed.

```bash
VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu uv run --no-sync .venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/v1/core/test_prefix_caching.py tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py \
  -q -k 'hybrid_converged_hit_reports_reused_blocks or hybrid_full_hit_events_reach_scheduler_publisher'
```

**Actual GPU inference and event subscription:** RTX 5060 8 GB, PyTorch 2.13.0+cu130, Qwen/Qwen3.5-0.8B at revision `2fc06364715b967f1860aea9cf38778875588b17`, real NixlPullConnector/UCX, real ZMQ publisher/subscriber over IPC, MRV2, eager execution. No mock connector, mock publisher or synthetic worker output was used in this run.

| Run | Reused prompt tokens | Reuse BlockStored groups received over ZMQ | Generated token IDs |
|---|---:|---|---|
| Baseline | 544 | none | [1000, 1000] |
| Fixed | 544 | 0, 1, 2, 3 (once each) | [1000, 1000] |
| Restored baseline | 544 | none | [1000, 1000] |

Each run primes a 545-token prompt (`[1000] * 545`) and generates from it again with `extra_args={"kv_cache_report_mode": "full"}`. All cache groups have one cached block at the 544-token hit. A read-only wrapper records the connector lookup's hit length and divergence flag. For baseline/restored runs, only the lookup method is loaded from the saved pristine source in-process; the fixed run uses the patched method. Model, native extensions, configuration and subscriber are otherwise unchanged.

This validates the affected **local cache reuse path with a real connector**, not cross-node P/D transfer or HTTP serving. It is not a benchmark or a model-accuracy evaluation.

<details>
<summary>GPU run configuration and reproduction flow</summary>

```bash
VLLM_ENABLE_V1_MULTIPROCESSING=0 VLLM_SSM_CONV_STATE_LAYOUT=DS \
  uv run --no-sync .venv/bin/python repro.py
```

Construct `LLM` with:
```python
llm = LLM(
    model="Qwen/Qwen3.5-0.8B",
    revision="2fc06364715b967f1860aea9cf38778875588b17",
    language_model_only=True,
    max_model_len=4096,
    max_num_seqs=1,
    max_num_batched_tokens=4096,
    gpu_memory_utilization=0.7,
    enforce_eager=True,
    enable_prefix_caching=True,
    mamba_cache_mode="align",
    attention_config={"backend": "TRITON_ATTN"},
    additional_config={"gdn_prefill_backend": "triton"},
    kv_transfer_config=KVTransferConfig(
        kv_connector="NixlConnector", kv_role="kv_consumer"
    ),
    kv_events_config=KVEventsConfig(
        enable_kv_cache_events=True, publisher="zmq",
        endpoint="ipc:///tmp/candidate-c-repro.ipc", topic="candidate-c",
    ),
)
params = SamplingParams(
    max_tokens=2, temperature=0, ignore_eos=True,
    extra_args={"kv_cache_report_mode": "full"},
)
prompt = {"prompt_token_ids": [1000] * 545}
llm.generate([prompt], params, use_tqdm=False)  # prime
llm.generate([prompt], params, use_tqdm=False)  # reuse
```

Start a ZMQ SUB subscriber before constructing the engine, subscribe to `candidate-c`, and decode the final multipart frame with `msgspec.msgpack.Decoder(KVEventBatch)`. Wait for the prime batch to drain before recording the second request. The prime request publishes initial storage events in both versions; the second request publishes the four reuse events only with this patch. The included Scheduler regression exercises the same routing and guards independently of GPU timing.

The validation environment used the checkout's Python sources with native extensions copied from an existing editable installation. The separate PR virtualenv borrowed existing read-only Python dependencies; additional runtime packages were installed only in that PR virtualenv. The learning environment was not modified. No CUDA/C++ source changes were made.

</details>

## Details

`Scheduler._get_local_prefix_cache_hit` selects `get_computed_blocks_for_connector` for capable connectors. Unlike `get_computed_blocks`, its successful per-group return path did not emit full reuse reports. The patch reuses the coordinator's existing emitter, guarded by a nonzero converged hit and the existing reporting switches. It does not add a second cache lookup.

Duplicate searches for `get_computed_blocks_for_connector` and `kv_cache_report_mode` and inspection of adjacent PR patches found no fix for this converged missing-event path. #57358 addresses sparse event encoding, not this omitted call; #54302 changes divergent-hit reconciliation, not the converged case. This PR deliberately does **not** solve sparse event encoding or change divergent-hit policy; it may need rebasing if #57358 changes the emitter's signature.

items.title: [KV offload] Add max_recompute_pending_tokens to skip waiting on short in-flight offloads
items.body:
## Purpose

When a KV offload lookup hits chunks whose GPU->CPU store is still in flight (`HIT_PENDING`), the scheduler always defers the request until the store completes, even if only a chunk or two are pending. Behind a backlog of serialized stores that wait can reach tens of seconds, which shows up as large `vllm:kv_offload_lookup_async_delay_seconds` observations. Recomputing a handful of tokens would have been far cheaper.

This PR adds a `kv_connector_extra_config` option, `max_recompute_pending_tokens`, that bounds the wait:

- If the run of chunks from the first pending chunk to the end of the hit would gain at most this many tokens (rounded down to whole chunks), the prefix lookup is cut before the first pending chunk. The request loads the ready prefix immediately and recomputes the rest.
- The partial-tail lookup applies the same budget.
- `RETRY` results still defer (the chunk's location is unknown), as do pending chunks inside a sliding-window group's required window.
- Negative values are rejected at spec construction.
- Default is `0`, which keeps the current always-wait behavior, so this is a no-op unless opted in.

The option is documented in `docs/features/kv_offloading_usage.md`.

### Not a duplicate

Searched open PRs for `HIT_PENDING offload recompute` and `max_recompute_pending_tokens`. The closest is #53087, which is complementary rather than overlapping: it adds a wall-clock deadline (`hit_pending_timeout_s`) inside `TieringOffloadingManager` for *stalled* primary-tier writes. This PR is a token-budget decision in the connector scheduler that applies to all offloading specs and avoids the wait up front when the pending run is small, rather than timing out after the fact.

## Test Plan

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector/test_scheduler.py -q
```

New tests:

- `test_recompute_budget_decides_whether_pending_chunks_are_awaited` (end-to-end through the request runner): with chunks `[HIT, HIT_PENDING, HIT]`, a budget covering the pending run loads the ready first chunk and records no async lookup delay; a smaller budget defers as before.
- `_maximal_prefix_lookup` unit cases: short pending run is cut before the first pending chunk, a run one chunk over budget defers, a leading pending chunk within budget is a miss, and `RETRY` defers regardless of budget.
- `test_negative_recompute_budget_is_rejected`.

## Test Result

```text
318 passed, 14 warnings in 106.53s (0:01:46)
```

No model eval or serving benchmark was run: the default (`0`) leaves lookup behavior unchanged, and with the option enabled the request only recomputes tokens it would otherwise have loaded, so outputs are unaffected.

---

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used to write this change.

items.title: [Bugfix][Core] Retain fine-grained EAGLE replay checkpoints
items.body:
With EAGLE, Mamba align mode, fine-grained prefix hits, and retention interval 0, scheduler-aligned replay retention can discard a materialized checkpoint that lookup could reuse. For a 95-token prompt with a 64-token Mamba/scheduler block and 16-token hashes, the old calculation selects 0 even though attention through 80 supports a 64-token hit after EAGLE drops 16 tokens.

Use one effective alignment in `get_replay_boundaries()`: the hash block size when partial hash hits are enabled, otherwise the scheduler block size. Compute the identical-resend and longer-sibling candidates with that alignment. The 95-token repeated-prompt hit changes from **0 to 64**, without internal checkpoint export.

This changes retention selection only. It does not change scheduler stops, checkpoint materialization, attention key publication, lookup, EAGLE-drop rules, or the retention configuration. Memory/performance impact is unbenchmarked.

## Known tradeoff

The single-alignment calculation does not retain additional scheduler-aligned fallback states. With a 160-token prompt, attention/Mamba blocks of 64, and hashes of 16, it selects 128 and 144. Attention registers keys at 64, 128, and the final partial tail at 160, but not 144. An identical resend is capped at 159, so attention matches 128 and EAGLE reduces that to 112. Neither selected Mamba checkpoint fits; the resend hit changes from **64 to 0**. A longer sibling still hits **144**.

The test retains this case and explicitly expects the lost fallback. Using one alignment does not repair the underlying attention-key/lookup limitation or preserve every previous hit.

## Scope and duplicate-work checks

Migrated from https://github.com/Dao007forever/vllm/pull/9, based on `e85c8826ce2a810367e8a70eedb987e31b140800`. This core retention change is independent of https://github.com/Dao007forever/vllm/pull/8, which publishes completed attention tails to Mooncake. Remote reuse also requires the attention data.

The original duplicate-work investigation checked open upstream/fork PRs for `get_replay_boundaries`, `mamba retention`, `fine-grained retention`, `replay boundary`, and `56615 in:body`. Related changes address separate mechanisms:

- #53802: scheduler/partial-tail checkpoint placement.
- #57180: lookup proof limits and Mamba partial-tail registration.
- #53803: grid/decode retention and state lifetimes.
- #56615: Mooncake publication.

Open upstream searches for `get_replay_boundaries` and `mamba retention` were refreshed for this update. The exact-function search returns this PR only; the scoped change remains the replay-retention alignment calculation.

## Validation

The existing partial-prefix-cache suite exercises the real scheduler split method and cache manager with internal checkpoint export disabled. Its seven cases cover FA, SWA, DCP, aligned/unaligned prompts, identical/extended requests, exact-boundary Mamba handoffs, and the documented 160-token limitation.

- Broader cache/scheduler suites: **294 passed, 4 failed**, including all seven updated replay cases passing. The four failures are `test_hisparse_async_admission_requires_only_import_destinations` parameterizations failing in `DeviceConfig` with `Failed to infer device type` on this macOS host, before the changed retention method runs. These match the failures previously reproduced with the original runtime.
- Changed-file pre-commit hooks, Python 3.12 mypy, and `git diff --check`: passed.
- GPU/model evaluation: **not run** on this host without CUDA/the vLLM accelerator extension. These tests validate cache bookkeeping and handoff metadata, not model tensor contents or generated output.

Commands (the cleanup opt-out avoids the unrelated PyTorch MPS allocator teardown assertion):

```bash
.venv/bin/python - <<'PY'
import pytest
class CpuTests:
    def pytest_collection_modifyitems(self, items):
        for item in items:
            item.add_marker(pytest.mark.skip_global_cleanup)
raise SystemExit(pytest.main([
    'tests/v1/core/prefix_cache',
    'tests/v1/core/test_prefix_caching.py',
    'tests/v1/core/test_single_type_kv_cache_manager.py',
    'tests/v1/core/test_mamba_align_chunk_split.py',
    '-q', '--tb=short',
], plugins=[CpuTests()]))
PY
.venv/bin/pre-commit run --files vllm/v1/core/kv_cache_coordinator.py tests/v1/core/prefix_cache/test_partial_prefix_cache_hits.py
.venv/bin/pre-commit run mypy-3.12 --hook-stage manual --files vllm/v1/core/kv_cache_coordinator.py tests/v1/core/prefix_cache/test_partial_prefix_cache_hits.py
git diff --check
```

items.title: [Feature] [KV Offload] Support sharing SimpleCPUOffload prefix caches across local DP replicas
items.body:
# [Feature] [KV Offload] Support sharing SimpleCPUOffload prefix caches across local DP replicas

## Summary

Implement #58240. `SimpleCPUOffloadConnector` currently keeps an independent CPU prefix cache
in each DP replica. When a request is routed to another local replica, that replica recomputes
a prefix even though a completed CPU copy is available. This change adds an opt-in
`cpu_offload_shared=true` mode that lets local DP replicas reuse completed CPU prefixes.

This builds on [#37160](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/37160), which
introduced `SimpleCPUOffloadConnector` and its private per-replica CPU cache.
This PR extends that connector with opt-in cross-DP publication and lookup; it
does not change the native offloader's per-replica semantics.

## Configuration

Add `cpu_offload_shared`, a JSON boolean in `kv_connector_extra_config`,
defaulting to `false`. Set it to `true` to share completed CPU prefixes with
compatible DP replicas in the same IPC namespace and distributed DP group.
Leaving it unset retains the existing private CPU pools.

The CPU capacity remains a per-worker budget: `cpu_bytes_to_use_per_rank`
reserves each worker's write partition. Corresponding local DP peers can read
published entries from one another's partitions, while writes remain owned by
the worker that allocates the slot. For example, two local DP peers configured
with 8 GiB each expose a 16 GiB node-local region for published slots and
metadata; this is shared visibility, not a dynamically rebalanced write pool.

Pass the following to `--kv-transfer-config`:

```json
{
  "kv_connector": "SimpleCPUOffloadConnector",
  "kv_role": "kv_both",
  "kv_connector_extra_config": {
    "cpu_offload_shared": true,
    "cpu_bytes_to_use_per_rank": 8589934592,
    "lazy_offload": false
  }
}
```

Shared mode requires the CPU backend, eager offloading (`lazy_offload=false`),
prefix caching, compatible model/KV layouts and reproducible prefix hashes.
It supports fixed MoE DP groups and TP, with `PP=DCP=PCP=1` and no LoRA or
elastic EP. Each TP coordinate shares its own KV shard with corresponding
local DP peers. Cross-node transfer requires a network-capable connector or tier.

## Implementation

Use the existing `SharedOffloadRegion` type, as established for native
`CPUOffloadingSpec` storage by
[#50094](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/50094), and the DMA/`BlockPool`
interfaces for storage and transfers; the cross-DP publication index, locking
and reader reference semantics are new code in this PR. Each writer owns a
fixed partition, and the shared pool does not dynamically move free write slots
between workers. Lookup and pinning use `flock` on the metadata region's descriptor;
prefixes are published after all worker stores complete, and reader references
prevent slot reuse until peer loads finish. The workers use the existing DMA
backend for transfers.

The rebased base also includes the upstream prefix-cacheable-group handling from
[#56810](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/56810). This PR consumes that
group eligibility behavior and adds cross-DP publication; it does not duplicate
the upstream hybrid-model bug fix.

| Production file | Change |
| --- | --- |
| `vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/simple_cpu_offload_connector.py` | Parse and validate `cpu_offload_shared`; connect worker and scheduler handshakes. |
| `vllm/v1/simple_kv_offload/shared_offload.py` (new) | Discover local DP peers, verify cache identity/layout, and allocate shared KV views per TP coordinate. |
| `vllm/v1/simple_kv_offload/shared_block_pool.py` (new) | Add shared hash publication, slot versions, locking and peer read references to `BlockPool`. |
| `vllm/v1/simple_kv_offload/metadata.py` | Define the worker-to-scheduler shared-pool handshake. |
| `vllm/v1/simple_kv_offload/manager.py` | Attach the shared pool and synchronize scheduler lookup, allocation and completion handling. |
| `vllm/v1/simple_kv_offload/worker.py` | Allocate/pin shared CPU views, expose the handshake and release mappings on shutdown. |

Tests and documentation changed:

- `tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_simple_cpu_offload_connector.py`
- `tests/v1/simple_kv_offload/test_scheduler.py`
- `tests/v1/simple_kv_offload/test_worker.py`
- `docs/features/kv_offloading_usage.md`

## Why this is not a duplicate

The following open PRs address adjacent behavior, but none adds cross-DP CPU
prefix publication and peer loading for `SimpleCPUOffloadConnector`:

- [#53073](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/53073) targets shared mmap
  startup ownership and cleanup. This PR targets completed-prefix visibility
  and safe peer reads after asynchronous DMA. It follows the mmap lifetime
  rules but adds a different metadata publication and reader-lifetime protocol.
- [#53474](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/53474) targets node-local
  sizing and worker placement for native `OffloadingConnector`. This PR targets
  node-local prefix reuse for `SimpleCPUOffloadConnector`, including one pool
  per TP coordinate. The connectors, allocation path and target behavior differ;
  this PR has no code dependency on #53474.
- [#47324](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/47324) targets a GPU
  load/compute stream race inside one worker. This PR targets host-side slot
  ownership when another worker reads a completed prefix. It does not implement
  the open PR's load-path stream-ordering fix; the two changes are complementary,
  and this PR adds separate cross-worker reader references.
- [#57418](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/57418) targets concurrent
  requests waiting for the same in-flight load inside one engine. This PR
  targets completed CPU prefixes shared by different DP engines; it does not
  change connector-side coalescing of simultaneous loads.
- [#43483](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/43483) targets routing a
  request to the DP rank that already owns a GPU prefix. This PR targets actual
  CPU KV publication and peer loading when routing selects another replica;
  routing-only ownership hints cannot provide that transfer.
- [#57422](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/57422) targets inode-safe
  unlinking of existing shared mmap files. This PR uses the existing mmap
  lifetime model but adds cross-DP prefix metadata and reader references.
- [#54743](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/54743) targets which KV
  groups receive offload configuration. This PR keeps the existing group
  eligibility rules and adds sharing only for groups already handled by
  `SimpleCPUOffloadConnector`.
- [#52921](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/52921) targets aligning
  scheduler and worker pool sizes across PP/speculative workers. This PR keeps
  the existing per-worker capacity calculation and adds node-local sharing
  after those capacities agree.

## Validation

Validation was run on `b9b640c09dd7ace867f84077902567c5625cad06`, based on
upstream `3e2a7e74a556623ddee3a327299d7bf04055501e`.
The current branch commit `c7756cf854aad81a6adb5d4c749886c96fb5b3d4` rebases
that version onto upstream `dd30786fef8b15bd83205833c7b3348b0ba0ebc7`;
conflict resolutions and a type-checking adjustment are limited to tests,
leaving this PR's implementation patch unchanged.

On the rebased source, the focused scheduler, KV-event and connector suite passed
**135 tests** on the DGX Spark CUDA environment:

```bash
HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 .venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/v1/simple_kv_offload/test_scheduler.py \
  tests/v1/simple_kv_offload/test_kv_events.py \
  tests/v1/simple_kv_offload/test_worker.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_simple_cpu_offload_metrics.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_simple_cpu_offload_connector.py -q
```

The suite includes shared scheduler publication, reader pinning, delayed
publication, metadata mismatch rejection, non-prefix-cacheable groups and the
TP configuration acceptance test. Ruff and the applicable pre-commit checks pass.

The model validation used two DGX Spark hosts, each with one NVIDIA GB10
(SM121), CUDA 13.2, driver 580.173.02, PyTorch 2.13.0+cu132 and
FlashInfer 0.6.18.post1. Because only two physical GPUs were available, the
model tests used a diagnostic topology with two logical workers per GPU. This
is functional evidence, not independent-GPU performance evidence; PyTorch
requires NCCL processes to have exclusive GPU access.

All TTFT and GSM8K results below use the TP2×DP2 topology described above.

For the TP2×DP2 diagnostic, the four logical workers were mapped as follows:

| Logical launch rank | DP | TP | Host | HTTP port |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | --- | --- |
| 0 | 0 | 0 | DGX Spark 1 | DP0 endpoint |
| 1 | 0 | 1 | DGX Spark 2 | Headless |
| 2 | 1 | 0 | DGX Spark 1 | DP1 endpoint |
| 3 | 1 | 1 | DGX Spark 2 | Headless |

The TP shard probe restored distinct TP0 and TP1 byte patterns through their
corresponding local DP groups and passed the all-shard publication barrier.
The full model run used DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731, DSpark K5 probabilistic
sampling, CUDA graphs, Rust frontend, RoCE and 2 GiB CPU/GPU KV capacity per
worker.

### Experiment setup

Use the same source commit and model weights for both modes. The launch below
shows the TP2×DP2 settings used for the TP shard and recovery probe. Run one
process for each logical launch rank in the table above: ranks 0 and 2 on the
first host, and ranks 1 and 3 on the second. Here `--nnodes 4` counts four logical
launches across two physical hosts; the DP size is 2.

Set `MODEL` to the
[DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731](https://huggingface.co/deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731)
weights, then set `NODE_RANK`, `DP_RANK`, `DP_PORT` and the coordinator ports and
address for the deployment. Use distinct HTTP ports for DP0 and DP1, one shared
DP RPC port, and one shared TP master port. Logical ranks 1 and 3 are headless.
The host-specific network environment is intentionally omitted.

```bash
KV_CONFIG='{"kv_connector":"SimpleCPUOffloadConnector","kv_role":"kv_both","kv_connector_extra_config":{"cpu_offload_shared":true,"cpu_bytes_to_use_per_rank":2147483648,"lazy_offload":false}}'

PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=expandable_segments:False \
.venv/bin/python -m vllm.entrypoints.cli.main serve "$MODEL" \
  --host 0.0.0.0 --port "$DP_PORT" \
  --data-parallel-size 2 --data-parallel-rank "$DP_RANK" \
  --data-parallel-external-lb \
  --data-parallel-address "$HEAD_IP" --data-parallel-rpc-port "$DP_RPC_PORT" \
  --tensor-parallel-size 2 --enable-expert-parallel --enable-ep-weight-filter \
  --nnodes 4 --node-rank "$NODE_RANK" \
  --master-addr "$HEAD_IP" --master-port "$TP_MASTER_PORT" \
  --distributed-executor-backend mp --disable-custom-all-reduce \
  --trust-remote-code --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v4 --reasoning-parser deepseek_v4 \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --block-size 256 --max-model-len 32768 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.47 --kv-cache-memory-bytes 2147483648 \
  --max-num-seqs 16 --max-num-batched-tokens 2048 \
  --max-cudagraph-capture-size 64 \
  --compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mode":"FULL_AND_PIECEWISE","custom_ops":["all"]}' \
  --kernel-config '{"enable_flashinfer_autotune":false}' \
  --enable-prefix-caching --prefix-caching-hash-algo sha256 \
  --enable-prompt-tokens-details --per-request-spec-decode-metrics detailed \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"dspark","num_speculative_tokens":5,"draft_sample_method":"probabilistic"}' \
  --kv-transfer-config "$KV_CONFIG"
```

Add `--headless` for logical ranks 1 and 3. For the private control, change only
`cpu_offload_shared` to `false`. Keep `expandable_segments:False` in both
connector runs because the upstream KV-connector guard rejects
`expandable_segments:True`.

External DP routing gives one configured endpoint port to DP0 and another to DP1
on the coordinator host; the TP followers are headless. Send case `i` to DP rank
`i % 2` for the cold phase and to `1 - (i % 2)` for the peer phase, preserving
the prompt and `cache_salt`. The port selects the replica; it is not part of the
prefix hash.
Between phases, wait for requests and stores to finish, then POST to
`/reset_prefix_cache?reset_external=true` on both endpoints for a cold run, or
`/reset_prefix_cache?reset_external=false` to clear only GPU caches before peer
replay. Check that both resets succeed before issuing requests. Confirm reuse
with the external CPU-prefix counters.

### Offload correctness and latency

The GPU DMA tests and TP2 shard probe restored distinct TP0/TP1 byte patterns
after peer loads and withheld publication until all TP workers completed their
stores.

#### Performance improvement test

The rebased-source one-shot test used 24 unique approximately 6K-token prefixes,
one in-flight request per endpoint and streaming `max_tokens=1` requests. Each
prefix was populated on its owner, GPU caches were reset, and the prefix was
requested exactly once from its local DP peer.

| Mode | Peer TTFT p50 | Peer TTFT p95 | External transfer | Local compute |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Private | 9.17 s | 12.22 s | 0 / 140,652 | 140,652 |
| Shared | 4.91 s | 9.29 s | 129,024 / 140,652 | 11,628 |

Shared peer TTFT was 46.4% lower in this rebased-source diagnostic run. All 24
peer requests had zero errors, empty outputs, replacement characters,
invalid controls or cold/peer output mismatches. This is a diagnostic result;
the topology with two logical workers per GB10 is not a production throughput
setup.

### Accuracy validation

The rebased-source GSM8K evaluation used three fresh cold/peer pairs with the
same 200 five-shot questions, `temperature=0`, `seed=0`, concurrency 32 and a
512-token output limit:

| Configuration | Round 1 | Round 2 | Round 3 | Mean | Min–max | DSpark acceptance |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Private cold | 189 | 189 | 189 | 94.50% | 94.50–94.50% | 64.10% |
| Private peer | 191 | 189 | 190 | 95.00% | 94.50–95.50% | 64.20% |
| Shared cold | 188 | 189 | 189 | 94.33% | 94.00–94.50% | 63.94% |
| Shared peer | 190 | 190 | 189 | 94.83% | 94.50–95.00% | 64.60% |

All 2,400 requests completed without request errors, empty output, replacement
characters or invalid control characters. These repeated evaluations show normal
serving-workload variation and are not a statistical equivalence claim. The
TP2×DP2 recovery probe separately passed 8/8 cold and 8/8 peer requests in both
modes with token-exact output; private peer CPU hits were 0 and shared peer CPU
hits were 45,056 tokens. The independent TP-shard/publication probe also passed.

## AI assistance

The implementation and analysis were assisted with AI and reviewed by human.

items.title: [Bugfix] Bound prefix cache reuse by the first requested prompt score
items.body:
## Overview

When `prompt_logprob_token_ids` is combined with explicit `skip_reading_prefix_cache=False`, limit local prefix reuse to rows before `prompt_logprob_start`. Otherwise a cache hit can skip rows whose scores were requested.

## Claims

Preserve all requested scores while allowing cached, unscored prefix rows to be reused. The default behavior still skips prefix reads for prompt scoring.

## Validation

386 regression tests and full manual pre-commit passed. Real Qwen3-0.6B scoring reproduced missing rows on main; the candidate returned all requested rows with cache-on/cache-off scores matching.

<details>
<summary>Reproduction: environment, complete script and before/after results</summary>

On main `ab905a885d`, real Qwen3-0.6B/MMLU scoring reproduced:

```text
AssertionError: Missing scores: skip_cache=False, cached=32, first_scored_row=27
```

With candidate `6344014bb8`, 32 requests containing 184 scored rows matched exactly across eight cache-on/cache-off runs in batch-invariant mode. They also matched main with cache reads disabled. Qwen3-0.6B revision: `c1899de289a04d12100db370d81485cdf75e47ca`; dataset: `cais/mmlu`, revision `c30699e8356da336a370243923dbaf21066bb9fe`, first eight high_school_biology/test questions and all four options. Hardware: RTX 5090; PyTorch 2.13.0+cu130. This checks score completeness and consistency, not MMLU accuracy.

A separate default compiled/CUDA graph run passed start offsets 0, 31, 32 and 33, with 0, 16, 32 and 32 cached tokens respectively. The cached scores matched uncached scores at the existing numerical tolerances.

386 tests and full manual pre-commit passed:

```bash
python -m pytest tests/v1/core/test_prefix_caching.py tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py -q
pre-commit run --hook-stage manual --files vllm/sampling_params.py vllm/v1/request.py vllm/v1/core/kv_cache_manager.py vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py tests/v1/core/test_prefix_caching.py tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py
```

Save the script below as `reproduce.py` outside the checkout. Use an installed build of the selected vLLM revision with `numpy`, `transformers`, `pyarrow` and `huggingface_hub` available. Download the pinned MMLU input beside the script:

```python
from huggingface_hub import hf_hub_download
import shutil
revision = "c30699e8356da336a370243923dbaf21066bb9fe"
shutil.copyfile(hf_hub_download(
    "cais/mmlu", "high_school_biology/test-00000-of-00001.parquet",
    repo_type="dataset", revision=revision,
), "mmlu.parquet")
```

Run the same script from that directory against baseline `ab905a885dfbfc60a2c02286cc9c608c93884de3`, then against the candidate with this patch applied:

```bash
VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1 python reproduce.py result.json
```

The model resolves to the pinned public revision in the script. The validation used local cached copies of those same model and dataset revisions.

```python
import argparse
import atexit
import json
import time
from pathlib import Path

import numpy as np
from transformers import AutoTokenizer

from vllm import LLM, SamplingParams, TokensPrompt


def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    parser.add_argument("output", type=Path)
    args = parser.parse_args()
    import pyarrow.parquet as pq
    model = "Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B"
    revision = "c1899de289a04d12100db370d81485cdf75e47ca"
    data = pq.read_table(Path(__file__).with_name("mmlu.parquet")).slice(0, 8).to_pylist()
    tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(model, revision=revision)
    prompts, starts = [], []
    for row in data:
        context = tokenizer.encode("Question: " + row["question"] + "\nAnswer:", add_special_tokens=False)
        for option in row["choices"]:
            suffix = tokenizer.encode(" " + option, add_special_tokens=False)
            ids = (context + suffix)[-4095:]
            prompts.append(TokensPrompt(prompt_token_ids=ids))
            starts.append(len(ids) - len(suffix) - 1)
    assert len(prompts) == 32 and min(starts) >= 0
    llm = LLM(
        model=model, revision=revision, dtype="bfloat16", max_model_len=4096,
        max_num_seqs=128, max_num_batched_tokens=8192,
        gpu_memory_utilization=0.65, enforce_eager=True, seed=233,
    )
    atexit.register(llm.llm_engine.engine_core.shutdown, timeout=30)
    arms = []
    # The first pair warms scorer kernels; retain three further pairs for timing.
    for skip in [True, False] * 4:
        assert llm.reset_prefix_cache()
        llm.generate(prompts, SamplingParams(temperature=0, max_tokens=1), use_tqdm=False)
        params = [
            SamplingParams(
                temperature=0, max_tokens=1, prompt_logprob_start=start,
                prompt_logprob_token_ids=[[token] for token in p["prompt_token_ids"][start + 1:]],
                skip_reading_prefix_cache=skip,
            )
            for p, start in zip(prompts, starts)
        ]
        begin = time.perf_counter()
        outputs = llm.generate(prompts, params, use_tqdm=False)
        elapsed = time.perf_counter() - begin
        rows = []
        for output, p, start in zip(outputs, prompts, starts):
            scores = output.prompt_token_id_logprobs
            assert scores is not None, (
                f"Missing scores: skip_cache={skip}, cached={output.num_cached_tokens}, "
                f"first_scored_row={start}"
            )
            assert scores.shape == (len(p["prompt_token_ids"]) - start - 1, 1)
            assert 0 <= (output.num_cached_tokens or 0) <= start
            rows.append({"scores": scores.tolist(), "cached_tokens": output.num_cached_tokens})
        arms.append({"skip_cache": skip, "elapsed_s": elapsed, "rows": rows})
        args.output.write_text(json.dumps({"prompts": prompts, "starts": starts, "arms": arms}))
        print("ARM", len(arms), skip, elapsed, sum(r["cached_tokens"] or 0 for r in rows), flush=True)
    for arm in arms[1:]:
        for reference, actual in zip(arms[0]["rows"], arm["rows"]):
            np.testing.assert_allclose(actual["scores"], reference["scores"], atol=1e-2, rtol=1e-3)
    assert any(r["cached_tokens"] for r in arms[1]["rows"])
    print("INTERVAL_OK", flush=True)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
```

Candidate success marker (excerpt from the original log):

```text
INTERVAL_OK
```

The MMLU run and 386-test regression run validated the final candidate `6344014bb8`. The separate compiled boundary run validated the same product code before repository tests were simplified.

</details>

## Details

The request provides the maximum reusable prefix length to both local cache lookup paths. The first scored causal row is still recomputed. Full prompt logprobs disable this reuse, and external KV loads are suppressed because connectors cannot bound a load at the first scored row.

SGLang uses the same principle: [`Req._compute_max_prefix_len`](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/51686cf8e7fee0ae773c5c9b8ede356507abef7b/python/sglang/srt/managers/schedule_batch.py#L1666-L1677) caps prefix reuse at `logprob_start_len` when prompt logprobs are requested. This provides a reference for the cache boundary used here.

Repository tests cover cache boundaries and synchronous/asynchronous connector behavior. Model scoring and compiled execution remain separate validation evidence. No new configuration or default change is introduced.
