items.title: [Bugfix][KV Connector] Serve and store OffloadingConnector partial tails with EAGLE/MTP groups
items.body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

**Problem.** With an EAGLE/MTP draft model and `mamba_cache_mode="align"`, the native CPU `OffloadingConnector` never serves a partial tail. So every hit from the CPU tier stops at a scheduler-block boundary, and the tokens after it are computed again.

**Fix, in three parts:**
1. **Lookup:** look up the tail at the EAGLE proof position, as Mooncake does since #60695.
2. **Store:** fix the store gate. Before, it always skipped the one step that can store the tail.
3. **Store policy:** store an EAGLE tail only for a request that loaded from the CPU tier. Without this, parts 1 and 2 double the GPU → CPU traffic, and serving gets slower (P95 TTFT 13 % higher without it in a same-day control, see Validation).

**Result** (8 × A100, MLPerf agentic, 3 × 60 min per arm): no serving regression; SLO pass 92.42 % against 91.70 % without this PR. The CPU-tier hits now end at partial tails, as designed.

Related: #60533 (core proof), #52832 (producer partial tails), #54165 (a different bug in the same file).

## Claims

- With an EAGLE group and align Mamba, a CPU-tier hit can now end at `prefix_match_unit` granularity, as a GPU prefix-cache hit already does. Before, it ended at a whole scheduler block, minus one more block for the EAGLE pop.
- The EAGLE group's tail is keyed at `boundary + eagle_proof_margin`, the same proof that core uses since #60533. Mamba groups and non-EAGLE groups stay keyed at the boundary.
- The tail is stored on the step that computes the proof.
- With an EAGLE group, only a request that loaded from the CPU tier stores its partial tail.
- No change without an EAGLE group, or where partial tails are not supported (DCP > 1, `blocks_per_chunk > 1`, mixed block sizes, sliding-window groups). No new config option.

## Validation

### Serving A/B

**Setup.** Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-FP8 (36 GDN + 12 full-attention layers + 1 MTP layer), TP8 + EP on 8 × A100-SXM4-40GB, MTP 3, scheduler block 800 tokens, `prefix_match_unit` 16, `--kv-offloading-backend native --kv-offloading-size 256`. MLPerf agentic multi-turn workload, 20 concurrent sessions, 3 × 60 min per arm, same node type.

**SLO** (Artificial Analysis percentile convention): **P95 TTFT ≤ 2.93 s** and **P95 TPOT ≤ 21.74 ms** (that is, P5 output speed ≥ 46 tokens/s). "SLO pass" below is the share of requests that meet both limits. The SLO holds when SLO pass ≥ 95 %.

| Arm | SLO pass, run 1 / 2 / 3 | Mean | Goodput | CPU → GPU load (whole run) | GPU prefix hit |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Without this PR | 92.01 / 90.92 / 92.18 % | 91.70 % | 1.866 req/s | — | — |
| Parts 1 + 2 only (tail stored on every turn) | 85.2 / 87.3 / 87.2 % | 86.6 % | 1.67–1.72 req/s | 19.9 TB | 79.0 % |
| **This PR** (parts 1 + 2 + 3) | 93.49 / 91.93 / 91.84 % | **92.42 %** | **1.922 req/s** | **16.0 TB** | **85.2 %** |

The gain of this PR over "without" (+0.7 points, +3 % goodput) is within about two repeat spreads. So I claim no regression, not a speed-up. The "This PR" arm ran a backport on vLLM 81198e97 with the store policy behind an opt-in flag. On this model every partial tail is an EAGLE tail, so that flag gives the same rule as this PR's default.

**Same-day control (15 Oct, one node, 1 × 60 min per arm, same setup).** The "parts 1 + 2 only" arm above ran on another day; on the same day and node as this PR the gap is smaller:

| Store rule | GPU → CPU store per request | Requests done | Output tok/s per GPU | TTFT P50 / P95 | TPOT P50 / P95 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Parts 1 + 2 only (no store gate) | 247 MB | 7,450 | 111.7 | 949 / 2,297 ms | 14.07 / 23.41 ms |
| Store gate `num_locally_computed_tokens >= boundary` (review suggestion) | 247 MB | 7,490 | 111.6 | 935 / 2,203 ms | 14.16 / 23.07 ms |
| **This PR** (store only after a load from the CPU tier) | **126 MB** | **7,721** | **113.6** | 924 / **2,025 ms** | **13.69 / 22.56 ms** |

Part 3 halves the stores and, against no gate, lowers P95 TTFT by 12 % and P95 TPOT by 4 % (one run per arm). The "−5 points" of the 3 × 60 table is not reproduced on a single day; treat it as an upper bound. The review-suggested gate rarely applies here: the stored tail is past the request's GPU prefix hit.

<details>
<summary>Why parts 1 + 2 alone are slower (earlier A/B)</summary>

| Measure | Without this PR | Parts 1 + 2 only |
|---|---|---|
| CPU-tier hit tokens mod 800 | 0 in all snapshots | not 0 (e.g. 224): partial tails are served |
| SLO pass, run 1 / 2 / 3 | 90.0 / 89.2 / 89.5 % | 75.1 / 79.3 / 79.9 % |
| Goodput | 1.83–1.89 req/s | 1.31–1.43 req/s |
| P95 / P99 TTFT | 2.22–2.35 / 3.13–3.58 s | 2.94–4.18 / 5.5–13.9 s |
| P50 / P95 TPOT | 14.1–14.3 / 23.9–24.5 ms | 15.7–16.4 / 29.0–34.0 ms |
| MTP mean acceptance length | 2.676 | 2.676 |
| GPU → CPU store bytes / time | 3.00 TB / 3,814 s | 6.93 TB / 8,196 s |
| Scheduler lookup time (sum) | 1.3 s | 8.4 s |

The tails work: they are stored, found and loaded, and the drafter is unchanged. But each turn stores one new tail block (800 tokens, about 6 MB) in every KV group. Most requests hit the GPU prefix cache on the next turn, so most of these stores are never read. Tail stores were 18,650 (about one per request) and 64.5 % of the 6.93 TB stored. Part 3 removes these stores.

How the bug was found: without this PR, `vllm:external_prefix_cache_hits_total` was an exact multiple of 800 in all 17 snapshots of two 3-hour runs (example: 402,580,800 = 503,226 × 800). With part 1 only, it was still a multiple of 800. That pointed to the store gate.

</details>

### Unit tests

All in `tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector/test_scheduler.py`:

| What | Tests |
|---|---|
| Proof key: store and lookup | `test_eagle_proof_margin_follows_core_hit_alignment`, `test_eagle_partial_tail_store_keys_attention_at_proof`, `test_eagle_partial_lookup_loads_attention_proof` |
| Store gate (part 2): round trip | `test_eagle_partial_tail_round_trip_serves_mamba_checkpoint[True]`: fails with part 1 only, passes with part 2 |
| Store only when the proof is in the prompt | `test_eagle_partial_tail_store_needs_proof_in_prompt` (5 cases) |
| Popped chunk looked up once | `test_eagle_partial_lookup_probes_popped_chunk_once` (6 lookups instead of 7; 7 instead of 9) |
| Store policy (part 3) | `test_eagle_partial_tail_store_needs_offload_load` ([False] and [True] cases) |

| Run | Result |
|---|---|
| A100 (CUDA), nightly 5555a2d8 image, whole `offloading_connector/` | 589 passed, 0 failed. With #61375 also applied: 590 passed. |
| macOS (CPU), whole `offloading_connector/` | 476 passed. The same 105 failures occur with and without this PR; they are macOS platform errors (`Hybrid KV cache manager ... not supported`, `Invalid device string: ':0'`). |
| `ruff check`, `ruff format --check` (ruff 0.14.0) | clean |

```bash
python -m pytest -q tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector/
```

This PR and #61375 (a different bug in `offloading/scheduler.py`) merge without conflicts.

## Details

**Root cause 1: lookup.** `SchedulerOffloadConfig.from_spec` set `supports_partial_tail = False` when any group was an EAGLE group. For an EAGLE group, the complete-chunk lookup asks for one extra chunk and then drops it. So the hit ended one scheduler block before the last stored chunk, and no partial tail was tried.

**Root cause 2: store gate.**
1. With EAGLE block drop, core stops the prefill at the Mamba checkpoint T = floor(P/h)·h − h.
2. On the next step (tokens T..P), the state is copied (CoW), and the manager hands `(group, cow_block, T)` to the connector one time.
3. The scheduler builds the connector metadata before `_update_after_schedule`, so `num_computed_tokens == T` at that point.
4. So the gate `boundary + margin > num_computed_tokens` reads `T + h > T`. This is always true, so the store is always skipped, and the hand-off does not come again.

**Changes.**
- Remove the EAGLE exclusion from `supports_partial_tail`.
- Key the EAGLE non-recurrent groups at `boundary + margin` in store, lookup and load.
- Margin rule as in core: one hash unit if `cache_hit_alignment_tokens` < block and the group manager supports fine-grained lookup; else one block.
- Widen the partial search by one block, with bridge keys for the dropped chunk. That chunk is looked up once per lookup; a miss skips that block.
- Check the proof against `min(num_computed_tokens + num_scheduled_tokens[req_id], num_prompt_tokens)`. The cap keeps the proof out of speculative tokens.
- With an EAGLE group, store a partial tail only if `update_state_after_alloc` scheduled a CPU-tier load for this request (`RequestOffloadState.loaded_from_offload`). Complete chunks and aligned boundary states are stored as before.

**Why the proof-step store is safe.** Stores are only queued in `wait_for_save` and are sent at the start of the next step. The CPU transfer stream waits on the compute stream at that point, so the copy runs after this step's forward wrote the proof block.

**Difference from #60695.** Mooncake stores one key per hash unit. The native connector stores whole chunks and keeps its chunk-level EAGLE drop for complete chunks. So only the partial-tail key of EAGLE groups changes.

**Limitations.**
- If the hand-off step stops before `T + h`, the tail is not stored. I ran core's chunk-split code on 20,000 prompts (1k–200k tokens) per configuration. No hand-off was lost when block ≤ `max_num_batched_tokens` with EAGLE or single-module MTP. Losses occur only with multi-module MTP (0.2–0.45 %) or with a block larger than the token budget (≤ 1.7 %). A fix would need core to keep the CoW block across steps; not done.
- The store policy is a heuristic. A request served only from the GPU prefix cache stores no EAGLE tail. If the GPU later evicts that prefix, the next turn's CPU-tier hit ends at the last complete chunk. That turn then loads from the CPU tier and stores its tail, so the turn after it can get a partial hit. Measured on one workload only.
- When the dropped chunk is present, the search covers two blocks. This applies only with an EAGLE group.
- Existing CPU caches hold no EAGLE tails, so no migration is needed.

**Size:** `offloading/scheduler.py` +170 / −34 (no core files changed); tests +348 / −1.

items.title: [Metrics] Report shared-prefix tokens lost to a missing sparse-retention checkpoint
items.body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Adds a counter and startup message that explain when a hybrid model loses prefix-cache reuse because a Mamba or sliding-window group has no usable saved state. This helps operators understand why repeated prompts still need processing. Relates to #45238.

## Claims

- Reports shared-prefix tokens lost to missing sparse state through `vllm:prefix_cache_sparse_retention_misses`.
- Fixes attribution: dense-cache eviction and EAGLE's required replay/alignment are excluded from this counter.
- Explains at startup when zero retention keeps only selected checkpoints. Cache-hit decisions and model computation are unchanged.

## Validation

Rebased onto main `8fb16ea5a66f0ef362e728f0ff025f2845927fd5`; validated source head `065a6406df1af9bc9ace987c7b98914096e7ffe8` on WSL2/Ubuntu, uv-managed Python 3.12, PyTorch 2.13.0+cu130 and one RTX 4080 Laptop GPU (12 GB), using the existing precompiled vLLM artifacts.

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/core/test_prefix_caching.py \
  tests/v1/core/prefix_cache/ tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_utils.py \
  tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py -q

.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/core/test_prefix_caching.py \
  tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py -q \
  -k 'sparse_retention_miss or zero_retention_is_announced'

mapfile -t changed_files < <(git diff --name-only 8fb16ea5a6 HEAD)
pre-commit run --files "${changed_files[@]}"
pre-commit run mypy-3.12 --hook-stage manual --files "${changed_files[@]}"
```

- **672 passed, 4 failed, 2 setup errors** in the broader suite. All six failures/errors reproduce on unchanged main at `8fb16ea5a6`: four require 2–4 GPUs, and two serving fixtures reject this machine's available GPU memory at their default 0.92 memory utilization. No PR-specific failure was found.
- **11 focused tests passed**, including admission-time accounting, startup logging and all seven new attribution cases. The new cases cover dense eviction, EAGLE replay, mixed dense/Mamba losses, and sliding-window EAGLE with equal and unequal block sizes; they also check the existing hit lengths and retention boundaries.
- **Negative control: all seven new cases fail** when the original boundary-subtraction counting method is restored.
- All PR-file pre-commit checks and the manual Python 3.12 mypy hook pass.
- **Fresh GPU end-to-end check passed** on `Qwen/Qwen3.5-0.8B`, default Model Runner V2, Mamba align mode and retention 0. Three sequential 2,176-token requests share 1,088 tokens, with different tails. The engine chooses 544-token blocks:

| Request | Prefix hits (tokens) | Sparse-retention misses (tokens) |
|---|---:|---:|
| Cold seed | 0 | 0 |
| Shared prefix, checkpoint missing | 0 | 1,088 |
| Shared prefix, learned checkpoint reused | 1,088 | 0 |

Each request generated one token successfully. This validates the live counter and recovery path; it is not a model-quality evaluation or throughput claim. Hosted CI still requires maintainer authorization.

<details>
<summary>Fresh GPU reproduction</summary>

Use the model revision `2fc06364715b967f1860aea9cf38778875588b17`. With the rebased source installed, run through `.venv/bin/python`:

```python
from vllm import LLM, SamplingParams

if __name__ == "__main__":
    llm = LLM(
        model="Qwen/Qwen3.5-0.8B",
        revision="2fc06364715b967f1860aea9cf38778875588b17",
        enable_prefix_caching=True,
        mamba_cache_mode="align",
        enforce_eager=True,
        language_model_only=True,
        disable_log_stats=False,
        max_model_len=8192,
        max_num_seqs=1,
        max_num_batched_tokens=2048,
        kv_cache_memory_bytes=1024 * 1024 * 1024,
        gpu_memory_utilization=0.7,
        seed=0,
    )
    params = SamplingParams(temperature=0, max_tokens=1, ignore_eos=True)
    for tail in (52, 53, 54):
        tokens = [17] * 1088 + [tail] * 1088
        llm.generate([{"prompt_token_ids": tokens}], params, use_tqdm=False)
        print([
            (m.name, m.value)
            for m in llm.get_metrics()
            if m.name in (
                "vllm:prefix_cache_queries",
                "vllm:prefix_cache_hits",
                "vllm:prefix_cache_sparse_retention_misses",
            )
        ])
```

Read per-request deltas from those cumulative counters. The startup log also confirms retention 0 and the 544-token scheduler block size.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Hardware-limited tests, verified on unchanged main</summary>

```text
test_get_kv_cache_config_mamba_hybrid_sharing_pp_group_count_bump
test_get_kv_cache_config_mamba_hybrid_sharing_pp_starved_stage
test_async_scheduling_pp_allows_rescheduling_with_output_placeholders
test_diffusion_read_deferral_keeps_a_longer_pp_wait
test_prefix_cache_hit_rate[base]
test_prefix_cache_hit_rate[mtp]
```

The serving fixtures report 10.78 GiB free versus 11.03 GiB requested. The fresh GPU reproduction above uses a smaller memory budget and runs successfully without changing production code or weakening the fixtures.

</details>

## Details

The original counter subtracted the final hit from the shared-prefix retention boundary. That boundary can also include tokens lost to dense eviction or EAGLE replay, so it could incorrectly blame sparse retention. The coordinator now records reductions made by sparse groups during the existing lookup. Sliding-window diagnostics separate intentional EAGLE costs using the same cache queries, and the request carries the result to admission-time statistics.

The existing boundary still controls checkpoint retention. This change adds no cache lookups, changes no hit decisions and adds no GPU synchronization.

Issue and open PR searches for #45238, the metric name and sparse retention found no other open PR exposing this counter. Related PRs such as #50551, #53479, #57613 and #58549 change checkpoint retention or materialization; this PR reports missing-state losses. The startup message from the closed #53596 is consolidated here, with @jschmied's authorship preserved through the rebase.

<details>
<summary>Earlier author validation and serving measurements (before this rebase)</summary>

## Test plan

```bash
uv venv --python 3.12
VLLM_USE_PRECOMPILED=1 uv pip install -e . --torch-backend=auto

.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/core/test_prefix_caching.py \
  tests/v1/core/prefix_cache/ tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_utils.py \
  tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py -q

pre-commit run --files vllm/v1/metrics/stats.py vllm/v1/metrics/loggers.py \
  vllm/v1/core/kv_cache_manager.py tests/v1/core/test_prefix_caching.py \
  tests/entrypoints/serve/instrumentator/test_metrics.py docs/design/metrics.md
```

## Test result

`348 passed, 1 failed`. The single failure is `test_async_scheduling_pp_allows_rescheduling_with_output_placeholders`, which fails identically on the unmodified base commit (`4d2a68d64`) — verified by checking out the base and running it in isolation. It is unrelated to this change.

All `pre-commit` hooks pass, including `mypy`.

Two unit tests are added to `tests/v1/core/test_prefix_caching.py`: one asserting the counter reports the lost tokens when an align-mode Mamba group holds no checkpoint at the shared-prefix junction, and one asserting it stays at zero on a hit every group agrees on. As a negative control, stubbing the computation to `0` makes the first test fail (expected 32, got 0), confirming it exercises the new path rather than passing vacuously.

The consolidated commit from #53596 adds a third test, `test_zero_retention_is_announced_on_sparse_models`, covering the startup log line; it passes on this branch together with the existing zero-retention tests (`.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/core/test_prefix_caching.py -k 'zero_retention or sparse_retention or reachable_block_mask or junction'` → 10 passed).

The admission test, `test_sparse_retention_miss_recorded_at_admission` in `tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py`, drives a vetoed lookup through `schedule()` and reads the counter back from `make_stats()`. The updated implementation stores the loss diagnostic on the request during lookup and records it at admission. The existing shared-prefix boundary assertion still guards the retention boundary; that boundary is no longer used to derive this metric.

### End to end

`Qwen3.5-4B` (AWQ 4-bit), single GPU, `--enable-prefix-caching --enforce-eager`, `--max-model-len 8192`, concurrency 1, 32 prompts over 8 prefix groups. Engine selected `mamba_cache_mode="align"` and `block_size=528`, matching the geometry in #45238. Workloads are `vllm bench serve --dataset-name prefix_repetition`, differing only in where the 1584-token block boundary falls:

| | 1600 / 600 (boundary inside shared prefix) | 1500 / 700 (boundary in unique tokens) |
|---|---|---|
| `prefix_cache_queries` | 70,400 | 70,400 |
| `prefix_cache_hits` | 38,016 (54.0%) | 17,952 (25.5%) |
| **`prefix_cache_sparse_retention_misses`** | **0** | **8,448** |
| Mean TTFT | 245.95 ms | 300.25 ms |

The counter stays at exactly zero on the healthy workload and reports 8,448 tokens (16 × 528, whole blocks) on the geometry-unlucky one, alongside a halved hit rate and a 22% TTFT regression that is otherwise unattributable.

Note the unlucky case is 25.5%, not 0% — the Marconi admission policy (#37898) recovers most of it. The original 0% case from #45238 was not reproduced in that tested main build; the measurements above show the residual loss this counter is intended to expose.

Independent reproduction: @jschmied traced the same found-then-discarded pattern live on a GB10 (https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/52527#issuecomment-5398286287) — Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4 hybrid GDN, MTP, block size 1,600, measured at the default `prefix_cache_retention_interval=0`. The default cost one extra cold prefill per fresh prefix on unaligned prompts there (first hit on request 3 rather than 2), with hit amounts unchanged once warm.

## Model evaluation

No model-quality evaluation was run: this change adds statistics and a startup log without changing cache-hit decisions or model computation. The serving measurements above validate the intended metric behavior on the tested workloads.

</details>

items.title: [Bugfix][KV Offload] Don't pop a verified full-attn eagle prefix chunk
items.body:
## Purpose

Fixes `OffloadingConnector` storing CPU KV but serving **0** hits when the eagle group is **full-attention** (prefix scan). The lookup pops one chunk from every unverified eagle group:

```python
if is_eagle_unverified:
    num_hit_chunks -= 1
```

The compensating over-query (`query_max += tokens_per_chunk`) is **SWA-only**. Full-attn eagle never over-queries, so the pop removes a *matched* prompt chunk. With a stored prefix of ≤ 1 chunk, `new_num_hit_tokens < tokens_per_chunk` then `return 0` aborts the **whole** request. `GPU_to_CPU` grows; `CPU_to_GPU` stays 0.

`offload_prompt_only` (default True) plus the store-side decode drop already omit the volatile full-attn tail. There is no extra chunk on the prefix path for the pop to eat.

## Fix

Gate the decrement on the same condition as the over-query:

```python
if is_eagle_unverified:
    if sliding_window_size_in_chunks is not None:
        num_hit_chunks -= 1
    eagle_verified.add(group_idx)
```

SWA eagle is unchanged (over-query + pop). Full-attn eagle keeps the verified prefix.

## Not a duplicate of #52771

[#52771](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/52771) is the right fix for **unannotated shared-group MTP** (Qwen3.5/3.8: mark-every-group fallback + finish-time store hole). Its lookup hunk **widens every eagle group and keeps the pop**.

That does not cover this bug:

1. Widen is capped by `len(offload_keys)`. A 1-chunk stored FA prefix has no second key, so the extra query is a no-op and the pop still goes 1 → 0.
2. [#52669](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/52669) / [#52674](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/52674) already tried widen-only on this path and were closed; they did not restore reads.
3. #52771 explicitly treats DSpark draft-group AND-poison ([#47891](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/47891) / [#48459](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/48459)) as a different mechanism. This PR is the **annotated full-attn eagle pop** on that DSpark path, not the shared-group MTP fallback.

[#52807](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/52807) originally dropped this pop (same polarity), then deferred the eagle half to #52771. This PR restores the SWA-only pop for the 1-chunk FA case widen cannot save.

If #52771 lands first, this rebases to: **only pop when the query was actually widened**. Composing the other way (widen FA *and* skip the pop) would keep a volatile extra chunk; we are not proposing that.

[#52047](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/52047) (draft-group annotation) is already on `main` and is not this pop.

## Test Plan

`tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector/test_scheduler.py`:

- full-attn eagle 3 hits stay 12 (no pop)
- full-attn eagle 1 hit stays 4 (the veto case; this is the 1-chunk prefix #52771's widen cannot save)
- existing SWA pop tests unchanged

`VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector/test_scheduler.py`

Production: Kimi-K3 DSpark + `SimpleCPUOffloadConnector`. Before: CPU→GPU = 0. After: c16 CPU hit ~60% under the same recipe.

items.title: [Bugfix][KV Events] Emit BlockRemoved only for the last cached copy of a block hash
items.body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Emit `BlockRemoved` only when the last physical copy of a prefix-cache hash disappears. This keeps KV-event consumers from discarding a prefix that the engine still caches.

## Claims

- Evicting one of several copies leaves the external hash resident until the final copy disappears.
- The guard applies to eviction and partial-prefix replacement or promotion through the shared event emitter.
- The change preserves the event schema, cache-group isolation, `BlockStored` behavior, and the internal `pop` contract.

## Validation

The existing eviction test checks that the first duplicate removal emits no event and the final removal emits the expected hash. It also checks single-copy removals.

```bash
.venv/bin/python3 -m pytest tests/v1/core/test_prefix_caching.py \
  -k 'maybe_evict_cached_block or kv_cache_events' -q --confcutdir=tests/v1/core
.venv/bin/python3 -m pytest tests/distributed/test_kv_cache_events.py \
  -q --confcutdir=tests/distributed
.venv/bin/pre-commit run --files \
  tests/v1/core/test_prefix_caching.py vllm/v1/core/block_pool.py
```

The refreshed branch passes the selected eviction/event tests (7 passed, 158 deselected) and event-schema tests (17 passed). The repository pre-commit hooks pass on both changed files.

End-to-end serving validation is pending for this revision. The unit commands exclude the root `tests/conftest.py` because the available environment lacks `tblib`. The regression already runs in the Buildkite CPU job.

## Details

vLLM can keep several physical blocks for the same prefix hash. On current `main`, removing any copy emits `BlockRemoved`, even while another copy remains available. A router that treats this event as hash eviction can underestimate the engine's cached prefix and choose another engine. This PR makes no throughput or latency claim.

The shared emitter checks the existing hash map after removal. The key includes the cache group, so another group's copy cannot suppress an event. Event-disabled execution returns before the added lookup. Event-enabled removal adds one dictionary lookup per removed hash. Hash relocation remains event-free. Both model runners use this scheduler-side cache pool, so a separate MRV2 change is unnecessary.

This existing PR overlaps [#55092](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/55092), which fixes the same behavior through copy counts. This version retains the existing map-removal contract and adds a guard in the event emitter. The overlap needs maintainer coordination before either equivalent fix merges.

items.title: fix(mooncake): Restore TP replication awareness for DCP and reduce write amplification
items.body:
### Motivation

When `dcp_size > 1`, `_spec_tp_replication_factor` unconditionally returns 1, forcing every TP rank to save every chunk — `tp_size`× write amplification (e.g. 8× under TP8+DCP4). This is correct but wastes store bandwidth and capacity.

### Changes

**Restore TP replication awareness** (`worker.py`):
- Remove the `if self.dcp_size > 1: return 1` override in `_spec_tp_replication_factor`, so the true factor is used (MLA=`tp_size`, GQA=`tp_size//num_kv_head`, Mamba=1).
- Generalize `put_step` to `max(1, group_put_steps[g_idx] // dcp_size)` so each chunk is saved by exactly one rank per DCP namespace, reducing write amplification from `tp_size`× to `dcp_size`×.
- Adjust `put_step_rank` to `(tp_rank // dcp_size + g_idx) % put_step` to stripe within each DCP subgroup.

**Explicit per-rank DCP namespace** (`worker.py`, `data.py`):
- Add `dcp_size`/`dcp_rank` to `KVCacheStoreSendingThread` and `KVCacheStoreRecvingThread`.
- `key_for()` gains an optional `dcp_rank` parameter; save and load pass `dcp_rank=self.dcp_rank` so each rank writes to its own namespace.
- Restructure `_init_lookup_key_prefixes` into `(shard_rank, dcp_rank, prefix)` tuples with separate TP-shard and DCP-namespace dimensions. Add `_lookup_num_shards` for the total shard count per group.

**Safety guards** (`worker.py`):
- Clamp `token_len` to `len(block_hashes) * hash_block_size` before save (prevents `AssertionError` after external cache hit).
- Skip `NULL_BLOCK_ID` chunks during load (protects against abort races).
- Early return when all load chunks are filtered out (prevents `ZeroDivisionError`).

### Performance impact (MLA, TP8, DCP4)

| Metric | main | this PR |
|--------|------|----------|
| Write amplification | 8× per chunk | 2× per chunk |
| Lookup keys per chunk | 8 | 4 |
| Correctness | ✓ | ✓ |

### Production verification

Deployed to GLM-5.2 (TP8, DCP4, MLA): external prefix cache hit rate 28.3%, no regressions.

### Breaking changes

Store key `dcp_rank` now passed explicitly via `key_for(dcp_rank=...)` instead of baked into the cached prefix. Existing cache entries are unreachable after upgrade; requires one-time `reset_prefix_cache`. Rolling update is safe — old/new keys coexist.

### Test coverage

- 21 existing tests updated for new key format and lookup shard counts
- 5 new regression tests: namespace isolation, put_step coverage, partial lookup miss, save/load roundtrip, non-power-of-2 DCP size
- All **148** unit tests pass

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_store_worker.py -v
```

This PR was developed with AI assistance (Sisyphus/OhMyOpenCode). The submitting human has reviewed every changed line, run the full unit test suite, and verified the fix in production.

items.title: [Bugfix][Core] Redo prompt logprobs for requests resumed after reset_prefix_cache
items.body:
## Overview

Fixes #61490. After `reset_prefix_cache(reset_running_requests=True)`, a request whose in-flight prefill output carried the completed prompt logprobs is resumed without re-registering the requirement on the V1 runner, so the client gets null prompt logprobs. The scheduler now marks such requests when the output is dropped as stale and passes the ids to the runner, which re-registers the requirement for the re-run prefill.

## Claims

- Fixes the null prompt logprobs from #61490 on the V1 model runner path.
- No behavior change on the default V2 runner, which already re-registers resumed requests on its new-request path, and none for requests without prompt logprobs.

## Validation

New tests in `tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py`:

- `test_reset_prefix_cache_redoes_dropped_prompt_logprobs`: reset lands mid-prefill, the stale output carrying prompt logprobs is dropped, and the resumed schedule carries the redo directive exactly once (V1 runner).
- `test_stale_output_without_prompt_logprobs_sets_no_redo_flag`: a dropped stale chunk without prompt logprobs sets no marker.
- `test_redo_marker_cleared_on_v2_resume`: the V2 path clears the marker and sends no directive.

```
python -m pytest tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py tests/v1/core/test_async_scheduler.py -q
# 230 passed
```

`ruff check` and `ruff format --check` are clean on all touched files.

No GPU end-to-end run here (no CUDA build on this machine); the bug and fix live in scheduler/runner bookkeeping, which the tests above drive directly through the public scheduler API. CI covers the serving path.

## Details

Root cause: the reset preempts running requests with `drop_stale_output=True`. When the in-flight output then returns, it is discarded as stale, but that output carried the completed prompt logprobs and the runner had already retired its `num_prompt_logprobs` entry at prefill completion. The resumed request goes through the V1 cached-request path, which never re-registers the requirement, so the recomputed prefill emits no prompt logprobs.

The runner cannot infer the redo on its own: when a `num_prompt_logprobs` entry is gone it cannot distinguish "popped because delivered" from "popped because the output was dropped", and re-registering on every preemption would double-deliver for ordinary decode-time preemption. So the scheduler marks the request exactly where the stale drop happens, sends the affected ids once via `CachedRequestData.redo_prompt_logprobs_req_ids`, and the runner re-registers using the same expression as its new-request path. The marker is cleared when the directive is sent, on the V2 resumed-to-new conversion, and on any fresh schedule, so it cannot leak into a later step.

Duplicate check: no open PR references #61490, and keyword searches over open PRs (`prompt logprobs reset prefix`, `reset_prefix_cache logprobs`) turn up nothing addressing this. The issue had no linked PR and no one claimed it.

MRV1 note: this fix targets the V1 runner's cached-request path, where the bug lives. MRV2 is not affected, since it converts resumed requests into new requests and re-registers prompt logprobs there; the marker is explicitly cleared on that path.
