items.title: [ROCm][Perf] Batch short TurboQuant verify blocks and enable split-KV
items.body:
## Overview

Batch short TurboQuant continuation/verification requests and preserve their real query blocks so the existing attention kernel can reuse KV history and select split-KV. Actual vLLM HTTP serving on MI355X improves **2.71x, 1.66x and 1.14x** across the three eager speculative-decoding cells below.

Follow-up to AMD's #47896. No Triton kernel body or cache-format change. This closes both launcher selection and backend integration: a launcher-only change left the backend issuing attention separately for each request.

The large gains are specific to eager execution. Default graph-enabled serving is measured separately below; these are not universal serving speedups.

## Claims

- Short SoA continuation batches with an explicit maximum query length of at most 32 use one batched attention call, real query offsets, and the existing decode-sized/split-KV policy. First prefills keep their original raw-K/V path; long/mixed batches retain per-request handling.
- No new GPU-to-host read or synchronization, scheduler change, or stored-cache-format change. All six Triton kernel bodies are unchanged.
- ROCm D256 uses the existing launcher-side query rotation, avoiding the fused rotation's 262144-byte LDS request on a device with a 163840-byte limit.

## Validation

Head `0288f37b5927c90bd38c54240f7b1b3a405c50c8`; base `d6aca837c3c6b773a557448d526db219a5a5718b`. Final commit adds tests only; runtime source is identical to measured `d0d447e26277915a5e838b66c100f1dc7ac7500e`.

**Actual vLLM serving, not SGLang or a kernel microbenchmark:** one MI355X, Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct, BF16 weights, `turboquant_4bit_nc`, eager execution, ngram speculation with three draft tokens, prefix caching and chunked prefill enabled. Output throughput includes prefill and decode. No hot-path instrumentation in these timings.

| Input / concurrency / output | Base output tok/s | Patched output tok/s | Median paired speedup | Range over 3 pairs |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1024 / 16 / 128 | 347.68 | 942.92 | 2.712x | 2.678-2.776x |
| 8192 / 16 / 128 | 443.52 | 736.38 | 1.660x | 1.644-1.693x |
| 8192 / 64 / 128 | 499.36 | 568.81 | 1.139x | 1.132-1.195x |

Three fresh server pairs, order base/patched, patched/base, base/patched; same prompts and fixed output counts. Each cell warms C requests, then measures 2C requests. Throughput columns are arm medians; speedup is the median paired ratio. This is a finite synthetic repetition workload with nonzero ngram acceptance, not AgentX or a steady-state large-model throughput claim.

**Default graph-enabled serving**, same workload and three alternating pairs, also without counters. This additional scope check was selected after a flat paired smoke; it is separate from the original eager campaign.

| Input / concurrency / output | Base output tok/s | Patched output tok/s | Median paired ratio | Range over 3 pairs |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1024 / 16 / 128 | 2688.94 | 2681.27 | 0.997x | 0.983-1.007x |
| 8192 / 16 / 128 | 918.01 | 953.94 | 1.038x | 1.037-1.046x |
| 8192 / 64 / 128 | 570.16 | 570.92 | 1.003x | 0.996-1.010x |

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| CPU dispatch tests | 33 passed |
| MI355X GPU tests | 74 passed |
| Paired first-128 GSM8K model regression | 128/128 output token sequences identical |
| Actual worker dispatch | Real four-row query blocks and batched continuation calls observed |
| Source provenance | Both exercised runtime files match the committed head by SHA256 |
| Applicable pre-commit hooks | Passed, including Ruff, mypy, SPDX and CI test tethering |
| Kernel source comparison | All six Triton bodies unchanged; 7200 policy comparisons passed |

GPU coverage includes D64/128/256, K4/V4, K3/V4 and K3/V3, query lengths 1/2/4/8/16/32/33, ragged/zero-length query blocks, GQA4/6/8, sinks, rotated queries, histories to 65536, future-token poisoning, graph replay, and actual backend routing against an independent FP32 decoded-cache reference. Tests are wired into CPU and AMD Buildkite jobs.

<details>
<summary>Latency, output comparisons and measurement limits</summary>

All latency entries are base → patched. Percentiles use linear interpolation over per-request samples, then medians across the three runs. TPOT is each request's time from first to last output divided by output_tokens-1; speculative streaming chunks are not labeled individual-token intervals.

| Input / concurrency / output | TTFT p50, ms | TTFT p95, ms | TPOT p50, ms | TPOT p95, ms |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1024 / 16 / 128 | 148.19 → 102.03 | 155.64 → 154.39 | 34.27 → 10.76 | 60.31 → 22.15 |
| 8192 / 16 / 128 | 343.59 → 326.19 | 1447.87 → 1391.50 | 30.13 → 16.80 | 43.09 → 25.50 |
| 8192 / 64 / 128 | 3294.71 → 3427.15 | 8723.30 → 8735.99 | 80.22 → 77.61 | 139.46 → 141.65 |

C64 is a throughput improvement, not a uniform latency win: median TTFT is about 4% worse and p95 TPOT about 1.6% worse. Reported ranges describe three observed pairs, not confidence intervals.

Both 8K cells produce identical output IDs between arms for every request in every pair. At 1K/C16, 14/32 output sequences match exactly in each pair; differences occur on this repetitive, ignore-EOS workload despite fixed token counts. Do not interpret the throughput table as a claim of bitwise output invariance. The separate 128-example model regression is token-identical.

A separate instrumented holdout at 8K/C64/O512 measured a 1.922x median paired gain. A C1 diagnostic measured 1.235x but has only two measured requests per arm/run. These have Python worker counters and are corroborating diagnostics only; neither is pooled with the uninstrumented headline.

The initial pilots are excluded because the cache-reset endpoint returned HTTP 404. Final runs explicitly enable the localhost development endpoint, require successful resets, verify exact input/output counts, and record zero prefix-cache hits. Hot-path counters were removed for the headline reruns because reducing call count can also reduce instrumentation overhead.

Default graph startup and HTTP execution pass in both arms. The paired smoke produced 32/32 identical output sequences; the repeated graph grid's output comparisons are retained separately. Both initial startup attempts failed on the same read-only FlyDSL cache directory; reruns used the same writable `FLYDSL_RUNTIME_CACHE_DIR` and `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` in both arms. Eager and graph-mode ratios are never pooled.

Hardware qualification is MI355X only. Runtime: HIP 7.2.53211, Torch 2.13.0+git733fca1, Triton 3.8.0, FlyDSL 0.2.0. Exact base and PR Python/Triton sources share the ROCm vLLM 0.31.0 image's compiled native extensions. This is a source overlay, not a clean native-extension rebuild. No native extension source changes are in this PR. Other jobs used other GPUs, never the allocated benchmark GPU.
</details>

<details>
<summary>Model regression protocol</summary>

Qwen/Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct revision `aa8e72537993ba99e69dfaafa59ed015b17504d1`, BF16 weights, same TurboQuant cache, eager execution, ngram speculation (3 tokens, lookup 2..5), prefix caching/chunked prefill on, seed 0. Context 4096, batched-token cap 2048, max sequences 8, GPU memory utilization 0.15; greedy generation with a 512-token cap and no custom stop string. The first 128 GSM8K test examples were fixed before running. The tokenizer chat template wraps each question plus `\nSolve step by step and put the final numeric answer after ####.`

Dataset SHA256: `3730d312f6e3440559ace48831e51066acaca737f6eabec99bccb9e4b3c39d14`. Serialized prompt-list SHA256: `fb2a5c51069419136e490fdb4dbeb26cc95c6589ef60aa3f1a83d6e59e074217`.

All input IDs and 128 output token sequences match. Eight examples hit the output cap in both arms. Strict #### extraction scores 44/128 with 77 unparsed in both arms because many answers use boxed notation; the existing upstream last-number extraction scores 101/128 in both arms. Both scoring paths are retained, not cherry-picked. This is a regression check, not a quality noninferiority study.
</details>

<details>
<summary>Reproduce tests and HTTP serving workload</summary>

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest --noconftest tests/kernels/turboquant/test_triton_turboquant_dispatch.py -q
.venv/bin/python -m pytest --noconftest tests/kernels/turboquant/test_triton_turboquant_verify.py -q
.venv/bin/pre-commit run --from-ref d6aca837c3c6b773a557448d526db219a5a5718b --to-ref HEAD
```

Start each revision in the same compatible ROCm environment. Use separate writable caches if the container package directory is read-only. The development endpoint below is bound to localhost for explicit prefix-cache resets.

```bash
VLLM_SERVER_DEV_MODE=1 vllm serve Qwen/Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct \
  --revision aa8e72537993ba99e69dfaafa59ed015b17504d1 \
  --served-model-name qwen --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8000 \
  --dtype bfloat16 --kv-cache-dtype turboquant_4bit_nc \
  --attention-backend TURBOQUANT --max-model-len 16384 \
  --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 --max-num-seqs 128 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.5 --enforce-eager \
  --enable-prefix-caching --enable-chunked-prefill --seed 0 \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"ngram","num_speculative_tokens":3,"prompt_lookup_max":5,"prompt_lookup_min":2}'
```

Save the following as `reproduce_client.py` and run it against each fresh server. Repeat three pairs in alternating order. It emits the measured duration, output throughput and per-request records; retain server logs and `/metrics` for speculative acceptance and cache behavior.

```python
"""Run against one already-started baseline or patched vLLM server."""
import asyncio
import json
import os
import time

import aiohttp
from transformers import AutoTokenizer

URL = os.environ.get('SERVER_URL', 'http://127.0.0.1:8000')
MODEL = os.environ.get('MODEL', 'Qwen/Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct')
TOKENIZER = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(
    MODEL, revision='aa8e72537993ba99e69dfaafa59ed015b17504d1'
)
UNIT = TOKENIZER.encode(
    'The red fox visits the blue lake. The green bird visits the yellow tree. ',
    add_special_tokens=False,
)
ENDING = TOKENIZER.encode(
    '\nContinue repeating the following text exactly: The red fox visits the blue lake. '
    'The green bird visits the yellow tree.\n', add_special_tokens=False,
)


def prompt(length, index):
    prefix = TOKENIZER.encode(f'Document {index:06d}.\n', add_special_tokens=False)
    body = (UNIT * ((length + len(UNIT) - 1) // len(UNIT)))
    return prefix + body[:length - len(prefix) - len(ENDING)] + ENDING


async def request(session, ids, output):
    start = time.perf_counter()
    first = last = None
    tokens = []
    usage = None
    async with session.post(URL + '/v1/completions', json={
        'model': 'qwen', 'prompt': ids, 'max_tokens': output, 'temperature': 0,
        'ignore_eos': True, 'stream': True, 'return_token_ids': True,
        'stream_options': {'include_usage': True},
    }) as response:
        assert response.status == 200, await response.text()
        async for line in response.content:
            line = line.decode().strip()
            if not line.startswith('data: ') or line == 'data: [DONE]':
                continue
            data = json.loads(line[6:])
            if data.get('usage'):
                usage = data['usage']
            for choice in data.get('choices', []):
                delta = choice.get('token_ids') or []
                if delta or choice.get('text'):
                    last = time.perf_counter()
                    if first is None:
                        first = last
                    tokens.extend(delta)
    assert usage['prompt_tokens'] == len(ids)
    assert usage['completion_tokens'] == len(tokens) == output
    return {'ttft': first - start, 'tpot': (last - first) / (output - 1),
            'output_ids': tokens}


async def cell(session, length, concurrency, output, warmup=False):
    for _ in range(20):
        async with session.post(URL + '/reset_prefix_cache') as response:
            assert response.status == 200
            reset = await response.json()
        if reset['success']:
            break
        await asyncio.sleep(.25)
    else:
        raise RuntimeError('Prefix-cache reset failed')
    semaphore = asyncio.Semaphore(concurrency)

    async def one(index):
        async with semaphore:
            return await request(session, prompt(length, index + (500000 if warmup else 0)), output)

    count = concurrency if warmup else 2 * concurrency
    start = time.perf_counter()
    records = await asyncio.gather(*(one(i) for i in range(count)))
    duration = time.perf_counter() - start
    print(json.dumps({'input': length, 'concurrency': concurrency, 'output': output,
                      'warmup': warmup, 'seconds': duration,
                      'tokens_per_second': count * output / duration, 'records': records}))


async def main():
    cells = json.loads(os.environ.get('CELLS', '[[1024,16,128],[8192,16,128],[8192,64,128]]'))
    async with aiohttp.ClientSession(timeout=aiohttp.ClientTimeout(total=900)) as session:
        for length, concurrency, output in cells:
            await cell(session, length, concurrency, 16, warmup=True)
            await cell(session, length, concurrency, output)


asyncio.run(main())
```
</details>

## Details

The unified kernel already has per-query causal masking. The original launcher classified multi-row verify blocks as prefill-like; the backend also expanded short continuations into synthetic single-token requests and launched separately per sequence. Passing real offsets and batching short continuation requests removes those integration costs while selecting the existing 3D kernel. Long blocks, caller tile overrides, `force_2d`, the 1024-token split threshold and conservative missing-maximum fallback retain their behavior. This does not implement the full-graph metadata changes proposed in #53410.

The previously reported **2.785x** AgentX result used SGLang calling AMD's public vLLM kernel. It motivated the PR, but is not this PR's vLLM serving result. The table above supplies that missing validation.

AI assistance was used to implement, test and document this change. Human review remains pending; it is not represented as completed. Upstream's contributor-authorization gate currently requires maintainer action before hosted CI can run; local checks above have passed.

items.title: [KVConnector] Decouple store retention from HBM retention
items.body:
## Purpose
This PR decouples Mooncake Store retention from local HBM prefix-cache retention. For hybrid KV-cache layouts, local residency and remote persistence serve different purposes. Local retention controls what must stay in HBM to continue execution, while store retention controls what can be reused by future shared-prefix requests.

This distinction matters for sliding-window style cache groups. To keep only the latest replayable sliding-window tail in HBM, users may set:
```bash
VLLM_PREFIX_CACHE_RETENTION_INTERVAL=0
```
## Design
The change is intentionally small: MooncakeStoreWorker now initializes MooncakeStoreCoordinator with retention_interval=None. This keeps the existing local retention behavior unchanged, while allowing Mooncake Store to persist reusable sliding-window checkpoints independently.

This matches the direction described in the DeepSeek-V4 inference framework: hybrid attention introduces heterogeneous KV entries with different cache sizes and policies, and on-disk SWA KV storage is managed through full caching, periodic checkpointing, or zero caching depending on the storage/computation tradeoff.

## Tests

```bash
pytest -q tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_store_coordinator.py -k store_mask
```

items.title: [Metrics][Frontend] Pluggable KV connector metrics on the Rust frontend via connector metrics descriptor
items.body:
## Purpose

Today the Rust frontend's `/metrics` can only export KV connector metrics for Nixl and Mooncake, because each of them has dedicated Rust code. Stats from every other connector (Offloading, HF3FS, HiSparse, and out-of-tree connectors) do reach the Rust process, but are silently dropped, so these metrics disappear as soon as `VLLM_USE_RUST_FRONTEND=1` is set.

This PR lets a connector describe its own metrics, so the Rust frontend can export them without any per-connector Rust code. Design discussion: RFC: #58562.

## Changes

How it works:

1. On the Rust frontend, the first time a connector reports stats, it also sends a short description of its metrics: name, type, help text, histogram buckets, and where each value sits in its stats. The description rides the existing scheduler stats message; there is no new RPC.
2. When the Rust frontend sees a description, it registers those metrics. After that, every stats tick carries values only, and Rust updates the metrics from them.
3. On the Python frontend nothing changes: no description is sent, and the existing Prometheus metrics stay as they are.
4. With MultiConnector, each child sends its own description and is exported separately.

Nixl and Mooncake keep their existing Rust code paths.

Key pieces:

- **`maybe_attach_metrics_descriptor()`** (Python): attaches the description once, and only when the Rust frontend is on. A connector calls it from its stats `to_dict()`.
- **Built-in connectors** (Python): Offloading, HF3FS, and HiSparse build their description from the same definitions their Prometheus metrics use; a unit test keeps the two in sync.
- **`DescriptorDrivenAdapter`** (Rust): registers metrics from a description and applies later values to them.
- **Routing in `metrics.rs`** (Rust): stats from connectors without dedicated Rust code go to the adapter, whose metrics are rendered on `/metrics` after the built-in ones.

- **Rust frontend zero-series pre-create:** once a connector metrics descriptor arrives, the Rust frontend pre-creates zero-valued series for every engine × model_name × const labels.
- **Rust HELP trailing-period strip:** when registering from a descriptor, the Rust frontend strips a single trailing `.` from HELP text before Prometheus adds its own, so HELP lines end with one period (matching the Python frontend).
- **List-valued gauge samples:** when a gauge's stats value is a list (HiSparse reports per-step lists), the Rust frontend sets the gauge to the last element, matching the Python Prometheus logger's last-value behavior.

An out-of-tree connector adopts this the same way: attach a description in its stats `to_dict()`.

> **NOTE:** On the Rust frontend, connector series are registered from the metrics descriptor carried on the first `SchedulerStats` that includes KV connector stats. Engine cores emit no stats while idle, so connector series appear after the connector first reports stats (then pre-created at 0 for all DP engines), rather than immediately at startup as on the Python frontend. The engine core was left untouched; a startup-only stats message from the core would close this gap but is not required for correct values after the first report.


## Known field differences (Rust vs Python)

These are field-level (name / HELP / TYPE / labels / suffixes), not value mismatches:

- **(a) Inherent encoder format:** Python's Prometheus client emits `_created` timestamps and names counters with a `_total` suffix in HELP/TYPE; the Rust encoder does not. Rust also pre-creates zero series after the first descriptor, so some families appear as samples earlier than on Python (where samples appear lazily after the first increment).
- **(b) Legacy / deprecated Python-only:** a few older Offloading families remain on the Python frontend only and are not part of the descriptor surface.
- **(c) Config-gated:** `stores_skipped` is always present in the Offloading descriptor (and therefore on Rust); the Python Prometheus path registers it only when `store_threshold >= 2`.
- **Nixl / Mooncake HELP punctuation:** on the Rust frontend, Nixl and Mooncake HELP strings still end with `..` because those connectors use the pre-existing typed Rust registration path, which is outside this PR; the trailing-period strip applies only to descriptor-registered metrics. The Python frontend's Nixl HELP lines end with a single `.`.
- **(d) Real adapter bugs:** none found in the paired field comparison across Offloading, HF3FS, HiSparse, OOT, and Multi.

## Test Plan

Unit tests:

```bash
cargo test -p vllm-engine-core-client connector_metrics
pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_metrics_descriptor_emit.py
```

E2E: for each connector, start `vllm serve` with that connector, scrape `/metrics`, send a few requests, then scrape again. Each case runs on both frontends; the two runs differ only in `VLLM_USE_RUST_FRONTEND=1`.

- Rust frontend passes if the connector's metrics appear on `/metrics` and update after the requests.
- Python frontend passes if no description is emitted and the metrics are the same as before this change.

<details>
<summary>E2E commands</summary>

Every case uses `--load-format dummy`. The Python and Rust frontend runs are identical except that the Rust run sets `VLLM_USE_RUST_FRONTEND=1`. `<OutOfTreeConnector>` / `<out_of_tree_pkg>` stand for the out-of-tree connector used in the test.

```bash
# Rust frontend only:
export VLLM_USE_RUST_FRONTEND=1

# Traffic and scrape (same for every case)
curl -s localhost:8000/metrics > before.txt
PREFIX=$(python3 -c 'print("token block cache reuse " * 80)')
for i in 1 2 3 4; do
  curl -s localhost:8000/v1/completions -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
    -d "{\"model\":\"$MODEL\",\"prompt\":\"$PREFIX req $i\",\"max_tokens\":16,\"temperature\":0}"
done
curl -s localhost:8000/metrics > after.txt
curl -s localhost:8000/v1/models   # owned_by: vllm-frontend-rs (Rust) / vllm (Python)
```

**Offloading**

```bash
MODEL=moonshotai/Kimi-K3  # config reduced to 4 layers / 8 experts so it fits one GPU with dummy weights
vllm serve $MODEL --trust-remote-code --load-format dummy --enforce-eager \
  --data-parallel-size 2 --max-model-len 4096 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.45 \
  --enable-prefix-caching --mamba-cache-mode align \
  --kv-transfer-config '{"kv_connector":"OffloadingConnector","kv_role":"kv_both",
    "kv_connector_extra_config":{"cpu_bytes_to_use":1073741824}}'
```

**HF3FS**

```bash
python3 -m vllm.distributed.kv_transfer.kv_connector.v1.hf3fs.hf3fs_metadata_server \
  --host 127.0.0.1 --port 18000 &
MODEL=Qwen/Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct
vllm serve $MODEL --load-format dummy --enforce-eager \
  --max-model-len 4096 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.45 --enable-prefix-caching \
  --kv-transfer-config '{"kv_connector":"HF3FSKVConnector","kv_role":"kv_both",
    "kv_connector_extra_config":{"hf3fs_storage_path":"/tmp/hf3fs_mock",
      "hf3fs_file_size":1073741824,"hf3fs_metadata_server_url":"http://127.0.0.1:18000"}}'
```

**HiSparse**

```bash
export VLLM_DEEP_GEMM_WARMUP=skip
MODEL=deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V3.2
vllm serve $MODEL --trust-remote-code --load-format dummy --enforce-eager \
  --hf-overrides '{"num_hidden_layers": 8}' \
  --tensor-parallel-size 8 --max-model-len 1024 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.75 \
  --kv-transfer-config '{"kv_connector":"HiSparseConnector","kv_role":"kv_both",
    "kv_connector_extra_config":{"host_pool_gib":4}}'
```

**Out-of-tree connector**: same `vllm serve` flags as Offloading, with

```bash
--kv-transfer-config '{"kv_connector":"<OutOfTreeConnector>",
  "kv_connector_module_path":"<out_of_tree_pkg>","kv_role":"kv_both"}'
```

**MultiConnector (Offloading + out-of-tree)**: same flags as Offloading, with

```bash
--kv-transfer-config '{"kv_connector":"MultiConnector","kv_role":"kv_both",
  "kv_connector_extra_config":{"connectors":[
    {"kv_connector":"OffloadingConnector","kv_role":"kv_both",
     "kv_connector_extra_config":{"cpu_bytes_to_use":1073741824}},
    {"kv_connector":"<OutOfTreeConnector>","kv_connector_module_path":"<out_of_tree_pkg>",
     "kv_role":"kv_both"}]}}'
```

**MultiConnector (Nixl + out-of-tree), 1 prefill + 1 decode**

```bash
export VLLM_SSM_CONV_STATE_LAYOUT=DS   # needed for Nixl with this hybrid model

    "kv_connector_extra_config":{"connectors":[
      {"kv_connector":"NixlConnector","kv_role":"'$1'"},
      {"kv_connector":"<OutOfTreeConnector>","kv_connector_module_path":"<out_of_tree_pkg>",
       "kv_role":"kv_both"}]}}'
}
FLAGS="--trust-remote-code --load-format dummy --enforce-eager --max-model-len 2048 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.45 --enable-prefix-caching --mamba-cache-mode align"
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 VLLM_NIXL_SIDE_CHANNEL_PORT=5610 \
  vllm serve $MODEL $FLAGS --port 8100 --kv-transfer-config "$(multi kv_producer)" &

  vllm serve $MODEL $FLAGS --port 8200 --kv-transfer-config "$(multi kv_consumer)" &
```

items.title: [Bugfix] Hybrid prefix caching: keep the Mamba prompt-boundary state until the request ends and evict it after its attention blocks
items.body:
## Overview

Fixes the lifetime of a hybrid request's reusable Mamba "align" state block: it stays referenced for as long as the request runs, and at request end it is the last of the request's blocks to reach the LRU free queue. FIX #61281

## Claims

- A running hybrid request no longer loses its prompt-boundary Mamba state to other requests' allocations: `MambaManager` holds one reference on that block from the moment it is registered, or taken over from the cache by a resumed or sibling request, until the request is freed, across the range retirement, the running-state swap and the partial-tail CoW copy.
- At request end attention groups are freed before Mamba groups on both the direct (`KVCacheCoordinator.free`) and the deferred (`pop_blocks_for_free`) path, so the single state block is evicted after the attention blocks it belongs with, not before.
- The next turn of a conversation now hits the previous prompt in every group; before, the attention group hit while the Mamba group returned 0 and the reconciled hit was 0.
- Cost: one extra block per Mamba group per running request (the running state plus the boundary state). Single-group and non-Mamba hybrid models are unaffected: no behaviour change in their managers, and the free order is the identity for them.

## Validation

Deterministic reproducer from the issue (no GPU, drives `KVCacheManager`), before and after:

```text
# main
--- 1. prompt boundary on a Mamba block boundary (remove_skipped_blocks)
after 1 decode step: snapshot ref_cnt=0 (0 = in the free queue while 'a' still runs)
after 12 unrelated requests while 'a' decodes: snapshot recycled
next turn: per-group hits (64, 0) tokens, reconciled hit 0
--- 2. prompt boundary inside a Mamba block (CoW copy released)
after 12 unrelated requests while 'a' decodes: snapshot recycled
next turn: per-group hits (48, 0) tokens, reconciled hit 0
--- 3. eviction order at request end
free queue position: snapshot 26, attention blocks [27, 28, 29, 30]   (both group orders, both free paths)

# this PR
after 1 decode step: snapshot ref_cnt=1
after 12 unrelated requests while 'a' decodes: snapshot still cached
next turn: per-group hits (64, 64) tokens, reconciled hit 64
next turn: per-group hits (48, 48) tokens, reconciled hit 48
free queue position: snapshot 30, attention blocks [26, 27, 28, 29]
```

New tests in `tests/v1/core/test_mamba_boundary_snapshot_lifetime.py` (fail on main, pass here):

- `test_boundary_state_outlives_decode[block-aligned|partial-tail × dense|sparse]`: the state block keeps a reference through decode and through 12 unrelated requests cycling the pool, the request holds at most two Mamba blocks, every block is back in the pool after `free`, and the follow-up prompt hits the boundary in both groups.
- `test_boundary_state_held_after_cache_hit[... × preempted|sibling × dense|sparse]`: a request that takes the boundary state over from the cache (re-admitted after preemption, or a second request with the same prompt whose producer finishes first) holds it the same way.
- `test_request_end_evicts_attention_before_boundary_state[attn-first|mamba-first × free|deferred]`: after the request ends, the state block sits behind all of the request's hashed attention blocks in the free queue.

Existing suites run locally on a CPU-only build (`VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu`): 
| suite | result on this branch | note |
|---|---|---|
| `tests/v1/core/test_mamba_boundary_snapshot_lifetime.py` (new) | 16 passed | fail on main |
| `tests/v1/core/test_single_type_kv_cache_manager.py`, `test_mamba_align_chunk_split.py` | 100 passed | |
| `tests/v1/core/test_deferred_block_free.py`, `test_swa_inflight_window_free.py`, `test_prefix_replay.py`, `test_async_scheduler.py`, `test_priority_preemption_bug.py` | all passed | |
| `tests/v1/core/test_prefix_caching.py` | 170 passed, 3 HiSparse failures | the same 3 fail on unmodified main in this environment (no accelerator) |
| `tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py`, `test_kv_cache_utils.py` | all pass except the multimodal / encoder-cache tests | those cannot inspect a Llava config offline; identical on main |
| `tests/v1/core/prefix_cache/`, `tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_connector_hybrid_mamba.py`, `test_mooncake_store_connector.py` | 250 passed, 6 failed + 2 errors | failures need an accelerator device or a model; identical on main |

Total over these suites on the branch: 908 passed, 53 failed, 2 errors; the failure set is exactly the environmental set seen on unmodified main.


`pre-commit run --all-files`: clean (ruff, mypy, typos, SPDX, test tethering and the rest all pass; nothing modified).

## Details

Root cause. Align mode keeps only the running state per request; every other state is a prefix-cache entry that lives in the free queue with its hash. That is fine for intermediate states, but the state at the prompt's reusable boundary is the one block a later turn needs together with the request's attention blocks, and those stay referenced until the request finishes. Three paths push the boundary block into the free queue a step into decode: `remove_skipped_blocks` -> `_remove_blocks_in_range` (boundary on a block boundary), the `last_state_block_idx` swap in the same function, and the release of the CoW copy of a partial tail by `Scheduler._free_cow_retained_blocks` once the copy step has run. Any allocation then recycles it (`get_new_blocks` -> `_maybe_evict_cached_block`), and the hybrid lookup is the minimum over groups. At request end the groups were freed in config order (direct path) or reversed config order (deferred path), so depending on the model's group order the state block was the first of the request's blocks to be evicted.

Design. Rather than special-casing each free path, the manager takes one reference on the boundary block on the request's behalf (`_retain_boundary_block`, mirroring the CoW retention refs that already exist) wherever the request comes to own that state: a full block whose hash ends at the boundary (`cache_blocks`), a re-keyed prefill checkpoint or a partial tail (`_cache_partial_tail_block`), and the hit block adopted by a resumed or sibling request (`add_local_computed_blocks`; registering the request's own boundary later replaces that hold). One helper, `_prompt_boundary`, defines the position at every site. The existing free paths then only drop the block's ref to 1 and null it out of the request's table as before. On the producer CoW the hold moves with the hash to `cow_block`, so the scheduler's post-copy release leaves the copy referenced. `pop_blocks_for_free` releases the hold: if the block is still in the request's table it just drops the extra ref, otherwise it lists the block first so it is the last one freed. The coordinator orders group frees once (`_free_order`: attention first, Mamba last) and `pop_blocks_for_free` returns groups in the reverse of that order so the caller's reversed free matches `free`.

Only the prompt boundary is held. Under sparse retention (the default `prefix_cache_retention_interval=0`) that is the request's only hashed state apart from a shared-prefix junction; under dense retention intermediate states keep their existing free-queue lifetime, so memory stays bounded at two blocks per Mamba group per running request.

Not covered / residual risk:

- A shared-prefix junction state (`shared_prefix_boundary`, behind `enable_mamba_shared_prefix_checkpoint`, off by default) is registered the same way and keeps the old lifetime; holding it too would double the per-request cost for a feature that is off by default, so it is left out.
- EAGLE/MTP: the hold follows `drop_eagle_checkpoint_block` like the partial-tail registration does, so it lands on the dropped-block boundary; the speculative scratch blocks are above the running state and never hashed, so `_relocate_speculative_block`'s writable assertion is unaffected.
- `evict_blocks` (connector-driven eviction) strips the hash from a held block; the block then stays allocated until the request ends. Harmless, and the same as a held attention block today.
- Non-align Mamba modes and non-Mamba groups take none of the new paths.

items.title: [Bugfix][Core] Unblock scheduling after a failed async KV load
items.body:
## Overview

With `kv_load_failure_policy="recompute"`, a request whose async KV load fails with no usable prefix can sit in WAITING forever, even on an idle engine, and the requests queued behind it never run. Nothing errors. It takes a connector that offers the same async load again on the retry, e.g. MooncakeStoreConnector (async by default) or a MultiConnector whose offloading child holds the prefix after NIXL fails.

Related: #59096, #59099, #59102, #59325, #59329 (independent fixes in nearby KV load paths).

## Claims

- The failed request is admitted again once its load fits.
- Requests holding loaded blocks are no longer stuck behind it.
- No change when the failed load keeps a valid prefix.

## Validation

```bash
python -m pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_kv_load_failure_recovery.py -q
python -m pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit tests/v1/core -q
pre-commit run --files vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_kv_load_failure_recovery.py
```

On main the two no-prefix cases fail (`assert <RequestStatus.WAITING: 1> == <RequestStatus.WAITING_FOR_REMOTE_KVS: 3>`) and the three-request case schedules neither loaded request (`assert 'id-7' in {}`); the valid-prefix control passes. With the fix all 18 tests in the file pass, and either half of the fix alone leaves a test red.

Suites, macOS arm64 (CPU), with the fix:

- `tests/v1/kv_connector/unit`: 1905 passed, 12 failed, 42 skipped
- `tests/v1/core`: 919 passed, 1 failed, 4 errors

Without the scheduler change (new tests kept), `tests/v1/kv_connector/unit` gives 1902 passed and 15 failed: the same 12 plus the 3 new tests. `tests/v1/core` is unchanged. The other 12 and the core failures also fail on unmodified main here: NVIDIA-only paths (hf3fs, HiSparse, offloading tiering), Ray on the CPU platform, a gated model, and end-to-end tests that need more free RAM than this machine had.

CPU only: the tests drive the real Scheduler with a mocked connector, as the rest of this file does. No GPU run.

## Details

After the failure, `_update_waiting_for_remote_kv` frees the request's blocks ([scheduler.py:3097](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/84bcbc62644356270aaaa5e2d0237d03adc9bb3a/vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py#L3097)) but leaves it in `_inflight_prefills` and `kv_holding_waiting`.

- Async admission reserves the remaining blocks of every in-flight prefill (#44560, [scheduler.py:1214](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/84bcbc62644356270aaaa5e2d0237d03adc9bb3a/vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py#L1214-L1217)). Holding nothing, the request now reserves its whole sequence against its own retry, so the gate ([kv_cache_manager.py:575](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/84bcbc62644356270aaaa5e2d0237d03adc9bb3a/vllm/v1/core/kv_cache_manager.py#L575-L579)) needs room for the load plus its full size. In the test: 10 usable blocks, a 6-block prompt, a 5-block hit, and 10 - 6 < 5 on every step.
- `kv_holding_waiting` is drained first so that a block holder never waits behind a request whose failed allocation stops the scan (#58947). The freed request is exactly that request.

The fix discards it from `_inflight_prefills` when its blocks are freed, as preemption does, and moves a request that no longer holds blocks (by `_holds_kv_blocks`, which the queues already route by) from `kv_holding_waiting` to the front of `waiting` before scheduling it. The reservation itself is unchanged.

Not a duplicate: no open PR changes these lines on current main. #55297 makes MooncakeStore's next lookup a miss after an invalid-block failure; it is complementary and leaves the scheduler state, `failed_recving` and other connectors as they are. #57418 and #59343 use the reservation without touching this path; #53298, #54733 and #56733 handle sync or hybrid failures, and #59603 forwards failed loads to LMCache's scheduler side.

## AI assistance

I used an AI coding assistant (Claude) to audit this code path, write the fix and write the tests. I reviewed every changed line and ran the tests above myself. The commit carries a Co-authored-by trailer, as AGENTS.md asks.

items.title: [Bugfix][Spec Decode] Restore hybrid mamba align cache hits under spec decode with a KV connector (related to #53505)
items.body:
# PR: [Bugfix][Spec Decode] Restore hybrid mamba align cache hits under spec decode with a KV connector (related to #53505)

**Related**: #53505 (scoped as related — see Scope below)

## Summary

Fix three deterministic defects on the spec-decode + hybrid-mamba + KV-connector
path. Two of them misclassify DFlash/DSpark as eagle-family drafters and corrupt
or degrade the mamba align prefix cache; the third hard-crashes the EngineCore
when a finer `prefix_match_unit` meets a sliding-window draft group.

Local reproduction uses the native `kv_offloading_size` OffloadingConnector (no
LMCacheMP server was available): output is clean before and after, and the
change restores the expected prefix-cache hits (`[0, 560, 560]`). It does not
reproduce the reporter's retrieve-ON LMCache corruption cell, so this PR is
declared **related to** #53505 rather than a full fix of that issue.

## Stack

This PR stacks on #54163 (commit `e1b29d5`). The shared capability-bit change
(`use_eagle_preserves_target_kv_cache()` and the scheduler/KV-cache-manager
wiring) is reviewed once in #54163; once that PR merges, the diff here shrinks
to the delta below (offloading fallback + sliding-window tolerance + regression
test).

## Root Causes

### 1. DFlash/DSpark get the EAGLE last-block drop (primary corruption source)

Same root cause as #53477: `use_eagle()` returns `True` for `dflash`/`dspark`,
so `_mamba_block_aligned_split()` backs `last_cache_position` off by one mamba
block. Prompts shorter than two mamba blocks never materialize a block-aligned
recurrent state; the next lookup converges to 0 and decode resumes from a wrong
boundary. With a connector attached, its `update_state_after_alloc` /
`build_connector_meta` bookkeeping and mamba partial-tail CoW paths amplify the
bad boundary into corrupted decode (the issue reporter's U+FFFD garbage /
runaway turns).

Fix: introduce `SpeculativeConfig.use_eagle_preserves_target_kv_cache()`
(`eagle/eagle3/mtp` only) and use it in the scheduler split + the KV cache
manager's `use_eagle` argument (see #53477 PR for the full chain).

### 2. Offloading connector marks every KV group as eagle under DFlash

`SchedulerOffloadConfig.from_spec()` fell back to

```python
use_eagle = (spec_config is not None and spec_config.use_eagle())
if use_eagle and not eagle_groups:
    eagle_groups = set(range(len(kv_cache_config.kv_cache_groups)))
```

Under DFlash/DSpark this flags **all 38 groups — including the target's mamba
group — as volatile eagle groups**, so `storable_chunks()` excludes the trailing
chunk of every decode step from offloading and the store/lookup windows drift.
This matches the reporter's H12 instrumentation showing off-by-window store
ranges even with retrieval disabled.

Fix: use the precise capability bit here too, so only eagle-family drafters get
the fallback.

### 3. SlidingWindowManager assert-crashes on a finer prefix_match_unit

With a hybrid mamba target configured with `prefix_match_unit` finer than the
mamba block size, the coordinator's `alignment_tokens` becomes finer than the
draft model's sliding-window group block size, and
`SlidingWindowManager.find_longest_cache_hit()` hit:

```python
assert alignment_tokens % kv_cache_spec.block_size == 0
# 16 % 560 -> EngineDeadError, killing all in-flight requests
```

Fix: fall back to block-aligned hits for that group instead of crashing.
(Verified crash before fix, clean hit after fix.)

Reachability note: on current main the core coordinator guard (#51843) already
disables fine-grained hits when an incompatible sliding-window manager is
present, so this assert is not reachable on the native path; the fallback is
kept as defense-in-depth. The Mooncake store-side
`partial_hash_hits_enabled()` mirror does not include the same
unsupported-manager exclusion — a coordinator-level regression with real
fine-grained hashes is left for a separate follow-up.

## Scope / not covered

The reporter's corruption repro needs a running LMCacheMP server with retrieval
enabled and long (40 min) agent sessions; this PR restores cache hits under the
native OffloadingConnector path but does **not** reproduce or claim to close
the retrieve-ON LMCache corruption cell. The remaining suspect is the `assert
RequestStatus.is_finished(req.status)` in `_update_from_kv_xfer_finished`
(crashes the engine on a retrieve that finished after the request was dropped) —
kept out of this PR for a separate fix.

## Changes

- `vllm/config/speculative.py` — add `use_eagle_preserves_target_kv_cache()`.
- `vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py` — precise `drop_last_prefix_cache_block`;
  pass it as `KVCacheManager(use_eagle=...)`.
- `vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/offloading/scheduler.py` —
  eagle-group fallback uses the precise capability bit.
- `vllm/v1/core/single_type_kv_cache_manager.py` — SWA group falls back to
  block-aligned hits when the coordinator alignment is finer than its block size.
- `tests/v1/core/test_mamba_align_chunk_split.py` — two new regression tests
  (`test_dflash_does_not_back_off_last_cache_position`,
  `test_sliding_window_group_tolerates_finer_alignment`); stub updates.
- `tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py` — attribute update for the eagle encoder test.

## Test commands and results

Local reproduction (2×L40S, vLLM 0.26.0 layout, Qwen3.5-4B hybrid +
Qwen3.5-4B-DFlash draft, native `kv_offloading_size` connector):

| Configuration | Before fix | After fix |
|---|---|---|
| DFlash + align + offload 0/1/4 GB | clean, but boundary wrong | clean, hits restored `[0,560,560]` |
| DFlash + align + `prefix_match_unit=16` | **EngineDeadError (assert)** | hits `[0,560,560]` |
| 4 concurrent interleaved sessions + offload | clean | clean, identical output |

```bash
# CPU unit tests
python -m pytest tests/v1/core/test_mamba_align_chunk_split.py -q
python -m pytest tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py -q -k "mamba_align"
```

## Why this is not duplicating an existing PR

No open PR targets #53505. Overlapping/related work that touches the same files
or semantics and will need reconciliation:

- #54163 — this PR's stack base (the focused #53477 fix; same capability bit).
- #53479 — the same speculative back-off plus retained-boundary handling.
- #52771 — the same native-offloading fallback in `offloading/scheduler.py`
  under a different policy.
- #54076 — the splitter's mamba-group block-size source.
- #54041 — explicit DFlash draft-group annotation (closed).

Happy to reconcile or drop parts where the maintainer PRs cover the semantics.

## AI assistance disclosure

This fix was developed with AI assistance (static analysis, reproduction scripts,
test generation). All changes were reviewed and verified by a human.

items.title: [Perf][Kernel][LoRA] Optimize Multi-LoRA kernels for fragmented token distributions
items.body:
## Overview

This PR optimizes the Triton LoRA expand and shrink kernels for fragmented Multi-LoRA workloads where tokens are distributed across many adapters.

The current implementation uses the global token dimension for kernel grid generation, although each LoRA adapter only processes a subset of those tokens. This change uses the maximum number of tokens assigned to any active LoRA adapter as the kernel M dimension.

## Claims

- Reduces unnecessary M-dimension thread block launches for fragmented Multi-LoRA workloads.
- Improves end-to-end latency for workloads with many simultaneously active LoRA adapters.
- Preserves performance for non-fragmented single-LoRA workloads.

Example decode-heavy results on NVIDIA RTX 5090 with Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct, LoRA rank 32, batch size matching the number of active adapters, 8-token prompts, and 128 generated tokens:

| Active LoRAs | Baseline E2E latency | Optimized E2E latency | Latency reduction |
|-------------:|---------:|----------:|------------------:|
| 1 | 1.03 s | 1.02 s | ~1% |
| 8 | 1.20 s | 1.11 s | ~8% |
| 32 | 2.13 s | 1.64 s | ~23% |
| 64 | 4.06 s | 2.08 s | ~49% |
| 128 | 5.59 s | 3.37 s | ~40% |

## Validation

Validated with:

- Triton LoRA kernel correctness tests for expand and shrink paths.
- Multi-LoRA end-to-end benchmarks using Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct with:
  - 1, 8, 32, 64, and 128 active LoRA adapters
  - LoRA rank 32
  - batch size equal to the number of active adapters
  - 128 generated tokens
- The benchmark utility was extended to validate the modified LoRA kernel paths and evaluate fragmented Multi-LoRA workloads.

Additional long-context validation:

- 64 active LoRAs
- ~4k input tokens per request
- prefix caching disabled
- 1 generated token

Result:

| | Latency |
|-|-:|
| Baseline | 10.77 s/batch |
| Optimized | 8.27 s/batch |

(~23% latency reduction)

## Details

In Multi-LoRA serving, requests are grouped by adapter before executing the LoRA GEMMs. The existing kernels use the total number of tokens in the batch as the M dimension for Triton kernel configuration lookup and grid generation.

For highly fragmented workloads, this overestimates the required M dimension. For example, with 64 active adapters and one token per adapter, the kernel launch configuration is based on the global batch size even though each adapter only processes a single token.

This change:

- Tracks the maximum number of tokens assigned to any active LoRA adapter during the current forward pass.
- Uses this value for Triton kernel configuration lookup.
- Uses this value for M-dimension grid calculation in both expand and shrink kernels.

The change keeps the LoRA computation and numerical behavior unchanged while reducing redundant kernel work for fragmented adapter token distributions.


Additional benchmark details, profiler traces, Nsight Compute reports, and the RTX 5090-specific Triton configurations are available here: https://github.com/TimoSaemann/vllm-multilora-optimization

items.title: [Bugfix][Tool Parser] Preserve whitespace in HYV4 argument names
items.body:
## Overview

Preserve schema property names exactly in HYV4 streaming tool calls. For an integer property named `" count "`, streaming currently emits `{"count": "7"}` while non-streaming returns `{" count ": 7}`.

This addresses the argument-key whitespace case explicitly excluded from #60788.

## Claims

- Preserve whitespace in argument names in both completed-pair and partial-value streaming paths.
- Use the exact key for schema type lookup and keep `"count"` and `" count "` distinct, matching non-streaming parsing.

## Validation

Local results rerun on 2026-10-14 after updating to main `d5e62627a3ece4b2d045cbb2b22ac26c061c8313`, on macOS arm64 with Python 3.12.14 and xgrammar 0.2.8. The tested patch is `04aa841822468b4bcf66c90221cbd2e5df0e1ccc`. Tests use a tokenizer stub with the real vLLM parser, protocol objects, and xgrammar; no model weights are needed.

| Check | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Whitespace regression suite | 156 failed, 4 passed | 160 passed |
| Both complete test files | Not run | 428 passed |

Targeted reproduction (run the same tests with the original and patched production file):

```bash
HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 TRANSFORMERS_OFFLINE=1 .venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/tool_parsers/test_hy_v4_tool_parser.py \
  tests/tool_parsers/test_structural_tag_registry.py \
  --confcutdir=tests/tool_parsers -k whitespace -q --tb=short
```

Full-file regression:

```bash

  tests/tool_parsers/test_hy_v4_tool_parser.py \
  tests/tool_parsers/test_structural_tag_registry.py -q --tb=short

.venv/bin/pre-commit run --files \
  vllm/tool_parsers/hy_v4_tool_parser.py \
  tests/tool_parsers/test_hy_v4_tool_parser.py \
  tests/tool_parsers/test_structural_tag_registry.py
```

All applicable pre-commit hooks passed. The existing CPU Tool Parsers CI job runs this test directory; upstream CI has not been run for this change.

**Pending:** end-to-end validation with a real HYV4 model through the patched vLLM streaming service. Keep this PR in draft while H20 validation is pending. The results above establish parser/grammar behavior, not a successful model-serving run.

## Details

`_extract_streaming_incremental` strips keys in two places before schema lookup and argument tracking. This changes valid property names, can stringify non-string values, and can collapse two distinct properties. Remove those two normalizations; the structural-tag grammar already preserves exact schema keys.

Regression coverage includes whitespace-only names, seven value types, colliding trimmed names in both orders, whole/token/character chunks, both token suffix variants, emitted JSON prefixes, and state cleanup between tool calls. Four grammar cases check exact required/optional keys.

Upstream overlap was rechecked on 2026-10-14 at main `d5e62627a3ece4b2d045cbb2b22ac26c061c8313`: both key normalizations remain. No direct duplicate was found. #60788 excludes this case; #59620 handles truncated calls and inter-tag whitespace; #61205 limits grammar whitespace length. Those changes do not preserve whitespace inside argument keys.

items.title: [KV Offload] Let unfinished requests keep the chunks they will resume from
items.body:
## Summary

An offloaded chunk becomes evictable the moment its store completes, so the
prefix an *unfinished* request will resume from competes with everything else on
recency alone.

That is fine for serving, where a request either runs to completion or is
preempted and recomputed. It is not fine for a colocated RL rollout: generation
is paused for a weight update, the frozen requests touch nothing, they become
the LRU victims, and on resume they pay a full re-prefill even though their
blocks were already sitting in the CPU tier.

This adds `pin_in_flight_chunks` (default **off**) to the CPU offloading
manager. When enabled it refcounts the chunks observed by unfinished requests
and prefers evicting everything else; the refcount is released at request
finalization.

```
"kv_connector_extra_config": {"pin_in_flight_chunks": true}
```

## It cannot wedge the cache

Pinning is a preference, not a guarantee. If eviction cannot be satisfied
without touching pinned chunks, the manager retries with the original protected
set, so a cache holding nothing but in-flight chunks still admits new stores.
That fallback is covered by a test.

## Relationship to #50422

#50422 (`Session Aware Eviction Policy`) adds a new `CachePolicy` that groups a
session's blocks and evicts session-worst-first, tail-first, so a shared prefix
outlives its suffix. It orders eviction *within* the cache; it does not
distinguish a request that is still running from one that finished.

This PR is orthogonal and policy-agnostic: it is a lifetime signal in the
manager (`in flight` vs `finished`) that applies to `lru`, `arc`, a custom
policy, and to SAE if it lands. The two compose — SAE would still choose which
chunk dies first among the unpinned ones.

## Not a duplicate

Also checked: #50014 (protects unread *promotions* from speculative promotion
thrash — a different lifetime, inside the tiering path), #54327 (bounded
capacity for the filesystem tier), #38984 (SLRU policy). None of them expresses
"this request has not finished yet".

## Test plan

```
pytest tests/v1/kv_offload/cpu -q
# 161 passed, 1 skipped
# (test_swap_blocks_batch.py::test_swap_blocks_batch_default_stream fails on this
#  box with cuMemcpyBatchAsync error 1 — a CUDA kernel test, unrelated to this
#  change, on a node whose GPUs are fully allocated to another job)
```

Two new tests:

- `test_unfinished_request_chunks_survive_eviction` — an unfinished request's
  chunk survives while a finished request's chunk is evicted instead.
- `test_pinning_falls_back_when_every_chunk_is_in_flight` — a fully pinned cache
  still admits a new store.

Lint:

```
pre-commit run --files vllm/v1/kv_offload/cpu/manager.py vllm/v1/kv_offload/cpu/spec.py \
  tests/v1/kv_offload/cpu/test_manager.py docs/features/kv_offloading_usage.md
# all passed
```

No model-quality impact: eviction ordering only; no change to what is computed.

## AI assistance

Developed with AI assistance (Claude). The motivation comes from the
DeepSeek-V4.1 tech report §5.2.3, which requires exactly this lifetime rule for
async RL — in-flight rollout states are retained and released per sample as each
one completes. I reviewed every changed line, ran the tests above, and I am the
accountable submitter.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)


## Review rounds

A later adversarial round, told about the fixes already made (distinct-key scan
budget, ARC's carried `virtual_t1_size`, the capability flag replacing
signature sniffing, the two-argument call for out-of-tree policies, and the
keyword-only constructor argument) and asked for new defects, found two gaps in
what the pin actually covers.

**Fixed: a chunk still being stored was pinned only by its writer.**
`prepare_store` sorted an offered key into "not resident" or "resident and
ready". A chunk another request is *mid-store* on is neither, so it was never
recorded, and the pin counted only the writer. Two rollouts sharing a prefix —
the case this PR exists for — therefore lost the chunk the moment the writer
finished, while the reader was still unfinished. Reproduced in review and now
covered by `test_a_chunk_still_being_stored_is_pinned_by_its_second_reader`
on both policies.

The fix keeps the pin separate from cache-access accounting: pending chunks are
pinned through a new `_pin()` helper and tracked in `state.pinned_keys`, so
they do not enter `key_groups` or the reuse counters and nothing about policy
adaptation changes.

**Known limitation: a mixed GPU/CPU prefix hit does not pin the GPU-hit part.**
When part of the prefix is already in the GPU cache, the scheduler loads only
the suffix but advances `next_stored_chunk_idx` past the whole prefix
(`offloading/scheduler.py:1134`, `:1180`), so the manager never observes the
GPU-hit chunks and their CPU copies stay ordinary eviction candidates. If the
request is later preempted and those GPU blocks are lost, CPU prefix lookup
stops at the first missing chunk (`:700`), which costs the pinned suffix too.
Closing this means changing what the scheduler reports to the manager, which is
a different component's contract; this PR keeps the manager-side change and I
would rather do that separately than widen this one.

```
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/kv_offload/cpu/ -q
177 passed, 1 skipped
```

(`test_swap_blocks_batch_default_stream` fails identically on an unmodified
tree in my environment and is unrelated.)

items.title: [Bugfix] Safely resolve shared attention weights across TP > 8 and mu…
items.body:
closes #55725

1. Background & Bug Analysis
When launching models with shared/tied attention or transformer blocks (such as GLM-5.3-Flash and hybrid architectures like 
Zamba2Model
) in distributed environments across 2 nodes (e.g. 16x NVIDIA H100, tensor parallel size TP = 16):

Single-Node (TP <= 8): Ranks 0–7 load shards that contain lower-indexed hybrid layers (e.g. layer 1).
Multi-Node (TP = 16 / TP > 8): Ranks on node 2 (ranks 8–15) load shards containing higher-indexed hybrid layers, such as: 'layers.11.shared_transformer.self_attn.qkv_proj.weight'
During the weight loading phase with 
ShardedStateLoader
:

Deduplication via _filter_subtensors: _filter_subtensors(model.state_dict()) detects tensors that share the same underlying memory storage (via data_ptr()). Since layer 1 and layer 11 share the exact same shared_transformer block, the loader keeps the lower-indexed canonical key (layers.1...) and drops the higher-indexed alias key (layers.11...) from the target state_dict.
Direct Indexing Crash: When rank 8 reads its assigned checkpoint file containing layers.11.shared_transformer.self_attn.qkv_proj.weight, the code performed:
python


param_data = state_dict[key].data
Because layers.11... was filtered out of state_dict, this triggered:
text


KeyError: 'layers.11.shared_transformer.self_attn.qkv_proj.weight'
Weight Mapper & Auto Loader Limitations: 
_get_tied_embedding_params
 previously only checked VocabParallelEmbedding, ignoring tied shared_transformer blocks. Furthermore, 
WeightsMapper
 lacked a resolver to map alias layer keys to canonical parameter keys in model state dicts.
2. Architecture & Code Changes
A. 
vllm/model_executor/models/utils.py
WeightsMapper.resolve_shared_param_name(name, params_dict):
Detects shared transformer key patterns (?:^|\.)layers\.(\d+)\.shared_transformer\. and extracts the suffix (self_attn.qkv_proj.weight).
Searches params_dict for existing candidate layers (e.g. layers.1.shared_transformer...) and resolves the alias layer key to the canonical key.
WeightsMapper.resolve_param_name(name, params_dict):
Combines _map_name() (for stacked/prefix/suffix transformations) with resolve_shared_param_name().
_get_tied_embedding_params(module):
Extended submodule traversal to recognize submodules with "shared_transformer" in their prefix or with is_shared=True, registering them in aliased_params.
AutoWeightsLoader._filter_skipped(weights):
Updated so that if a checkpoint provides an alias key and its canonical key has not yet been loaded, the alias routes to the canonical parameter rather than being discarded.
B. 
vllm/model_executor/model_loader/sharded_state_loader.py
_get_subtensor_aliases(tensors):
Groups tensors by storage pointer and builds a mapping from every duplicate/subtensor filtered out by _filter_subtensors to the canonical key that was kept.
ShardedStateLoader.load_weights(model, model_config):
Computes subtensor_aliases from the raw state_dict.
Applies WeightsMapper if attached to the model (hf_to_vllm_mapper).
If target_key is not in state_dict:
Looks up target_key in subtensor_aliases.
Falls back to WeightsMapper.resolve_shared_param_name(target_key, state_dict).
Checks loaded_keys: if the canonical parameter or alias was already loaded from an earlier file/rank, it skips without error.
Avoids throwing unhandled KeyError when unexpected/duplicate keys appear.
C. Unit & Mock Multi-Rank Tests (
tests/model_executor/model_loader/test_shared_transformer_weight_loading.py
)
test_weights_mapper_resolve_shared_param_name: Tests resolution of higher-indexed layers (layer 11) to canonical layers (layer 1) with and without prefixes (model.layers...).
test_weights_mapper_resolve_param_name: Tests combining stacked weight remapping with shared parameter resolution.
test_get_subtensor_aliases_shared_transformer: Validates that _get_subtensor_aliases correctly maps layers.11 to layers.1.
test_mock_multi_rank_shared_transformer_weight_loading: Mocks multi-node loading for rank 0 and rank 8 (TP > 8), verifying that rank 8 safely loads layers.11.shared_transformer.self_attn.qkv_proj.weight into the tied storage without KeyError.
test_auto_weights_loader_shared_transformer: Tests AutoWeightsLoader loading into tied transformer modules.
3. Verification
Linter: uv tool run ruff check passed with zero errors.
Formatter: uv tool run ruff format --check confirmed full compliance with 88-character line limits.
Git Commit: Commit 41e28b4086 pushed to remote branch fix/issue-55725-glm53-weight-loading.

items.title: [Core][Spec Decode] Add lookahead-aware prefix cache hashing for EAGLE-style draft models
items.body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Implements #50438. EAGLE-family speculative decoding drops the last matched prefix-cache block and recomputes it, because the drafter's KV at the block's last position depends on the token after the block. **Lookahead block hashes** put that token into the cache key, so the block is reused only when it is proven equal. The drop costs one cache unit per hit, which is 544–1600 tokens on hybrid attention + Mamba/GDN models.

## Claims

- Prefix-cache hits with EAGLE, EAGLE3, MTP, DFlash and DSpark reach `floor((N - 1) / B) * B`, the same as without speculative decoding, instead of one unit less.
- Reuse stays correct: a hit reads the same draft KV as a cold run of the same prompt. A block whose lookahead token differs is not matched.
- Works with the local prefix cache and with Offloading, Nixl, Mooncake P2P, Mooncake Store and MultiConnector (when all children support it). Multi-module MTP and other connectors keep today's block drop.
- Model runners are unchanged; no new CPU/GPU synchronization.

## Validation

**End to end** (Qwen/Qwen3.6-27B, MTP k=4, align mode, 1x GB200; this PR at `3e7b8b93f1` vs its merge base `e58f8dde7f`, before #60533 and #60695 were merged in). `vllm bench serve --dataset-name prefix_repetition` with 16 prefixes of 6,007 tokens, 500-token suffixes, 128 output tokens, 512 prompts and concurrency 16. It ran three times (seeds 0–2), resetting the prefix cache before each run:

| | `main` | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| Prefix-cache hit rate | 72.7% | **85.0%** |
| Request throughput | 9.09 req/s | **12.43 req/s** (+37%) |
| Mean / median TTFT | 404 / 304 ms | **318 / 226 ms** |
| P99 TTFT (range over runs) | 3181–3681 ms | 2745–3725 ms |
| Acceptance length | 2.24–2.30 | 2.24–2.28 |
| GSM8K 5-shot, 1,319 q, max 4096 tokens | 0.4359 | 0.4359 |
| GSM8K acceptance length | 4.11 | 4.10 |

GSM8K is a parity check: its prompts are shorter than one cache unit, and about half of this chat model's completions-API answers fail the parser on both sides. With `OffloadingConnector` (single run), the hit rate rose from 72.7% to 85.0% and throughput from 8.93 to 11.26 req/s, with the same GSM8K accuracy and acceptance.

**Hit length** (Qwen/Qwen3.5-2B, MTP k=1, unit 544, 1,367-token prompt sent twice, same revision): `main` without spec decode 1088, `main` with MTP 544, this PR 1088.

**Draft-KV correctness.** Greedy output cannot reveal a wrong draft KV (the target verifies every draft), so the check compares the KV itself. The engine runs in-process and is stepped manually. Right after the step in which a request first hits the prefix cache, the KV of its hit blocks is read and compared per position with a cold run of the same prompt. Async scheduling is on; the hits include ones landing in the same step that computes the hit blocks.

| Model | Lookahead (this PR): block-end draft slots | Negative control (`disable_eagle_block_drop`, stale lookahead token) |
|---|---|---|
| Qwen3-8B + EAGLE3 (k=3) | 0.09–0.14 | **7.55** |
| Qwen3.5-2B, MTP | 0.19 | **14.53** |
| Qwen3.5-4B, MTP | 0.29 | — |

Values are the max abs diff in bf16.

**Tests** (GB200 via Slurm, current head `5f36a6cd20`):

```bash
python -m pytest tests/v1/core
python -m pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit tests/v1/streaming_input/test_scheduler_streaming.py \
  tests/models/kimi_k3/test_kda_metadata.py -k "not ray"
python -m pytest tests/v1/e2e/spec_decode/mtp/qwen3_5/test_mtp.py \
  tests/v1/e2e/spec_decode/mtp/qwen3_5/test_rejected_placeholders.py \
  tests/v1/e2e/general/test_mamba_prefix_cache.py
```

- `tests/v1/core`: 1029 passed, 0 failed. Errors are environmental: engine start-up with GPU 0 occupied by an earlier engine in the same process (2), and the `vllm` CLI missing from `PATH` on the node (2).
- Connector suites: 2220 passed. The 6 failures do not use speculative decoding: int8 `scaled_mm` is unsupported on GB200 (2), GPU memory not released by an earlier `LLM` in the same process (2), and `test_cpu_offloading` (2).
- E2E (one visible GPU): 8 passed: Qwen3.5 MTP correctness, `test_qwen3_5_mtp_prefix_cache_reuses_last_safe_block` (OffloadingConnector), rejected placeholders (2), and Mamba prefix cache MRV1 / MRV1 async / MRV2 / MRV2 async.
- `pre-commit` (incl. mypy) passes.

<details><summary>Earlier-revision evaluations (not re-run on this head)</summary>

Qwen/Qwen3.5-2B, MTP, real `OffloadingConnector`, GSM8K 200 questions, 10-shot, two passes with APC reset between passes: accuracy 0.515 / 0.515, 0 output mismatches, acceptance length 1.925.

Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct + `nm-testing/Llama3_2_1B_speculator.eagle3`, `NixlConnector` P/D with the toy proxy, GSM8K 1,319 questions, 5-shot, two passes: accuracy 0.3215 / 0.3207 (385 output mismatches between passes), acceptance length 2.077.

</details>

## Details

**Design**

- `is_lookahead_block_hashing_enabled` (`v1/core/kv_cache_utils.py`) turns the mode on when all of these hold; otherwise the existing drop is unchanged:
  - `SpeculativeConfig.use_eagle_block_drop()`;
  - `VllmConfig.num_prefill_lookahead_tokens == 1`, because the key proves only the next token;
  - prefix caching, or a KV connector whose `supports_lookahead_block_hashes` is true.
- `get_request_block_hasher(..., use_lookahead_block_hashes=True)` emits the hash for a block ending at `e` only once token `e` exists, with `(block_keys, token_e, token_e_keys)` as extra keys. All KV cache groups share these hashes, since a request has one hit length across groups.
- Blocks are cached at allocation, as without lookahead hashes. At request finish, the block whose lookahead token is the last sampled one is cached from `update_from_output`.
- The scheduler clears `use_eagle_block_drop` in this mode, so the last-block drop, Mamba checkpoint back-off and replay-boundary shift are skipped.
- Content-addressed connectors (Offloading, Mooncake Store) save only blocks covered by `request.block_hashes`, which lag the computed tokens by up to one block. Mooncake Store pins a final save job at request finish for that block. Nixl and Mooncake P2P transfer the request's own blocks; for Mamba models they keep truncating the prefill side at `h(N-1)`.
- MultiConnector's children are built from per-child configs, so the factory pushes the parent's decision down to every child.

**Why it is correct.** For a block `[s, e)` the key proves the prefix through `e - 1` and the token at `e`. The drafter writes the draft KV at `e - 1` (input `(h_{e-1}, token e)`) in the step that prefills or samples token `e`. The hash exists only once token `e` is in `all_token_ids`, which never holds draft or in-flight tokens. Caching at allocation therefore never exposes a block whose draft KV is not written by the end of that step. Later reads are ordered after that write on the GPU, as for regular prefix caching.

**Limitations**

- Multi-module MTP (`num_nextn_predict_layers > 1`, k ≥ 2) keeps the block drop. Its module j at position p reads token p + j, and during decode it can read unverified drafts.
- Engines sharing a content-addressed store must use the same mode. KV events keep `main`'s shape; lookahead extra keys are `(block_keys, lookahead_token_id, lookahead_keys)`, and no field marks the scheme for external consumers. When cache blocks are coarser than `prefix_match_unit`, an event carries one extra-key tuple per block, as on `main`.
- Hybrid models lose the hit when a prompt diverges exactly at the producer's last retained Mamba boundary. After a request finishes, align mode keeps its Mamba state only at the last aligned boundary of its prompt. The lookahead key then falls back one unit, where no state is kept, so the hit is 0; the drop on `main` keeps that unit's state and hits one unit. `prefix_match_unit` does not change this.
  <details><summary>Reproducer (Qwen3.5-2B, MTP k=1, unit 544)</summary>

  P1 = S + a, P2 = S + b with |S| = 1088 and a[0] != b[0], |a| = |b| = 279; requests run one after another: P1, P2, P1.

  | | P2 hit | P1 repeat hit |
  |---|---|---|
  | `main`, no spec decode | 1088 | 1088 |
  | `main`, MTP (block drop) | 544 | 544 |
  | this PR, MTP | 0 | 1088 |
  | this PR, MTP, `prefix_match_unit=32` | 0 | 1344 |

  </details>
- Model Runner V1 skips the whole drafter when a request exceeds the drafter's `max_model_len`; not handled since V1 is being removed.

<details><summary>Changes since the first review</summary>

- Merged `main` (adapted to `use_eagle_block_drop`, `num_prefill_lookahead`, Mamba checkpoint back-off, tagged extra keys, Mooncake store-job pinning, `get_transfer_results`, SWA bounded-replay window loads).
- Renamed to "lookahead block hashes".
- Removed the per-step draft KV ACK, the platform gate, the drafter-skip freeze and the V1 deferred-finalize changes; both model runners match `main`.
- Dropped the publication fence (`Request.num_publishable_block_hashes`, output-time publication, Mamba sub-block special case); blocks are cached at allocation, validated with the draft-KV check above.
- Folded the separate lookahead hasher into `get_request_block_hasher`. It had resumed incremental hashing from the last multimodal item (the pre-#51694 logic) and could drop an earlier overlapping item from the extra keys.
- Dropped per-block KV event emission and `BlockStored.hash_block_size`.
- Merged `main` with #60533 (hybrid Mamba prefix-cache boundaries) and #60695 (Mooncake partial tails). The PR's prompt-boundary helper is replaced by `get_mamba_prefill_checkpoint_position`, which lands on the last aligned boundary below the logits token once the drop is cleared. Two merge fixes: `find_longest_cache_hit_per_group` no longer widens the lookup by the EAGLE drop margin under lookahead hashes (new test), and the Mooncake finish-time lookahead save uses the new store-job pinning.
- `test_mamba_prefix_cache`: prompts whose length is a multiple of the block keep `main`'s split; prompts with a partial tail reuse one more block. The MRV2 cases spawn their subprocess like the MRV1 ones, since a forked child cannot re-initialize CUDA after earlier GPU tests in the same session.
- Other fixes: replay-boundary retention dropped the last prompt block after the merge; P/D + Mamba + MTP applied the last prompt token twice; non-EAGLE full-attention groups used the wrong prompt-tail boundary.
- Addressed review comments (boolean ACK and publication fence removed, `self.hash_block_size`).

</details>

<details><summary>Duplicate-work check</summary>

No open implementation PR references #50438 or adds the successor token to the prefix-cache key.

- #44986 skips the pop during prefill by phase; this PR makes reuse conditional on a content-based key.
- #45614 and #48375 repair or preserve the conservative Mamba back-off; this PR makes it unnecessary when the boundary token is proven equal.
- #39171 addresses hybrid coordinator drop behavior without changing the key.

```bash
gh issue view 50438 --repo vllm-project/vllm --comments
```
