items.title: [MooncakeStore] Report KV load tier in cache events
items.body:
## Purpose

Report the actual MooncakeStore replica tier in KV cache events.

Mooncake already exposes whether a loaded replica is memory-backed or disk-backed, but this information was not propagated to `BlockStored` events. This change maps:

* memory-backed replica → `CPU`
* disk-backed replica → `STORAGE`
* unknown tier → `None`

Successful events are emitted only for blocks that actually load successfully. Scheduler lookup and connector protocol behavior are unchanged.

## Test Plan

Run the focused MooncakeStore worker tests:

```bash
python -m pytest \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_store_worker.py \
  -v \
  --confcutdir=tests/v1/kv_connector/unit \
  -k "test_recv_thread_emits_tiered_events_after_rotation_and_split or test_recv_thread_emits_unknown_tier_with_no_medium or test_recv_thread_does_not_emit_event_for_failed_load or test_recv_thread_skips_tier_lookup_when_events_and_logging_disabled"
```

Also run an end-to-end MooncakeStore smoke test on the DGX/A100 setup to exercise the real replica-tier lookup path.

## Test Results

### Focused unit tests

```text
4 passed, 112 deselected in 7.02s
```

Validated:

* memory-backed replicas map to `CPU`
* disk-backed replicas map to `STORAGE`
* unknown tier leaves `medium` unset
* failed loads do not emit successful `BlockStored` events
* replica-tier lookup is skipped when both KV events and tier logging are disabled
* block hashes remain correctly aligned through rotation and disk-budget splitting

### Integration smoke test

Ran vLLM with MooncakeStore on an A100 using a 256 MB embedded Mooncake segment.

A real Mooncake-backed reload reported:

```text
batch_keys=35
memory_keys=35
disk_keys=0
unknown_keys=0
success_keys=35
failed_keys=0
bytes_by_tier={'memory': 82575360, 'disk': 0, 'unknown': 0}
```

This confirms that the runtime replica metadata path correctly identifies real memory-backed loads.

Disk persistence was also exercised successfully, but a disk-only reload could not be observed with the embedded-store setup because the in-memory replica remains available. A true disk-backed reload would require a standalone-store configuration.

The focused unit tests directly validate the disk-replica → `STORAGE` event mapping.

items.title: [KV Offload] Add admission policy framework and backpressure adapter
items.body:
## Summary

This PR implements the `TieringAdmissionPolicy` framework described in [RFC #53485](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/53485), building on the admission-policy skeleton in [#51576](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/51576).

It places the existing per-tier backpressure detectors from [#50045](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/50045) behind one admission gate for cascade stores and promotions. The production configuration preserves the existing backpressure decisions while making admission a policy-level extension point.

## Functionality

- Add `TieringAdmissionPolicy`, `AlwaysAdmitPolicy`, `BackpressureAdmissionPolicy`, and `AdmissionPolicyFactory`.
- Evaluate cascade admission before primary-tier pinning and job-ID allocation.
- Evaluate promotion admission before primary allocation.
- Route admitted-job completion and cache-reset lifecycle events through the policy.
- Reuse the existing backpressure detectors, drop accounting, labels, metrics, and transition logging.
- Move backpressure metric definitions and collection into the policy.
- Update P2P and KVCR callers to handle rejected store jobs.
- Add policy and manager-wiring tests.

The policy receives plain admission inputs (`keys`, `tier_idx`, and `is_promotion`). Promotion admission hooks run once for the real batched job, while `JobMetadata` remains defined by the manager and is referenced by policies through `TYPE_CHECKING`.

## Related work

- [RFC #51240: Tiering Admission Policy Design](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/51240)
- [RFC #53485: Reconcile Backpressure Admission](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/53485)
- [#51576: Add TieringAdmissionPolicy skeleton](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/51576)
- [#50045: Back-pressure detection and remediation](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/50045)

# Note

Model evaluation is not applicable. This changes KV-cache offload admission only; rejected cascades fall back to recomputation and do not change model outputs.

items.title: [Core] Add waiting-queue-informed KV cache eviction
items.body:
## Purpose

Related to #48485.

When prefix caching is enabled, ordinary LRU eviction can discard blocks that
ready waiting requests are about to reuse. Those requests then recompute a
prefix even though evicting a different cached block would have kept the
allocation feasible.

This PR adds an allocator-local, best-effort eviction hint:

- the scheduler supplies a bounded, read-only snapshot of the ready `waiting`
  queue to each `allocate_slots()` transaction;
- `KVCacheManager` resolves matching block IDs lazily, memoizes them for that
  transaction, and clears the context in `finally`;
- `BlockPool` preserves existing LRU behavior unless an allocation would scan
  a cached candidate, then prefers non-retained free blocks while preserving
  order within the non-retained and retained groups;
- allocation, eviction, ref-count, metrics, and event ownership remain in the
  existing BlockPool path, and lookup/allocation exceptions still propagate.

The first slice intentionally excludes `skipped_waiting`, queue reordering,
block pinning/reservation, connector I/O, and new production metrics.

## Test Plan

```bash
# Focused eviction-hint behavior and scheduler wiring.
python -m pytest -q \
  tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_utils.py \
  tests/v1/core/test_prefix_caching.py \
  tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py \
  -k 'eviction_hint or popleft_n_with_hint or has_cached_block_in_first_n or block_pool_resolves_eviction_hint or block_pool_does_not_resolve_eviction_hint or allocate_slots_propagates_error_and_clears_hint_context or waiting_eviction_hint_resolver'

# Complete directly affected core suites.
python -m pytest -q \
  tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_utils.py \
  tests/v1/core/test_prefix_caching.py \
  tests/v1/core/test_single_type_kv_cache_manager.py

# Repository lint/format checks for all changed files.
python -m ruff check <changed-files>
python -m ruff format --check <changed-files>
```

The registered single-GPU integration plan uses Qwen3-0.6B, prefix caching,
priority scheduling, two running guard requests, an exact 320-block KV cache,
and five alternating fresh-server baseline/proposed pairs. It records exact
target-prefix evictions, cache-hit tokens, request-level TTFT/E2E latency,
preemptions, completed tokens/s, scheduler CPU time per step, GPU telemetry,
and paired 95% bootstrap confidence intervals.

## Test Result

- Focused eviction-hint/context/provider/wiring tests: **14 passed**.
- Complete KV-cache utils, prefix-caching, and single-type-manager suites:
  **210 passed**.
- Ruff lint: **passed**; Ruff format check: **9 files already formatted**.
- `compileall` and `git diff --check`: **passed**.
- Five-pair Qwen3-0.6B A/B on one assigned RTX 4090: **BENEFICIAL**.
  Baseline evicted both target prefixes in 5/5 pairs; proposed evicted none and
  restored 192 cached tokens in 5/5 pairs. Mean scheduler CPU time was
  0.05790 ms/step baseline versus 0.06044 ms/step proposed (+4.38%, below the
  registered 5% ceiling). Target TTFT was effectively unchanged and its paired
  95% bootstrap CI crossed zero, so no latency improvement is claimed.

The local full scheduler file reached **120 passed** before its 36 multimodal
cases were blocked by a binary mismatch between the available precompiled
PyTorch and the current torchvision pin. The new scheduler wiring test itself
passes; the upstream CI matrix remains the authoritative multimodal check.

The worst-case selector microbenchmark (50,000 free blocks, 45,000 selected,
99% retained) measured 17.0 ms p95 for the hinted path versus 3.66 ms for plain
LRU. This is the deliberately pathological `O(F)` fallback bound; the paired
integration run above is used to quantify scheduler-step overhead in the
target workload.

For the paired run, both revisions used identical Qwen request warmups. The
public kernel configuration disabled optional JIT/CuTeDSL startup warmups and
FlashInfer autotune, and a benchmark-only shim skipped the unrelated
MiniMax-M3 multimodal warmup. These settings are benchmark-environment choices,
not changes in this PR.

items.title: [Bugfix] Fix TOCTOU race in KV block allocator causing prefix-cache block theft
items.body:
## Summary

Fixes #37076

When the V1 scheduler processes multiple WAITING requests in a single scheduling step, a **use-after-free / TOCTOU window** in the KV block allocator allows one request to silently steal another request's cached prefix block, causing KV data corruption (token bleed between requests).

## Root Cause

The scheduler loop calls two methods for each waiting request:

```python
for req in waiting_requests:
    computed_blocks, n = manager.get_computed_blocks(req)   # Step 1: lookup
    ...
    manager.allocate_slots(req, ..., computed_blocks)        # Step 2: pin + alloc
```

Between Step 1 and Step 2, other requests in the loop are also processed. The bug:

1. `get_computed_blocks(req_A)` finds cached `block_X` (`ref_cnt=0`, eviction candidate in the free queue)
2. Before `allocate_slots(req_A)` pins it via `touch()`, req_B's `allocate_new_blocks()` **steals** `block_X` from the free queue and erases its hash via `_maybe_evict_cached_block()`
3. `allocate_slots(req_A)` now `touch()`es a block that belongs to req_B → **req_A reads req_B's KV data**

```
Timeline (single-threaded scheduler loop):
  get_computed_blocks(A)   →  block_X found (ref_cnt=0)
                                              ← TOCTOU WINDOW OPENS
  get_computed_blocks(B)   →  no cache hit
  allocate_new_blocks(B)   →  steals block_X from free queue!
                                              ← block_X now has B's data
  allocate_slots(A)        →  touches stale block_X → TOKEN BLEED
```

## Fix

**Pre-touch (pin) cached blocks immediately inside `get_computed_blocks()`**, closing the TOCTOU window before any other request can run.

- Added `touch_computed_blocks()` and `release_computed_blocks()` to `KVCacheCoordinator`
- `get_computed_blocks()` calls `touch_computed_blocks()` right after `find_longest_cache_hit()` so `ref_cnt` goes 0→1 and blocks are removed from the free queue
- `allocate_slots()` on the **failure path** (not enough free blocks) calls `release_computed_blocks()` to undo the pin — no ref-count leak
- `allocate_new_computed_blocks()` no longer calls `touch()` (blocks already pinned); handles the sliding-window skipped-block case by freeing pre-touched skipped blocks before slicing

### Why the free-block budget check is unchanged

Before the fix: `num_blocks_to_allocate = num_new_blocks + N` (N evictable computed blocks) is compared against F free blocks (which include those N blocks). Equivalent to `num_new_blocks > F - N`.

After the fix: pre-touch removes N blocks from the free queue, so `get_num_free_blocks() = F - N`, and `_get_num_evictable_blocks() = 0`. Check becomes `num_new_blocks > F - N`. **Identical condition** — scheduling decisions are unchanged.

## Test Plan

- Added regression test `test_prefix_cache_block_not_stolen_between_get_and_alloc` that directly reproduces the TOCTOU scenario and verifies the prefix block's `ref_cnt == 1` after `get_computed_blocks()`
- All 56 unit tests pass (`test_prefix_caching.py` + `test_single_type_kv_cache_manager.py`)
- All pre-commit hooks pass (ruff, mypy, typos, SPDX, etc.)

items.title: [Bugfix][KV Offload] Advertise complete chunks as retrievable cache units
items.body:
## Purpose

Fixes #57159. Thanks to @nilig for the report and producer/consumer analysis.

An offloaded complete chunk is retrieved by its final block hash, but its
self-describing event currently advertises the constituent GPU-block hashes
as separate cache units. A request sharing only an interior prefix can
therefore appear to hit the CPU cache even though lookup misses.

This change advertises each complete chunk with its final hash and complete
token count as `block_size`. `BlockRemoved` uses the same saved chunk hash.
The preceding chunk's hash remains the parent. Existing tests and the option
documentation are updated to the corrected representation.

### Scope and compatibility

- Only self-describing complete-chunk event metadata changes. Cache keys,
  allocation, lookup, transfers, eviction, and generation are unchanged.
- Single-block chunks, opt-out/placeholder behavior, and partial recurrent
  tails retain their existing representation.
- No wire-schema field or default changes. Consumers must nevertheless honor
  the complete retrieval unit instead of splitting it into partial hits.
- The separate consumer issue llm-d/llm-d-router#2889 is not fixed here.

### Duplicate-work check

On 2026-09-17, the issue had no assignee or claim comments. PR searches for
`57159`, `offloading events`, and retrieval/chunk granularity found no direct
implementation. Related #52103 changes event provenance and metadata
lifetime, but the inspected patch retains per-GPU-block granularity. This
patch is limited to retrieval granularity; happy to coordinate merge order
and the event contract with that work.

## Test Plan

The new CPU-level regression pairs the actual `CPUOffloadingManager` with
`OffloadingEventsTracker`: a stored 64-token chunk is queried with shared
prefixes of 0, 16, 32, 48, and 64 tokens, using hash sizes of 4 and 16 tokens.
Additional cases check that overlapping chunks store/remove distinct hashes.
Existing tests retain coverage for parents, groups, promotion, placeholders,
and partial tails. GPU worker tests cover actual CPU/GPU transfers.

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector/test_events.py -q

VLLM_KV_EVENTS_USE_INT_BLOCK_HASHES=0 .venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector/test_events.py -q

.venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector \
  tests/v1/kv_offload/cpu/test_manager.py \
  tests/v1/kv_offload/tiering/test_tiering_offloading.py \
  tests/v1/kv_offload/tiering/test_kvcr_tier.py -q

.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/kv_offload/cpu/test_gpu_worker.py -q

.venv/bin/python -m pre_commit run --files \
  vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/offloading/events.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector/test_events.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector/test_scheduler.py \
  docs/features/kv_offloading_usage.md
```

## Test Result

Validated against main `2d8a5c5741dedb3559d26ce95fa894771cffa881`:

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Original existing event suite | 23 passed |
| Initial reproduction on original implementation | 6 expected failures, 4 passing controls |
| Patched event suite (includes 13 new cases) | 36 passed |
| Patched event suite with byte hashes | 36 passed |
| Connector/scheduler/CPU manager/tiering regression | 580 passed, 1 collection skip |
| GPU worker regression | 39 passed, 1 skip |
| All 13 new cases with original production file restored | 9 expected failures, 4 passing controls |
| Applicable pre-commit hooks and `git diff --check` | Passed |

The focused tests are included in the 580 count, not additional unique tests.
The two skips are missing optional `kvcr` and a ROCm-only case on NVIDIA.

Environment: RTX PRO 5000 72 GB Blackwell, Python 3.10.12, Torch 2.13.0+cu130.
Current-main Python source was installed editably using existing vLLM 0.27.1
precompiled native artifacts; this was not a fresh native build. Source paths
and all tracked regular-file hashes were verified. Tests ran offline.

Model evaluation: not run. This patch changes event metadata rather than
model computation or cache contents; no generation-quality, throughput, or

items.title: [AuxOutput] Keep routed experts while a KV cache tier caches their blocks

labels.name: ready
labels.description: ONLY add when PR is ready to merge/full CI is needed

items.body:
## Purpose

Keep routed-expert (R3) outputs while a KV cache tier (the GPU prefix cache, or CPU offload) can return a hit on their block, and cap prefix hits at blocks whose outputs exist. This replaces the earlier store cache-policy approach of this PR, which is reverted.

### Problems on `main`

- **CPU offload crash.** R3 with `OffloadingConnector` crashes the worker when the whole prompt is a CPU hit:

  ```
  auxiliary output capture is not contiguous: expected=1184, actual=1199
  ```

  `_update_waiting_for_remote_kvs` resumes at `num_tokens - 1`, which is not on a block boundary.
- **Stale hits.** The SHM store evicts by LRU independently of the KV cache, so a KV hit can outlive the routed experts of its blocks.
- **Store overflow.** The store raises `cannot retain` once referenced objects exceed `max_bytes`. #62044 reports this at full KV.

### Design

All changes live in the existing aux output classes.

- **Retaining** (`AuxOutputSchedulerConnector`). When a request finishes or is preempted, the connector retains its GPU-cached full blocks (the full-attention group, else group 0). Their hashes go out as `retained_block_hashes` in the same metadata that releases the request's own references; the worker retains before it releases.
- **Releasing** (`released_block_hashes`), driven by `update_kv_cache_events`.
  - CPU residency is counted from the connector's CPU `BlockStored`/`BlockRemoved` events. A block the CPU tier evicts, and no other tier holds, is released at once.
  - A block the GPU evicts with no tier reporting it may still sit in a KV connector without residency events (`MooncakeStoreConnector`, LMCache). It stays retained in an LRU of up to `num_blocks` such blocks; the oldest is released beyond that. The scheduler therefore knows exactly which outputs exist, for every KV connector.
  - GPU evictions are processed in the same step's metadata, before the worker stores new outputs.
  - Residency is looked up in the tracked group's own block pool, which HiSparse replaces with a host pool.
  - Blocks of a pending async load stay retained until the request is scheduled.
- **Hit cap.** `max_cache_hit(request)` is the longest prefix of full blocks that are GPU-cached or retained, at most `num_tokens - 1`. The scheduler only calls the connector's `cap_local_hit` and `cap_external_hit`.
  - A local hit past it is dropped and recomputed. With a full-attention group this never happens: every GPU-cached block is retained or held by a running request. Only partial-block hits (`--prefix-match-unit` finer than the block size) and sparse sliding-window hits reach it; a Mamba or sliding-window hit cannot be cut at another boundary. `KVCacheManager` is unchanged.
  - External hits are trimmed to it, so a block whose outputs left the LRU is recomputed instead of failing the read. The total is aligned down to the block size, where capture resumes; this fixes the crash above.
- **Shorter external prefixes.** A trimmed external hit reaches the KV connector as a smaller `num_external_tokens` in `update_state_after_alloc`. Not every connector can load that, so `KVConnectorBase_V1.external_load_alignment` says what it can:
  - an int: the unit a shorter prefix must end on, and the scheduler aligns the trim down to it;
  - `None` (the default, so out-of-tree connectors are safe): only the whole hit, and a trimmed hit becomes 0 and is recomputed. Mamba models also trim to 0.

  | Connector | `external_load_alignment` | Change |
  |---|---|---|
  | `OffloadingConnector`, `SimpleCPUOffloadConnector` | 1 | none: they already load a shorter prefix |
  | `MooncakeStoreConnector` | 1 | asserted the whole hit; now loads the accepted prefix and drops the tail key boundary |
  | `LMCacheConnectorV1` | LMCache chunk size | asserted the whole hit; the wrapper now shortens the load spec. LMCache retrieves whole chunks, so an unaligned prefix fails to load |
  | in-tree `LMCacheMPConnector` | chunk size | loads the accepted chunks and frees the lookup locks of the rest |
  | `MultiConnector` | least common multiple of its connectors, `None` if any is `None` | |
  | others, including the `lmcache` package's `LMCacheMPConnector` | `None` | |
- **Store growth** (`BlockObjectStore`, SHM). When new objects do not fit after evicting every unreferenced one, the arena grows instead of raising, and logs:

  ```
  Auxiliary output store grows past max_bytes to <bytes> bytes: running requests and KV cache tiers reference all <n> objects.
  ```

  Referenced objects belong to running requests, to blocks a KV cache tier holds, or to the LRU, so growth is bounded by the KV tiers. R3 rows are about 0.4% of a token's KV on Qwen3-30B-A3B. The default `max_bytes` is now twice the KV cache: one half for blocks the GPU caches, one half for the LRU. GPU-only serving does not grow it.
- **Resets.**
  - A prefix-cache reset releases all retained blocks, even if the KV connector reset fails. The worker releases them in the old generation before switching.
  - `reset_connector_cache` drops CPU residency and releases every retained block no GPU block holds, including the LRU.
- **KV events.** With aux outputs enabled, KV cache events are turned on with `publisher="null"` if they were off; nothing is published. `self_describing_kv_events` also defaults to true in `kv_connector_extra_config` (and in each `MultiConnector` child's), so each CPU chunk names every block it holds.

### Limitations

- **KV connectors without residency events.** `OffloadingConnector` and `SimpleCPUOffloadConnector` (CPU mode) report CPU `BlockStored`/`BlockRemoved`, so their blocks stay retained while offloaded. `MooncakeStoreConnector`, `LMCacheConnectorV1`, `LMCacheMPConnector` and `SimpleCPUOffloadConnector` in disk mode do not: their external hits reach back only as far as the LRU, and older blocks are recomputed. The LRU holds as many blocks as the GPU KV cache.
- **Trims to a connector's unit.** With LMCache a trimmed hit loses up to one chunk (256 tokens by default) more than with a block-granular connector. A connector without `external_load_alignment` recomputes a trimmed hit in full.
- **In-tree `LMCacheMPConnector` is not covered end to end.** vLLM prefers the MP connector shipped by `lmcache` (0.4.7 and later); it does not declare a load unit, so its trimmed hits are recomputed (tested below). The in-tree fallback is used only with `lmcache` 0.4.4, which fails at startup with this vLLM (`expected storage_offset 0`) with or without this change.
- **Mooncake object store.** `MooncakeBlockObjectStore` (#57968) ignores retain/release and has a deployment-sized pool.
- **Partial-block hits** (`--prefix-match-unit` finer than the block size) are recomputed: a local one in full, a CPU one on Mamba hybrids too. Default block hashing has no partial blocks.

## Test Plan

```bash
pytest tests/distributed/aux_output_connector/test_store.py tests/config/test_aux_output_config.py \
  tests/model_executor/test_routed_experts_capture.py tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py \
  tests/v1/core/test_prefix_caching.py tests/v1/core/test_async_scheduler.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_store_scheduler.py tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_store_connector.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_lmcache_connector.py tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_multi_connector.py
```

New tests:

- retaining and releasing across the GPU and CPU tiers;
- pending-load protection;
- releases on connector reset and on prefix-cache reset;
- the worker retaining in the sending generation;
- store growth with a warning;
- local and external hit capping, including to a connector's load unit and to 0 for whole-hit-only connectors;
- the LRU of evicted blocks no tier reports;
- `MooncakeStoreScheduler` and the `LMCacheConnectorV1` wrapper loading a shorter accepted prefix;
- `MultiConnector` combining its connectors' load units;
- evicted blocks released in the evicting step through a real scheduler.

E2E: Qwen3-30B-A3B on H200, `--enable-return-routed-experts --enable-prefix-caching`, 256 GPU blocks, `--max-num-seqs 8`, default `max_bytes`. Each round sends the same prompt after a flood of other prompts and compares its routed experts with round 0.

## Test Result

- **Unit tests:** all pass: 586 in the first six files (the two PP scheduler tests on 4 GPUs), and the KV connector files. `test_multi_example_connector_consistency` needs the gated `meta-llama/Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct` and could not run here.
- **E2E:** floods of 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8 and 12 prompts (63 requests per setup) unless noted. "Trimmed" is the hit the KV connector reported versus what the scheduler accepted.

  | Setup | Requests OK | Hit tokens per round | Trimmed |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | GPU only, flood 12 | 56/56 | — | — |
  | `OffloadingConnector` 8 GB | 63/63 | local 464 + CPU 720, then CPU 1184 | none (CPU events keep blocks retained) |
  | `OffloadingConnector` without its KV events (stands in for a connector without events) | 63/63 | CPU 1184 twice, 960, then 0 | 1184 → 960 |
  | `SimpleCPUOffloadConnector` CPU | 63/63 | local 464 + CPU 720, then CPU 1184 | none |
  | `SimpleCPUOffloadConnector` disk | 63/63 | disk 1184 twice, 960 twice, then 0 | 1184 → 960 |
  | `MooncakeStoreConnector` (RDMA) | 63/63 | Mooncake 1184 twice, 960, then 0 | 1184 → 960 |
  | `LMCacheConnectorV1`, chunk 256, CPU backend | 63/63 | local 464 + LMCache 560, LMCache 1024 twice, 768, then 0 | 1024 → 768 (R3 cap 960, aligned to the chunk) |
  | same, `save_unfull_chunk` | 63/63 | same | 1199 → 1024 and 1024 → 768 |
  | `LMCacheMPConnector` (`lmcache` 0.5.6 built against this torch, chunk 256) | 63/63 | local 464 + LMCache 560, LMCache 1024 twice, then 0 | 1024 → 0 (R3 cap 960; whole-hit-only connector) |
  | `main`, same, without R3 (reference for hit tokens) | 63/63 | ..., then LMCache 1024 in every round | |
  | `main`, `OffloadingConnector` | — | worker crash (`not contiguous`) | |
  | `main`, `MooncakeStoreConnector` / `SimpleCPUOffloadConnector` disk / `LMCacheConnectorV1` | — | engine dies on the first external hit: `auxiliary output object does not exist` | |

  Routed experts match round 0 for every row read from the store. After a trimmed hit, the recomputed tail (from token 992 here) can differ: a recomputed suffix does not match a full prefill bitwise even without this change; on `main` with no KV connector, a 960-token GPU prefix hit already changes rows 960 to 1198. The store grew (with its warning) only where a CPU tier keeps blocks retained: 3 times with `SimpleCPUOffloadConnector` CPU, as with `OffloadingConnector` before. No KV load failures in these runs. items.title: [Bugfix][KV Connector][Mooncake] Apply multi-module MTP prefill backoff in P/D
items.body:
## Purpose

Fix Model Runner V2 multi-module MTP with Mooncake P/D disaggregation.

The multi-module MTP scheduler exposes `VllmConfig.num_prefill_lookahead_tokens`
so the decoder can recompute the trailing lookahead window locally. The NIXL
connector already applies this backoff, but `MooncakeConnector` still transfers
the full prompt for dense MTP requests and does not truncate the producer-side
prefill request.

For example, with a prompt of 10 tokens and a three-token MTP lookahead,
Mooncake currently transfers 10 tokens while the decoder-side MTP path expects
the last 2 tokens to be recomputed locally. This can leave unverified MTP draft
KV in the P/D transfer state and make the decoder reuse KV that it does not
rebuild.

This change:

- applies the same prefill backoff as NIXL when calculating Mooncake's remote
  prefill token count;
- truncates the same trailing tokens on the producer before prefix-cache lookup;
- preserves the existing one-token Mamba backoff and leaves ordinary dense
  requests unchanged; and
- keeps the truncation idempotent across preemption and rescheduling.

This follows up on the multi-layer MTP P/D cache correction in #55055.

## Test Plan

```bash
pytest -q \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_connector_hybrid_mamba.py
python -m py_compile \
  vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/mooncake/mooncake_connector.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_connector_hybrid_mamba.py
```

The regression tests cover the dense multi-module MTP P/D case, verify that
both sides use the same lookahead backoff, and confirm that ordinary dense
requests keep the existing full-prompt behavior. Existing hybrid Mamba tests
cover the unchanged one-token behavior.

## Test Result

- `11 passed`
- An end-to-end multi-module MTP P/D accuracy run has not been performed.

items.title: [Feature] Add `response_prefix` parameter to audio transcription/translation endpoints
items.body:
## Summary

- Adds an optional `response_prefix` field to both `/v1/audio/transcriptions` and `/v1/audio/translations` endpoints
- When provided, the text is injected into the assistant turn of the prompt so the model continues generation from that point — as if it had already produced those words
- Enables callers to implement streaming-quality transcription over REST without WebSocket infrastructure

This implements **Option A** from RFC #35908.

### How it works

For Qwen3-ASR, `response_prefix` is appended after the `<asr_text>` tag in the assistant turn, matching the prompt shape used by the [Qwen3-ASR SDK's `streaming_transcribe`](https://github.com/QwenLM/Qwen3-ASR/blob/main/qwen_asr/inference/qwen3_asr.py#L657):

```
<|im_start|>assistant
language English<asr_text>{response_prefix}
```

A caller implements the streaming loop as:

```
1. POST audio[0:2s], response_prefix=""               → T1
2. POST audio[0:4s], response_prefix=rollback(T1)     → T2
3. POST audio[0:6s], response_prefix=rollback(T2)     → T3
...
```

The caller handles audio accumulation, rollback, and prefix capping — the server just runs a single transcription with the given prompt.

### Changes

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `vllm/config/speech_to_text.py` | Add `response_prefix: str = ""` to `SpeechToTextParams` |
| `vllm/entrypoints/speech_to_text/transcription/protocol.py` | Add `response_prefix` to `TranscriptionRequest` and pass it through |
| `vllm/entrypoints/speech_to_text/translation/protocol.py` | Add `response_prefix` to `TranslationRequest` and pass it through |
| `vllm/model_executor/models/qwen3_asr.py` | Sanitize `response_prefix` and append after `<asr_text>` tag in the assistant turn |

`response_prefix` rides on the existing `SpeechToTextParams` dataclass plumbing (the refactor from #36268), so no `SupportsTranscription` interface change is needed and other ASR backends pick up the new field as a no-op default `""` automatically.

### Companion PR

This sits on top of the same Qwen3-ASR prompt-handling surface as [#35415](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/35415) (`prompt` / `request_prompt`). The prompt sanitizer (`_sanitize_transcription_user_text`) is shared between the two — `response_prefix` is sanitized identically so a malicious prefix cannot escape the assistant role and inject control tokens. After #35415 lands, this PR rebases to a much smaller diff.

### Related

- RFC: #35908
- Original streaming issue: #35767
- Qwen ASR initial release examples of "streaming" rely heavily on prefixing the prompt of audio as it accumulates [[ref]](https://github.com/QwenLM/Qwen3-ASR/blob/c17a131fe028b2e428b6e80a33d30bb4fa57b8df/qwen_asr/inference/qwen3_asr.py#L748).  This allows for a similar implementation to be achieved while hosting in vllm.

## Test plan

- [x] Pre-commit hooks pass (ruff, mypy, typos, etc.)
- [x] DCO sign-offs match author email on every commit
- [x] Built Docker dev image with patched files and started Qwen3-ASR-1.7B server
- [x] Verified baseline transcription still works (no `response_prefix`)
- [x] Verified `response_prefix` is accepted and changes model output
- [x] Sanitizer test added on companion PR #35415 covers the strip path used here too
- [ ] Upstream CI (`pre-run-check` is the label gate, not a code failure)

## Notes

- AI assistance (Cursor) was used; every line was reviewed and tested by the human submitter before push.

items.title: [Bugfix][KV Connector] Stop P/D transfers short of the last prompt token
items.body:
## Purpose

P/D decode recomputes the last prompt token. NIXL and Mooncake load all N prompt tokens and the scheduler then rewinds one token, but by then every group was laid out for position N. For a sliding window, prefill and decode both drop the block holding position N - W whenever N % block_size == block_size - 1, so the recomputed token N - 1 attends to the null block. With a zeroed null block this silently perturbs one window position for 1/block_size of requests; on DeepSeek-V4.1, whose null block is not zero, it corrupts the output (NaN logits at 1023/4095/8191 tokens, reported in #59197).

The local prefix cache never has this problem: it caps a hit at N - 1 before allocation. Mamba P/D already avoided it with a Mamba-only backoff. This PR makes the backoff unconditional, so P/D follows the same rule as the local cache for every model.

## Changes

- NIXL `_prefill_backoff()` and Mooncake P2P: the prefiller always stops at N - 1, and the decoder loads N - 1 tokens and computes the last one (multi-module MTP still backs off its lookahead). Both sides then lay out every group for the position decode resumes at.
- NIXL bidirectional transfer: the prefiller pulls the decoder's KV from an earlier turn only if that KV ends before its last prompt token. The workers pair blocks from the end of the sequence, so a shorter pull (a prompt shorter than the decoder's context, e.g. a regenerated turn, or one the decoder's KV fully covers now that the prefiller stops one token short) shifted every block.
- The cut never splits a multimodal item: if the prompt ends inside one, both sides back off to the item's start, the prefiller drops the item and the decoder computes it. Models parse an item from its whole placeholder (Qwen3-VL looks up each video frame's end marker), and with `disable_chunked_mm_input` and a lookahead (EAGLE) the scheduler could never schedule an item running past the cut prompt. Shared helpers `get_prefill_stop` / `truncate_prompt_for_prefill` in `kv_connector/utils.py` hold this rule for NIXL and Mooncake, and also cut mixed token-id / embeddings prompts consistently (they used to keep the embeddings and mask at full length, which the worker rejects).
- The cut stays off other prompt-indexed request features: a request with prompt logprobs (e.g. completions with echo and logprobs) transfers nothing, since it skips reading the prefix cache and the decoder never loads its KV (the prefiller returned prompt logprobs for one token fewer than the prompt and the frontend failed); the routed-experts (R3) start is clamped to the prompt length (a start equal to the original length made the scheduler assert); and the cut rebinds the prompt and kv_transfer_params, which in-process parallel samples share.
- NIXL push: a decode-side prefix hit of N - 1 tokens leaves nothing to receive; stop heartbeating the prefiller so it reclaims its blocks when the lease lapses, instead of holding them until the decode request ends.
- `get_num_new_matched_tokens` documents the contract: the count should leave the last prompt token to compute, and a connector transferring from a peer must have the peer stop at the same position, since P2P connectors pair blocks from the end of the sequence.

Behavior changes for full-attention-only models, which previously loaded all N tokens:

- Decode computes the same single token as before; prefill computes one token less and transfers one block less when N % block_size == 1.
- A request sent to the prefiller with `do_remote_decode` always generates one token, which routers already discard (as for Mamba today); P/D prompt logprobs omit the last prompt token.
- The prefiller no longer caches the block holding the last prompt token when N % block_size == 0. A resend of the same prompt is unaffected, since local hits stop at N - 1 anyway.
- Known pre-existing limitation, fixed by #59746: with different P/D block sizes and a decode-side prefix hit, NIXL pairs the transferred blocks one prefill block off whenever the decoder pads past the last token (about half of prompt lengths, on main and with this PR alike); this PR changes which lengths are affected, since decode now loads N - 1 tokens.
- Prefill and decode must run this change together: a decode with it and a prefill without it pair blocks one position apart when N % block_size == 1. NIXL's compatibility version is bumped to 14, so the handshake rejects such a pair.

## Not a duplicate

No open PR addresses the sliding-window rewind. #58556 aligns Mooncake with NIXL's multi-module MTP backoff in the same Mooncake functions; the two compose (the larger backoff wins).

## Test Plan

- `pytest tests/v1/core/ tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/ tests/v1/kv_offload`; NIXL, Mooncake, remote prefill lifecycle and bidirectional tests updated for the unconditional backoff; new `test_p_node_pulls_only_kv_ending_where_it_resumes` (fails without the bidirectional fix); `test_mamba_n1_p_side_truncation` covers a mixed-mode prompt and a prompt ending in an image (both sides stop before the image); it also covers a prompt-logprobs request and two in-process parallel samples sharing a prompt; the aux output connector test covers an R3 start past the cut prompt; the push zero-external-tokens test checks the heartbeat stops and no empty recv is staged. Checked with the real code paths that failed: Qwen3-VL's video position parsing on the cut prompt, and the scheduler with `disable_chunked_mm_input` and a lookahead shift.
- `pre-commit`, mypy
- DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash P/D (NIXL, 1P1D TP4 + TP4), two-pass GSM8K 5-shot, concurrency 512; pass 2 re-sends the prompts so decode gets local prefix hits.

## Test Result

- Unit tests (`tests/v1/core/ tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/ tests/v1/kv_offload`): 3363 passed; the remaining failures start an engine and fail in this environment (INT8 w8a8 unsupported on SM100, GPU memory held by other jobs), as on main.
- Full-attention-only model, Qwen3-30B-A3B-Instruct-2507 P/D (NIXL, 1P1D TP4 + TP4), same two-pass GSM8K. The decoder's external prefix cache hit rate drops from 100.0% to 99.9%, i.e. it now loads N - 1 tokens:

| Build | Pass 1 | Pass 2 |
|---|---|---|
| main | 0.9439 | 0.9431 |
| this PR | 0.9431 | 0.9431 |

- DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, GSM8K flexible-extract (pass 1 / pass 2), measured with an earlier revision that backed off only for sliding window / Mamba models (the DeepSeek-V4.1 behavior is the same unconditionally); "N%32==31 wrong" counts pass-2 errors on prompts with N % 32 == 31:

| Build | Pass 1 | Pass 2 | N%32==31 wrong |
|---|---|---|---|
| main | 0.9174 / 0.9249 | 0.9219 / 0.9189 | 5 / 6 |
| this PR | 0.9249 | 0.9310 | 3 |
| #59197 without this PR | 0.9181 / 0.9212 | 0.9052 / 0.9083 | 13 / 12 |
| #59197 + this PR + #59504 | 0.9242 | 0.9212 | 6 |

items.title: [Core] Add remaining copy counts to KV removal events
items.body:
## Purpose

A logical block hash may map to multiple physical KV cache blocks because vLLM v1 keeps block tables append-only and does not deduplicate cached blocks. Today, every physical eviction emits a `BlockRemoved` event containing the hash, but consumers cannot tell whether another physical copy of that hash remains. Consumers that track logical cache residency can therefore invalidate a still-cached hash after the first physical copy is removed.

This PR adds an optional `remaining_copy_counts` field to `BlockRemoved`, aligned one-to-one with `block_hashes`. The GPU block pool reports the number of physical copies remaining after each removal. It obtains that count in the same average O(1) `BlockHashToBlockMap` pop operation, while preserving the existing `pop` API and physical-event frequency. Producers that cannot provide the count, including offloading events, leave the field as `None`.

The field is included in event hashing, the subscriber example is updated, and the wire-compatibility tests cover both legacy consumers and multi-hash events. Core tests cover duplicate full-block and partial-prefix copies, including hash/group/count alignment and the final-copy transition from one remaining copy to zero.

This is not a duplicate of an existing PR. I searched open issues and PRs for `BlockRemoved`, remaining copies/counts, duplicate block hashes, and KV cache events. #47715 addresses KV cache metrics event handling, while #43258 addresses hybrid Mamba/Attention hash granularity; neither changes physical-copy removal semantics.

AI assistance from OpenAI Codex was used to adapt the implementation and tests to current upstream `main`. The submitter reviewed the complete diff and test results before submission. This change does not affect model output or accuracy, so model evaluations are not applicable.

items.title: [KV Offload] Carry request provenance and emit chunk-key removals
items.body:
## Purpose

Emit self-describing KV-offload events without retaining a full payload per offloaded chunk. For a locally initiated store or promotion, the raw event carries the original `ReqContext`; when the asynchronous store completes, the tracker uses its `Request` and KV-group geometry to build `BlockStored` (block hashes, tokens, parent hash, block size, and per-block `extra_keys`). A removal needs only its `OffloadKey`.

## Changes

- Carry the exact `ReqContext` through CPU, FS, OBJ, cascade, and promotion completion. Resolve full chunks and partial tails lazily at stored-event translation time; use context identity rather than request ID for stale completions.
- Keep promotion hit-source attribution scoped to `ReqContext` identity, so a delayed old request cannot erase a newer request using the same ID.
- Generate aligned per-block `extra_keys` for offload events in the existing KV-event format (LoRA name, multimodal identifier/offset pairs, cache salt, and prompt-embedding digests). Explicit unsalted blocks carry `[None, ...]`, distinct from absent `extra_keys`.
- Emit chunk-key `BlockRemoved`: one tail block hash per offloaded chunk, grouped by KV group, with the original medium, locality, and ownership. Remove the long-lived metadata/residency map and the lookup/store-time recording hooks.
- Keep placeholder stored payloads for external work, unsupported cache shapes, and unsafe token-mutating requests. Preserve queued removal events across cache reset.

`OffloadKey` remains `(block_hash, group_idx)`; store admission/batching and worker transfer metadata are unchanged. `BlockStored.extra_keys` keeps its existing wire format; the offload path uses the same `to_event_extra_keys` conversion as GPU events.

## Event contract

OffloadingConnector reports chunks. Each self-describing `BlockStored` describes one chunk: `block_hashes` lists its member blocks in order, and the final hash is the producer-local chunk key. Each hash in `BlockRemoved.block_hashes` is a chunk key, not an independently removed block; one removal event may batch multiple chunks. A one-block chunk is 1:1. For a two-block chunk, `BlockStored([H0, H1])` is removed as `BlockRemoved([H1])`. See #49413.

Consumers derive their own per-block routing keys from the stored tokens and aligned `extra_keys`, then retain a producer-scoped mapping from each chunk key to its member keys, accounting for KV group, medium, and ownership. On removal, they use that mapping to remove the chunk's members. vLLM does not retain this long-lived expansion map. The matching Dynamo consumer change is tracked separately in ai-dynamo/dynamo#11930.

## Validation

On GPU Server at `eeaaf50f1`:

- Offloading connector unit tests (excluding the CUDA-only worker file), CPU manager, and tiering tests: 781 passed, 1 skipped (`kvcr` is not installed).
- CUDA-only worker tests on idle GPU 1: 17 passed.
- Ruff check/format across all 19 changed Python files, mypy-3.12 across changed production files, and `git diff --check`: passed.

Model evaluation is not applicable; this changes event metadata and lifecycle, not model execution or output.

## AI assistance

AI assistance was used to trace the event lifecycle, implement the change, and draft tests. The human submitter will review every changed non-test line and the test results before marking this PR ready for review.
